My name is Jiwoo, and I’m a first-year student at
Hankook High School. Two things I truly love are
animals and travel. I used to watch nature documentaries
as a child and ⓐhave always been fascinated by
different animals around the world. So, when I saw a
poster about a volunteer camp in Kenya, I knew this
was what I wanted to do during my summer break.
Day 1
When I arrived at the airport in Nairobi, Kenya’s
capital, I got my first taste of Kenya — busy, exciting,
and warm. When I went outside, I was greeted by
the camp supervisor, Henry. Other volunteers from
different countries also arrived at similar times, and
we started making new friends right away.
We got into a large van and drove around the
crowded city. Although English is widely spoken in
Kenya, the people here also use Swahili. The first Swahili
word we learned was jambo, ⓑwhich means “hello.”
Henry took all of us to the Nairobi National
Museum, ⓒwhere I became fascinated by the diverse
cultural and natural heritage of Kenya. ⓓGoing from
hall to hall, I learned about Kenya’s many natural
resources and animals, different communities and
languages, and even important artists. One of the
most impressive displays was the statue of Ahmed,
an elephant with massive tusks. It symbolizes the
movement against illegal hunting in Kenya. Then we
headed to the Kigio Wildlife Conservancy where we
would begin our volunteer work. There, several impalas
were waiting to welcome us. The camp house was
made of stone and olive wood. After an amazing
day, ⓔI fell asleep the minute my head hit the pillow.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: different animals around the world have alwaysfascinated me
ⓓ: As I’m going from hall to hall
ⓔ: I fell asleep as soon as my head hit the pillow,
solution: ⓓ는 주절 주어를 부연 설명하는 분사구문으로, 부사절로 전환할 수 있다. 주절의 주어가 I이고 과거 시제가 사용되었으므로, 현재 진행시제를 쓴 As I’m going from hall to hall로 전환한 것은 적 절하지 않다. 접속사 As를 사용하여 부사절 As I was going from hall to hall 또는 As I went from hall to hall로 바꿀 수 있다.

Day 2
In the morning, volunteers were told what they
were going to do. I was assigned to “the giraffe
survey” group. At the conservancy, there were 26
giraffes. All of them had names and could be
(A)[recognized / confused] by the spots on their
bodies. Like the human fingerprint, the pattern of
spots on a giraffe is unique. Our group’s job was
to find the giraffes and ⓐidentify them using cameras
and binoculars. Then we had to record their locations
and activities. We often needed to take pictures of
both sides of the animal for identification. It wasn’t
(B)[easy / difficult]. This required us to go around
the giraffe to the other side before it ran away.
Later, back at the camp, we had to compare our

identification
book.

not
only
successfully
identified most of the giraffes but also discovered

Day 4
Today’s camp dinner was chapati, ⓒwhich is one

vegetables and beans, and everything was so delicious!

the stars ⓔwhile listening to the sounds of wild

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

Day 2
In the morning, volunteers were told what they
were going to do. I was assigned to “the giraffe
survey” group. At the conservancy, there were 26
giraffes. All of them had names and could be
identified by the spots on their bodies. Like the
human fingerprint, the pattern of spots on a giraffe
is unique. Our group’s job was to find the giraffes
and identify them using cameras and binoculars. Then
we had to record their locations and activities. We
often needed to take pictures of both sides of the
animal for identification. It wasn’t easy. This required
us to go around the giraffe to the other side before
it ran away. Later, back at the camp, we had to
compare our photos of the giraffes with the ones in
the identification book. We not only successfully
identified most of the giraffes but also discovered
new baby giraffes that were not in the book yet!
Day 3
My assignment for today was to search for illegal
animal traps on the conservancy. Hunters illegally
set up wire traps and wait for animals to get
caught. To stop this from happening, my group
drove out to the field with some experienced trap
spotters. There, we spread out and looked for traps.
We found a lot of wire traps on the ground. Some
traps were hidden in the bushes and others were
attached to fences. Every time we found a trap, we
were saving the life of an animal. It was one of the
most rewarding moments during my time in Kenya.

like Leonardo da Vinci, who said, “Art is never
finished,” made revisions to his paintings over and
over again.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why did Van Gogh reuse canvases?

solution: 반 고흐는 평생 단 한 점의 그림을 팔았다고만 했을 뿐 누구 에게 팔았는지는 언급되지 않았으므로, ❷ ‘반 고흐는 자신의 그림을 누구에게 팔았는가?’가 답할 수 없는 질문이다.

body:
This next piece is by the great Vincent van Gogh.
It appears to be just an ordinary painting of a
woman wearing a white cap. But thanks to
technology, another person was discovered on the
other side of the canvas. Who do you think that
person was? It was Vincent van Gogh himself that
was hidden at the back of the painting. In 2022,
the National Galleries of Scotland took an X-ray of
this painting while preparing for an exhibition.
During this process, a hidden self-portrait of Van
Gogh was discovered.
You may be aware that Van Gogh’s fame came
after his death. In fact, he sold only one painting in
his lifetime. Being a poor artist, he often reused his
canvases to save money, turning them around and
painting on the opposite side. You might also
notice that Van Gogh’s left ear looks perfectly fine
in this painting. Since he cut off part of his ear
when he was 35, we can infer that this is __________
______________________________. It is possible that other
hidden paintings of Van Gogh will be revealed to
the world with the help of technology.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a copy made by another artist
an unfinished sketch of his ear
a restored version of his early work

W: This picture is beautiful. Who painted it?
M: Believe it or not, it was an AI program.
W: That’s amazing. Do you think AI can be considered
a true artist?
M: Why not? I thought this picture was painted by
a very skilled artist.
W: AI might have good techniques, but you must
admit that it lacks creativity.
M: I see your point, but (A)I believe AI is changing
the way art is created.
W: What do you mean?
M: I think AI can inspire artists by providing new
insights. It can also help artists add fine details.
I’m excited about how AI will change the future
of art.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 흐름상 바꾸어 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: I think AI is changing the way art is created.
I doubt if AI is changing the way art is created.
I suppose AI is changing the way art is created.
In my view, AI is changing the way art is created.
I’m convinced that AI is changing the way art iscreated.
solution: ‘I believe (that) ~(나는 ~라고 믿어)’은 자신의 의견이나 생각 을 나타내는 표현이며, ‘I doubt if ~(나는 ~인지가 의심스러 워.)’는 의문이나 불확신을 나타내는 표현이므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘난 AI가 예술이 창작되는 방식을 변화시키고 있다고 믿어.’를 ❷ ’난 AI가 예술이 창작되는 방식을 바꾸고 있는지 의심스러 워.‘와 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

This next piece is by the great Vincent van Gogh.
It appears to be just an ordinary painting of a
woman wearing a white cap. But thanks to
technology, another person was discovered on the
other side of the canvas. Who do you think that
person was? It was Vincent van Gogh himself that
was hidden at the back of the painting. In 2022,
the National Galleries of Scotland took an X-ray of
this painting while preparing for an exhibition.
During this process, a hidden self-portrait of Van
Gogh was discovered.
You may be aware that Van Gogh’s fame came
after his death. In fact, he sold only one painting in
his lifetime. Being a poor artist, he often reused his
canvases to save money, turning them around and
painting on the opposite side. You might also
notice that Van Gogh’s left ear looks perfectly fine
in this painting. Since he cut off part of his ear
when he was 35, we can infer that this is one of
his early works. It is possible that other hidden
paintings of Van Gogh will be revealed to the
world with the help of technology.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the influence of poverty on Van Gogh’s artisticstyle
the artistic meaning of self-portraits in Van Gogh’sworks
how Van Gogh lost part of his ear and what itmeant to him
the relationship between Van Gogh and the NationalGalleries of Scotland
the discovery of Vincent van Gogh’s hiddenself-portrait through modern technology

Social media algorithms play a huge role in our

(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 전치사 in의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we ~ interested in)이 이어져 있고, 앞에 명사 options가 있으므로, options를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이룰 수 있는 목적격 관계대명 사 that이 적절하다. (C) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(then decides ~ will see)이 이어져 있으므로 선행사 an algorithm을 부연 설명 하는 관계사절이 되어야 한다. 따라서 계속적 용법의 관계대명 사 which가 적절하다.

Ever since I was young, I have admired great
public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move
audiences like them someday. But every time I had
a chance to speak in front of people, I would get
scared. I didn’t want to make a fool of myself. This
fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it.
That’s why I never entered the annual speech
contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just
didn’t have enough courage. Last year, however,
was my final chance before graduating from high
school. When I saw the poster on the class board,
my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school
speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in
my head, saying “Go for it!” I decided to sign up
for the contest. To make a long story short, I did
it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How
did I do? Honestly, I don’t remember much from
the contest because I was so nervous. But my act
of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do
anything that I put my mind to.

You never get a second chance to make a first
impression. It is very important to make a good
impression on others when we meet them for the
first time. But people aren’t the only ones who
ⓐmake first impressions — books do as well. A
powerful first line of a book can catch readers’
attention and make them want to read on. Authors

up with the perfect opening line for their books.
Let’s take a look at some of them.
“It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks
were striking thirteen.” - 1984, George Orwell
Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times.
But George Orwell’s well-known novel, 1984, opens
with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal
world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the
ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn’t
seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all
clocks strike thirteen here. What’s more, the number
thirteen is often ⓒassociated with bad luck in
Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the
readers that they are about to enter a world that is
dark and unfamiliar.
The story takes place in an imaginary country
called Oceania in the year 1984. The government
tries to control everyone’s life. It has even created a
new language ⓓto limit people’s thoughts and
expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania,
watches everything that goes on through television
screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the
people of Oceania will never be free. The main
character, Winston Smith, does not agree with ⓔwhich
the government is doing. He wants to fight against
Big Brother, but he can’t do it by himself. Will
Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in
and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of
the people?

Day 1
When I arrived at the airport in Nairobi, Kenya’s
capital, I got my first taste of Kenya — busy,
exciting, and warm. When I went outside, I was
greeted by the camp supervisor, Henry. Other
volunteers from different countries also arrived at
similar times, and we started making new friends
right away.
We got into a large van and drove around the
crowded city. Although English is widely spoken in
Kenya, the people here also use Swahili. The first
Swahili word we learned was jambo, which means
“hello.”
Henry took all of us to the Nairobi National
Museum, where I became fascinated by the diverse
cultural and natural heritage of Kenya. Going from
hall to hall, I learned about Kenya’s many natural
resources and animals, different communities and
languages, and even important artists. One of the
most impressive displays was the statue of Ahmed,
an elephant with massive tusks. It symbolizes the
movement against illegal hunting in Kenya. Then we
headed to the Kigio Wildlife Conservancy where we
would begin our volunteer work. There, several
impalas were waiting to welcome us. The camp
house was made of stone and olive wood. After an
amazing day, I fell asleep the minute my head hit
the pillow.

[1]
5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The bell rings. Thrilled students rush
to the school cafeteria. As soon as they get their
food, they eat it as if it’s the last 10 seconds of a
speed-eating contest. The food is gone in the blink
of an eye, but are they really satisfied?
Probably not. Speed eaters tend to eat too much
before they realize they are full. Moreover, speed
eating takes away the experience of appreciating
the pleasures of a good meal. Although it may
seem advantageous to save some time from your
busy schedule by eating quickly, slowing down your
meals actually has more benefits. Give yourself at
least 20 minutes to eat your meals. Take smaller
bites and chew your food for a longer time. Not
only will eating slower prevent you from eating too
much, but it will also help you appreciate all the
flavors of your food.
[2]
You come home from school and lie on your bed
with a bag of potato chips in one hand and your
smartphone in the other. Checking your social
media, you start eating the chips. Suddenly, you
realize your fingers are touching the bottom of an
empty bag!
You have just become a prime example of a
mindless eater. Mindless eating happens when you
are distracted and do not pay attention to how
much food you are eating. It usually ends when
you run out of food, which is too late. So, instead
of being a mindless eater, you need to become a
mindful eater. Eat only when you can focus on
eating. In other words, don’t eat while doing
another activity. That way, you can be fully aware
of the food you are putting into your mouth.

Henry took all of us to the Nairobi National Museum,

massive tusks. It symbolizes the movement against

[2]

is unique. Our group’s job was to find the giraffes
and identify ⓑthem using cameras and binoculars.
Then we had to record their locations and activities.
We often needed to take pictures of both sides of
the animal for identification. ⓒIt wasn’t easy. This
required us to go around the giraffe to the other
side before ⓓit ran away. Later, back at the camp,
we had to compare our photos of the giraffes with
the ⓔones in the identification book. We not only
successfully identified most of the giraffes but also

For some time, my grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, known as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran
through the house and destroyed our past. In only
one night, everything we knew was gone. (A) Nani
Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my
Auntie Hiraina. (B) He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once more.
(C) The village went quiet and listened to his chanting.
(D) His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy,
searching back across the centuries. (E) Sometimes,
there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then
his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant.
The village waited in worried silence until the next
name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama
almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa,
but there were still missing names he needed to fill in.
Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to
finish his work.
Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called
Murupara. “Where do we go now?” I asked Nani. He
did not reply, but he was searching inside himself,
staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner,
he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw
an old man standing in front of a house. He
welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his
eyes, I saw the message, “We must hurry.”
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember
the two old men sitting at the table and the soft
sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through
the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled
missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were
other people in the room. I felt ⓐ마치 과거의 사람들
이 그 작업이 정확한지를 확인하기 위해 두 노인의 어깨
너머로 보고 있는 것처럼. Finally, they stopped. It was
done. After a moment of silence, the old man
whispered to Nani, “Goodbye, friend.” Crying, they
pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
It was early morning and still dark when we
returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on,
and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling,
Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it
to the village. Our hearts were full because
ⓑ____________________________________________________.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired.
He sighed. “At last, I may go now.” Then, he closed
his eyes. “No, Dad!” Auntie Hiraina cried. The sun
burst across the hills.

body:
Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. This explains why no two
tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have it on their lips and chins.
The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still practiced today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: More Than a Tattoo, Tā moko
The New Way of Decorating Faces
Tā moko: A Reflection of Ancestors’ Lives

Tā

is

art
of
tattooing, which has been a culturally significant

no
two

moko
designs
look
the

Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head

mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā

on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting
these designs in their teenage years, and as they

their
tattoos
to
reflect
their
life
experiences.
Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Sound is produced through vibrations that occur
from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar
are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound
source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to
travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a
lake when you throw a stone.
(A) There are two types of interference: constructive
and destructive. Constructive interference occurs
when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting
in a bigger wave and a louder sound.
(B) When these sound waves reach our ears, the
brain interprets them as sound. Just as different
ripples in water might overlap if you throw two
stones, sound waves can also interfere with each
other when they meet.
(C) Destructive interference, on the other hand,
occurs when a peak of one wave overlaps with
a valley of another wave, so they cancel each
other out and produce a quieter sound, or no
sound at all.
solution: 소리는 예를 들어, 기타 줄이 연주될 때 같이 음원에 발생하는 진동을 통해 생성되며, 돌을 던졌을 때 호수에 발생하는 잔물 결처럼 음원의 진동으로 공기가 진동하고 소리가 파도처럼 이 동한다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 주어진 글의 마지막 문장 에 언급된 ‘파도처럼 이동하는 소리’에 해당하는 these sound waves(이 음파)가 우리 귀에 도달하면 뇌는 이를 소리로 해석 하고, 물에 두 개의 돌을 던지면 다른 물결이 서로 겹쳐질 수 있듯 음파도 만나면 서로 간섭할 수 있다는 내용의 (B), (B)의 마지막 문장에 언급된 간섭에는 두 가지 종류인 보강 간섭과 상쇄 간섭이 있으며, 보강 간섭은 두 파동의 마루가 겹쳐질 때 일어나 파동과 소리가 더 커진다는 내용의 (A), 역접의 접속부 사 on the other hand(반면에)로 연결하여, (A)의 마지막 문장 에 언급된 보강 간섭과 대조되는 개념으로서의 상쇄 간섭은 한 파동의 마루가 다른 파동의 골과 겹쳐질 때 일어나서 서로 상쇄되어 더 작은 소리가 나거나 아무 소리도 나지 않게 된다 는 내용의 (C)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 3과

body:
Have you ever wondered what ⓐis happened to
sound waves when they enter our ears? Let’s take a
closer look. The journey starts from the external
part of the outer ear, which gathers the waves and
ⓑdirect them into the ear. The collected waves
then travel through the ear canal and reach the
eardrum located in the middle ear. When the
eardrum vibrates, these vibrations are transmitted to
three small bones in the middle ear. These bones
make the vibrations ⓒstronger and then pass them
to a snail-shaped structure in the inner ear. Inside
this fluid-filled structure ⓓis tiny hair cells. When
the vibrations make waves in the fluid, the tiny hair
cells move and generate electrical signals ⓔthat
travel to the auditory nerve. This nerve carries the
information to the brain, where the signals are
interpreted,
ⓕallowing
us
to
hear
sound.
Undoubtedly, it is a quite remarkable journey!

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Visual Signals That Travel to the Brain
The Process of Hearing: From Ear to Brain
The Importance of Sound in Communication

reaches

Sound (A)[produces / is produced] through vibrations
that occur from a sound source, when the strings
of a guitar are played, for instance. The vibrations
of the sound source (B)[cause / causes] the air to
vibrate and the sound to travel as waves, similar to
the ripples created in a lake when you throw a
stone. When these sound waves reach our ears, the
brain interprets them as sound. Just as different
ripples in water might overlap if you throw two
stones, sound waves can also interfere with each
other when they meet. There are two types of
interference: constructive and destructive. Constructive
interference occurs when the peaks of two waves
overlap, (C)[resulted / resulting] in a bigger wave
and a louder sound. Destructive interference, on the
other hand, occurs when a peak of one wave
overlaps with a valley of another wave, so they
cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound,
or no sound at all.

transmitted to three small bones in the middle
ear. These bones make the vibrations stronger
and then pass them to a snail-shaped structure
in the inner ear. Inside this fluid-filled structure

journey!

canal and reach the eardrum located in the

Sound is ⓐproduced through vibrations (A)[that /
what] occur from a sound source, when the strings
of a guitar (B)[is / are] played, for instance. The
vibrations of the sound source cause the air to
vibrate and the sound (C)[travelling / to travel] as
waves, similar to the ripples created in a lake when
you ⓑthrow a stone. When these sound waves
reach our ears, the brain interprets them as sound.
Just as different ripples in water might overlap if
you throw two stones, sound waves can also
interfere with each other when they ⓒmeet. There
are two types of interference: constructive and
destructive. Constructive interference occurs when
the ⓓpeaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a
bigger wave and a louder sound. Destructive
interference, on the other hand, occurs when a
peak of one wave overlaps with a valley of another
wave, so they ⓔstrengthen each other and produce
a quieter sound, or no sound at all.

solution: (A) 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(occur from a sound source) 이 이어지므로, 앞의 vibrations를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. 참고로, what은 선행사를 포함 하는 관계대명사이다. Sound is produced through vibrations that occur
from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar
are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound
source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to
travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a
lake when you throw a stone. When these sound
waves reach our ears, the brain interprets them as
sound. Just as different ripples in water might
overlap if you throw two stones, sound waves can
also interfere with each other when they meet.
There are two types of interference: constructive
and destructive. Constructive interference occurs
when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting in
a bigger wave and a louder sound. Destructive
interference, on the other hand, occurs when a
peak of one wave overlaps with a valley of another
wave, so they cancel each other out and produce a
quieter sound, or no sound at all.

waves, and as these waves travel, they can
(A)________________ each other in either a constructive
or destructive manner, (B)________________ the volume
of sound.
(A)                 (B)

(B) 보강 간섭은 파동이 더 커지고 소리가 더 커지는 반면에, 상쇄 간섭은 더 작은 소리가 나거나 전혀 소리가 나지 않게 된다고 했으므로, 간섭의 유형에 따라 소리에 다른 영향을 주 거나 소리를 달라지게 만들 수 있다는 흐름으로 빈칸에는 ‘altering(변경하면서)’ 또는 ‘affecting(영향을 미치면서)’이 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 3과

Who best understands the text below?

Have you ever wondered what happens to sound
waves when they enter our ears? Let’s take a closer
look. The journey starts from the external part of
the outer ear, which gathers the waves and directs
them into the ear. The collected waves then travel
through the ear canal and reach the eardrum
located in the middle ear. When the eardrum
vibrates, these vibrations are transmitted to three
small bones in the middle ear. These bones make
the vibrations stronger and then pass them to a
snail-shaped structure in the inner ear. Inside this
fluid-filled structure are tiny hair cells. When the
vibrations make waves in the fluid, the tiny hair
cells move and generate electrical signals that travel
to the auditory nerve. This nerve carries the
information to the brain, where the signals are
interpreted, allowing us to hear sound. Undoubtedly,
it is a quite remarkable journey!

(→ 비눗물) 3) (1) which is (2) being used across various fields to reduce unwanted noise : (1) 쉼표 뒤에 noise-cancelling technology를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 써야 하므로, <조건>에 따라 noise-cancelling technology를 선행사로 하는 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대 명사 which를 쓰고, 단수인 선행사에 수일치 시킨 단수동 사 is를 쓴다. which → where 20) ④: 관광지의 매표소에 마이크가 설치되어 외부 소음을 감 지하고, 반대 음파를 생성하여 스피커를 통해 전송한다 고 했으므로, ‘관광지의 매표소는 마이크를 사용해 외부 소음을 감지하고 제거한다.’라고 설명한 Peter는 글의 내용을 잘 이해했다고 볼 수 있다. 또한, 노이즈 캔슬링 장치 덕분에 운전자가 산만한 소음에 방해받지 않고 운전에 집중하는 것이 가능하다고 했으므로, ‘노이즈 캔 슬링 기술로 인해 운전자들은 외부 소음에 방해받지 않고 운전에 집중할 수 있다.’라고 설명한 David 역시 글의 내용을 잘 이해했다고 볼 수 있다. 오답 Emily: 노이즈 캔슬링 기술은 음악 관련 기기에서만 유 용하다. (→ 노이즈 캔슬링 기술은 음악 기기에서만 사 용되는 것이 아니라 관광지의 매표소, 드라이브스루 패 스트푸드 식당과 커피숍 등 다양한 분야에서 유용하게 사용됨) Lisa: 노이즈 캔슬링 장치는 드라이브스루에서 고객들 간의 의사소통을 개선하는 데 도움을 준다. (→ 차량 소음을 제거함으로써 직원과 고객 사이의 의사소통을 향상시키기 위해 노이즈 캔슬링 헤드셋이 사용됨) Ben: 자동차의 오디오 시스템은 엔진과 도로 소리를 더 크게 만들어 운전자가 명확하게 들을 수 있도록 한다. (→ 노이즈 캔슬링 기술이 적용된 자동차의 오디오 시 스템은 엔진, 바람, 도로 소음과 같은 불쾌한 소음을 상 쇄하기 위해 파동을 발생시켜 운전자가 소음에 방해받 지 않고 운전에 집중할 수 있게 함)

G: Hey, look at the woman in this picture. It looks
like she’s making fun of someone.
B: I know, it does look like that, but she’s actually
just saying hi. In certain regions of Tibet, sticking
out tongues like that is a traditional way of
greeting people.
G: Really? So, it’s like waving our hands or giving a
high-five?
B: Yes, exactly! There’s an interesting history behind
why Tibetans do it.
G: Oh, yeah? What’s that?
B: Well, it’s said that there was a cold-blooded king
named Lang Darma, who had a black tongue. To
prove they weren’t related to him, Tibetans started
showing their tongues when they met someone new.
G: Oh, interesting. But isn’t sticking out tongues
considered a bit rude in some cultures, like ours?
B: That’s true, but not in Tibet. So, if you ever visit
Tibet, (A)make sure not to get offended when
someone sticks their tongue out at you!

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: be sure not to get offended
ensure that you don't get offended
be careful not to get offended
solution: 밑줄 친 (A)는 ‘기분 나빠하지 마라’의 의미로, ‘~하지 않도록 조심해라’는 의미로 주의를 당부하는 표현인 ‘make sure not+to부정사’가 쓰였다. 그러나 ❺는 '기분이 상하지 않는 것 을 피하라‘의 의미로 이중 부정이 되어 다른 의미가 된다. 따 라서 avoid getting offended로 고쳐야 유사한 의미를 갖는다.

body:
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but (A)그가 채워야 할 빠진 이름
들이 여전히 있었다. Now, he wanted me to drive
him to Murupara to finish his work.

윗글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: Nani’s Search for the Lost Village
Lost Past and Halted Journey to the Past
solution: 나니가 와카파파를 다시 쓰기 시작했고 조상들의 이름을 읊조 리며 족보의 흐름을 되살리려고 한 나니의 노력에 대한 글이 므로 글의 제목으로 ❹ ‘과거를 연결하기: 나니의 사명’이 가장 적절하다. 미래엔(김성연) 2과

body:
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather
most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to
see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I said.
“I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on
me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me to
die here in this room? Looking at these four walls?
When the whakapapa is (A)___________________?”
The old man held on tightly to the side of the
bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow,
painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could
not help but carry him to the car, and we set off
with Auntie.
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a
song that he had taught Auntie. They sang
together, lifting up their voices to send the song
flying like a bird through the sky.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,

tattoos

life
experiences.

(A)
(B)
(C)

Western countries, it’s okay to open gifts right
away, but in China, it’s considered rude. Similarly,
touching a person’s head, including that of a child,
is impolite in Thailand and Laos, whereas it may be
no big deal in other countries. So it’s important to

body:
For some time, my grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, known as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which
ran through the house and destroyed our past. In
only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani
Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter,
my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: bringing peace to the family with chanting
overcoming Nani's despair through steady journaling
the challenges of rebuilding our lives after a big fire
restoring the whakapapa as a way to reconnectwith the past
Nani's hopelessness about failing to complete thewhakapapa
solution: 하룻밤의 화재로 인해 소실되어버린 와카파파를 복원하려는 나 니의 노력에 관한 내용이므로 글의 주제로 ❹ ‘과거와 다시 연결 되기 위한 방식으로서 와카파파를 복원하기‘가 가장 적절하다.

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of the
Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. (A) Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. (B) This explains why no
two tā moko designs look the same. (C) Traditionally,
the Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. (D) The permanence of facial tattoos makes
them a lifelong commitment, often leading to regret
or unforeseen consequences. (E) Men typically wear
tā moko over their entire faces, while women have
it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting
these designs in their teenage years, and as they
grow older, more lines and shapes are added to
their
tattoos
to
reflect
their
life
experiences.
Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a
rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā
moko is less common these days, it is still practiced
today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their
traditions and heritage for the next generation.

choices: Tā moko is the traditional tattoing art of Maori.
Tā moko represents the social status of the wearer.

Only Maori men have Tā moko on their faces.
The Maori add more tattoos as they grow older.

나니는 마을 계보를 기록하느라 바쁘지 않았다(→ 바빴다). ② 나니는 그의 집을 파괴한 화재로부터 와카파파를 지켰다(→ 화재로 인해 와카파파를 잃었다). ③ 나니는 너무 절망적이어서 와카파파를 다시 쓰는 것조차 생각할 수 없었다. (→ 나니는 와카파파를 다시 쓰기 시작했다) ⑤ 마을 사람들의 걱정스러운 속삭임이 나니가 읊조리 는 것을 멈추게 했다. (→ 나니가 읊조리는 것을 멈추자 걱정스러운 침묵으로 기다렸다.) 17) ③: 타 모코 디자인이 개인의 계보, 사회적 지위와 개인적 성취를 보여주며, 나이가 들수록 삶의 경험을 나타내기 위해 더 많은 선과 모양을 문신에 더한다고 했으므로 타 모코가 과거에서 현재에 이르는 개인의 삶의 여정을 상징한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ③ ‘한 사람의 삶의 진행(과정)’가 가장 알맞다. 본문변형 an individual’s journey → the progression of one’s life 오답 ① 지도자들의 권위 ② 적들을 위협하는 한 방법 ④ 마오리족의 문화유산 ⑤ 그들이 믿는 초자연적인 힘 18) ③: (A) 문장의 동사가 없으므로, 동사가 와야 한다. Each ~ tā moko가 문장의 주어이며, of 앞의 ‘Each+단수명사 구‘에 수일치하므로 단수동사인 represents가 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. (B) 등위접속사 and에 이어지는 두 번째 절로, 부사절 as ~ older에 대한 주절이 위치해야 한다. 뒤에 문장의 동사가 없으므로 동사의 위치이며, 주어 more lines and shapes가 ‘추가되는‘ 대상이므로 복수명사구에 수일치한 수동태 are added가 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. (C) 콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(hope ~ generation)을 이끌어, 사람을 가리키는 선행사 Maori people를 부연설명하고 있으므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 who가 알맞다. 참고로 that은 계속적 용법 에서 쓸 수 없다. 19) lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky : • ‘목소리를 높이면서’는 완전한 절 뒤에 오므로 분사구문 을 만들어야 하는데, 의미상 주어인 they가 ‘목소리를 높 이는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사를 사용하 여 lifting up their voices로 영작한다. • ‘노래를 날려 보내기 위해’는 동작의 목적(~하기 위해) 을 표현하는 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 이용하여 to send 를 쓰되, ‘~을 …하도록 보내다’를 뜻하는 5형식 ‘send+목 적어+목적격보어(현재분사)’ 구문을 사용하여, to send the song flying으로 영작한다. • ‘하늘을 가로지르는 새처럼‘은 두 개의 전치사구(‘하늘을 가로지르는’과 ‘새처럼’)로 이루어져 있으므로 ‘like a bird’ 와 ‘through the sky’를 붙여서 영작한다. 20) ⑤: ⓔ ‘미래를 위해 자원을 따로 모아 두다’의 영영풀이는 save가 ‘절약하다’의 의미로 쓰일 때의 풀이로 적절하다. 지문에 쓰인 saved는 ‘구했다’의 의미이므로 ‘to rescue someone or something from danger or harm(위험이 나 피해로부터 누군가 또는 어떤 것을 구해내다)’라는 영영풀이가 되어야 한다. 오답 ⓐ 응시하다: 눈을 깜빡이거나 돌리지 않고 오랫동안 무엇인가를 바라보다 ⓑ 친절한; 친절하고 차분하며, 누구나 어떤 것도 다치 거나 속상하지 않도록 조심하는 ⓒ 기억해내다, 상기하다: 과거의 어떤 일을 기억해 내다 ⓓ 속삭이다: 아주 작은 숨소리만 사용하여 부드럽게 말해, 소수의 사람만 들을 수 있도록 하다

presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures,
making natural eye contact, and (A)[speaks / speaking]
with an appropriate volume. But just as important,
well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively
conveying your message. Here are some useful tips
for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a
“less is more” approach by keeping your slides simple.
Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases
instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to
focus more on listening than on reading. Next,
prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive
font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally
(B)[achieved / achieving] with a font size of at least
18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four
colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides
with high-quality images (C)[what / that] complement
the text. By following these simple tips, you can
create effective slides that hold your audience’s
interest and keep them engaged from start to finish!

It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward
Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for
inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble
locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came
up to me and walked me here. It’s fascinating how,
in situations like this, we want to help someone in
need. Now, this raises some interesting questions:
where does our friendliness come from, and why is
it important? To answer these questions, I’d like to
tell you about my childhood companion dog,
Sparky. When we played with a ball, I noticed that
he responded well to my gestures.

and

(C)[recycled / destroyed].

coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and
governments around the world are working hard to
improve the environmental impact of the coffee
industry through circular economy measures. A
circular economy promotes the reuse of resources
for as long as possible, reducing waste and

(A)

How much of a coffee bean is used to make

The world’s widespread love of coffee comes at a
substantial environmental cost, as the extraction
process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent

remaining 99.8 percent ⓐdisposing of as waste. As
a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed
worldwide produces millions of tons of coffee waste
each year.
So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee
extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are
classified as general waste and ⓑsent to landfills.
There they break down, releasing methane, a
greenhouse gas ⓒwhat is approximately 25 times
more potent than CO₂. Some SCGs are incinerated
instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of
CO₂: 338 kg per ton. (A)_______________, neither of
these waste management options takes into account
the potential value of coffee grounds. Although the

minerals, they are simply destroyed.

of

coffee
waste
problem,
companies,
organizations, and governments around the world
ⓔare working hard to improve the environmental
impact of the coffee industry through circular
economy measures. A circular economy promotes

Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms
right in your home using spent coffee grounds?
Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for
growing mushrooms. (A)여기 당신이 버섯 키우기를
시작하는 데 도움을 주는 단계별 안내가 있다. First,
mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent
mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk
container and make four small holes in the sides.
Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture
and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark
place with a temperature between 18 and 25˚C, and
place the container there for two to four weeks
until the mixture turns completely white. When this
happens, move the container to a bright area with
indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the
mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a
day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms
emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are
ready to be picked. After that, you can enjoy your
mushrooms with your favorite dish!

An example of a circular economy in action occurs
when a chain of coffee shops (A)[collaborate /
collaborates] with an organization to collect spent
coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are
processed to remove impurities and dried out. The
(B)[resulted / resulting] SCGs are sold to fertilizer
companies, where they are transformed into organic
fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the
coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer
to local eco-friendly farmers, (C)[who / that] then
sell their produce back to the chain. The farm
produce can be used to create various food items,
such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which
are sold in the chain’s coffee shops. By repurposing
coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses
and local farmers can benefit both economically and
environmentally.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)         (C)
solution: (A) 주어부 a chain of coffee shops에 이어진 접속사 when의 부사절 동사 자리로, 주어부의 핵심 단어인 chain이 단수이므 로, 이에 수일치된 단수동사 collaborates가 알맞다. (B) 수식을 받는 명사 SCGs(커피박)가 ‘(결과로) 생기는’ 주체이 므로 능동 관계를 나타내는 현재분사 resulting이 알맞다. (C) 쉼표 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(then sell their produce back to the chain)을 이끌어 선행사 local eco-friendly farmers에 대해 부연 설명을 하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므 로, 주격 관계대명사 who가 알맞다. that은 계속적 용법으로 사용하지 않는다.

So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee
extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are
classified as general waste and sent to landfills.
There they break down, releasing methane, a
greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times
more potent than CO₂. Some SCGs are incinerated

governments around the world are working hard to
improve the environmental impact of the coffee
industry through circular economy measures. A
circular economy promotes the reuse of resources
for as long as possible, reducing waste and
environmental costs.

each year.

B: Hey, Yumin. You seem really focused. What are
you working on?
G: Oh, hi, Brent. I’m trying to understand the poem
we learned in class. I’m really ⓐinterested in poetry.
B: Really? That’s cool. Personally, I find poems a bit
ⓑboring. I prefer novels.
G: Well, I think poems tell stories and express
emotions just like novels do, but they just do
so in a different way.
B: But sometimes they’re so ⓒclear and hard to
understand. We have to read between the lines
to figure out the message.
G: I know what you mean, but that’s what makes
poetry beautiful. There’s no right answer, and
everyone can interpret a poem ⓓdifferently.
B: Hmm, I see. You seem to really love reading
poetry. Perhaps I’ll give it a try.
G: Actually, there’s a poetry reading event at the
local bookstore on Saturday. Would you like to
come with me?
B: Sure, why not? It could be a good chance to
start ⓔappreciating poetry.
G: Absolutely! Let’s meet at the bookstore at 3 p.m.
then.

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from
my hometown, Waituhi. “Can you take a week off?”
he asked. “Your Nani Tama wants you here.” “But
Dad!” I answered. “My boss won’t let me take any
more time off.” The phone went silent, and then I
heard my grandfather say faintly, “I need your help,
Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the
whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have
much time.” I just knew _______________________________
_______________________. “All right, Nani,” I replied with
a sigh. “I’ll come.”

body:
Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
ⓐthat has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative ⓑand symbolic of an individual’s journey
from their past to their present. Each curved line
and pattern of tā moko represents a person’s
whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and personal
accomplishments. This explains why no two tā
moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have ⓒit on their lips and
chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos ⓓto reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still ⓔpracticed today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,

(A) It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather
most of the whakapapa, but there were still
missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he
wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish
his work.
(B) He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining
the past to the present once more. The village
went quiet and listened to his chanting. His
voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy,
searching back across the centuries.
(C) Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult
to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped
in the middle of the chant. The village waited
in worried silence until the next name burst out
of his mouth.

When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to
see how (A)[fit / thin] Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I
said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on
me!” Nani looked at me in (B)[anger / smile]. “You
want me to die here in this room? Looking at these
four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?”
The old man held on tightly to the side of the
bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow,
painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could
not help but carry him to the car, and we set off
with Auntie.
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he (C)[burst into
/ left out] a song that he had taught Auntie. They
sang together, lifting up their voices to send the
song flying like a bird through the sky.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 나니의 모습을 보고 그의 여행을 말리고 있으므로 나니의 건 강 상태가 매우 안 좋았음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 나니 타마가 얼 마나 thin(말랐는지)를 보고 충격 받았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. (B) 와카파파를 다 마치지도 못한 상태에서 가만히 앉아서 죽 음을 기다리는 대신 고통스럽고 힘들더라고 와카파파를 마무 리하러 가겠다는 강한 의지를 소리치며 보여주고 있으므로, 화 자가 그를 말렸을 때 분노의 감정을 느꼈다는 흐름이 자연스 럽다. 따라서 anger(화)가 난 상태로 화자에게 말했다는 표현이 오는 것이 알맞다. (C) 그가 딸에게 가르쳐준 노래였다고 하고 둘이 같이 목소리를 높여 불렀다는 내용이 이어지므로 나니가 딸에게 가르쳐줬던 노 래를 burst into(갑자기 불렀다)라는 표현이 흐름상 자연스럽다.

For some time, my grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, known as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which
ran through the house and destroyed our past. In
only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani
Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter,
my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
choices: Nani kept the whakapapa in his old house.
The whakapapa was destroyed in a fire overnight.
Nani stayed with Hiraina after his house caughtfire.
Nani was able to remember some of the namesof his ancestors.
Sometimes Nani stopped his chanting to drawattention from the village.

Just before noon, we arrived at a small town
(A)[calling / called] Murupara. “Where do we go
now?” I asked Nani. He did not reply, but he was
searching inside himself, staring at the small houses.
Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After
turning the corner, we saw an old man (B)[to stand
/ standing] in front of a house. He welcomed Nani
Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the
message, “We must hurry.”
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I
remember the two old men sitting at the table and
the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked.
All through the quiet afternoon and into the
evening, they recalled missing names. I had a
strange feeling (C)[which / that] there were other
people in the room. I felt as if people from the
past were looking over the shoulders of the two
old men to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment
of silence,
the old man whispered
to Nani,
“Goodbye, friend.” Crying, they pressed their noses
together to say goodbye.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 완전한 절(we ~ town)에 이어져 앞의 명사구 a small town 을 수식하는 분사구로, 수식을 받는 명사구 a small town가 무 루파라라고 ‘불려지는’ 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분 사 called가 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. (B) ‘…가 ~하는 것을 보다’의 의미로, ‘see+목적어+목적격보어 (동사원형/현재분사/과거분사)’의 구조로, 지각동사 saw와 목적 어 an old man 뒤에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리이다. 지각동사 의 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 때 목적격보어로 동사 원형 또는 진행을 강조하는 현재분사를, 목적어와 목적격보어 가 수동 관계일 때 과거분사를 사용하므로, 여기서는 an old man이 ‘서있는‘ 주체이자 진행을 강조하는 현재분사 standing 이 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. It was early morning and still dark when we
returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on,
and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling,
Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it
to the village. Our hearts were full because our
grandfather had saved our past for us. Our Nani
Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired. He sighed.
“At last, I may go now.” Then, he closed his eyes.
“No, Dad!” Auntie Hiraina cried. The sun burst
across the hills.

solution: 완성된 와카파파를 마을 사람들에게 건넨 뒤 눈을 감은 나니 타마의 마지막을 묘사하는 글이므로 글의 제목으로 ❶ ‘나니 타마의 마지막 선물’이 가장 적절하다. ② 우리의 과거의 마지막 숨결 ③ 잃어버린 고향으로의 귀환 ④ 우리의 과거와 끊어진 연결 ⑤ 마을 사람들과의 마지막 재회 미래엔(김성연) 2과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연) 2과 예상문제 3회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ③ 2. ① 3. ① 4. 주관식 5. ②, ④ 6. 주관식 7. 주관식 8. 주관식 9. ①, ② 10. 주관식 11. ③ 12. ④ 13. ③ 14. ⑤ 15. ③ 16. 주관식 17. ① 18. ⑤ 19. ② 20. ① 정답 및 해설 ┃3회┃ 1) ③: ⓒ they는 시들을 가리키고 메시지를 이해하기 위해 추 론해야(행간 사이를 읽어야) 하며 이해하기 힘들다고 설 명하므로 시들이 clear(명확한)하다는 표현은 어색하다. 대신 ambiguous(모호한) 또는 unclear(분명하지 않은)의 표현이 오는 것이 알맞다. *본문에는 unclear가 쓰임 오답 ⓐ 유민이는 시의 모호성이 시를 아름답게 만든다고 생 각한다고 말하고 있으며, Brent가 유민이 시 읽기를 정 말로 사랑하는 것 같다고 언급되었으므로, 유민이는 시 에 interested(관심 있는) 상태라는 표현은 알맞다. ⓑ 시보다는 소설을 더 선호한다고 했으므로 Brent에게 시가 약간 boring(지루한) 것으로 생각된다는 흐름은 자 연스럽다. ⓓ 시를 해석하는 데 있어 정답이 없다고 설명하고 있으 므로 누구든지 시를 differently(다르게) 해석할 수 있다 는 표현은 자연스럽다. ⓔ Brent가 시 읽기를 시도해보겠다고 한 말에 유민이 시 낭독회에 Brent를 초대하여 그가 가겠다고 대답하므 로 낭독회에 가서 시를 자연스럽게 접하고 좋은 시들을 만나게 될 것이므로 이는 시를 appreciating(감상하기) 시작할 좋은 기회라는 흐름은 자연스럽다. 2) ①: 유민이 수업 시간에 배운 시를 이해하려고 하고 있다고 설명하고 있으므로 ① ‘유민이 수업에서 공부한 소설을 공부하고 있다.’는 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ② 유민과 달리, Brent는 소설을 시보다 더 좋아한다. ③ 유민은 시와 소설이 공통점이 있다고 생각한다. ④ Brent는 시에서 숨겨진 메시지를 해석하는 것이 어렵 다고 느낀다. ⑤ 유민과 Brent는 토요일에 함께 시 낭독 행사에 갈 것 이다. 3) ①: 처음엔 휴가를 더 이상 내기 힘들다고 거절하던 화자가 할아버지의 간곡한 부탁으로 결국 가겠다고 대답하고 있 으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 표현은 어쩔 수 없이 가기로 결심 했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ① ‘나는 선택의 여지가 없었다’가 가장 알맞다. 오답 ② 그가 나에게 거짓말을 했다 ③ 나는 그를 위해 시간을 더 벌어야 했다 ④ 나는 그에게 내 상황을 말해야 했다 ⑤ 그것이 그가 원하는 것인지 확실히 해야 했다 4) (1) allow him to take any more time off (2) drive, complete the whakapapa 질문 (1) 화자는 아버지의 요청을 왜 거절했나? → 그의 상사가 그가 더 이상 휴가를 내는 것을 허락하지 않을 것이라 생각했기 때문이다. (2) 나니는 그의 손자에게 무엇을 하도록 요청했나? → 그는 와카파파를 완성할 수 있도록 손자가 그를 무루파 라로 운전해 줄 것을 요청했다. 5) ②, ④ : ⓑ when → which (콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 문 장을 이끌어 the fire를 부연 설명하고 있으므로, 완전한 문장과 함께 쓰이는 관계부사 when은 올 수 없으며, when을 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which로 고쳐 써 야 한다.) ⓓ for Nani Tama → Nani Tama (‘(사람)이 ~하는데 (시간) 이 걸린다’는 ‘it+take+사람+시간+to부정사’ 또는 ‘it takes+ 시간+for+사람+to부정사’로 표현하는데, 여기서 시간에 해 다하는 almost two years가 간접목적어로 뒤에 쓰였으므로 for을 삭제하고 직접목적어 Nani Tama로 고쳐야 한다. 오답 ⓐ 콤마 뒤에 ‘관계대명사+be동사‘인 which was가 생략되 어 있는 분사구로, 부연 설명하는 the village genealogy는 와카파파로 ’알려진‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거 분사 known(알려진)의 쓰임은 어법상 알맞다. ⓒ lines를 수식하고 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장을 이끌고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓔ ‘~이 있다’는 의미의 ‘there+be동사’는 동사 뒤에 주어 가 오고 be동사는 주어의 수와 일치시키므로 복수주어인 missing names와 수일치시킨 복수동사 were의 쓰임은 어 법상 적절하다. 6) everything we knew was gone. : • ‘모든 것이 사라졌다’는 everything was gone으로 영작할 수 있다. • ‘우리가 알았던’은 everything을 수식하는 형용사절이므로 관계대명사 that 뒤에 we knew를 쓰고 선행사인 everything 바로 뒤에 이어 쓰는데 총 5단어로 영작하라는 조건이 있으므로 목적격 관계대명사 that을 생략시켜 everything we knew was gone으로 영작을 완성한다. 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연) 2과 예상문제 3회 - 주관식(서답형) 4. 있으므로, 분사구문 이 오는 자리이다. 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어 인 he이며 ‘응시하는’ 주체이므로 stared를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사인 staring으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ 접속사가 남아있는 분사구문으로, 의미상 주어인 주절의 주어 we가 길모퉁이를 ‘돈‘ 주체이므로, 과거분사 turned를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사인 turning으로 고쳐야 한다. 또는 전치사 after 뒤에 이어지는 목적어로 볼 수도 있는데, 전치사 뒤에 동사가 올 수 없으므로, turned를 동명사 turning으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ 구접속사 as if[as though](마치 ~처럼)는 추측하거나 실제와는 다른 것을 가정하는 표현으로, 사실일 수 있는 추측의 경우 직설법으로 쓰지만, 가정의 경우 주절과 같은 시제이면 가정법 과거로 ‘were/과거형’을 쓰고, 주절보다 이전 시제이면 가정법 과거완료 ‘had p.p.’를 쓴다. 본문에 서는 주절 동사 felt의 과거시제와 같은 시제로, 과거에서 온 사람들이 실제로는 없지만 마치 보고 있는 것처럼 가 정하고 있으므로, 가정법 과거완료인 had been은 가정법 과거 were로 고쳐야 한다. 오답 ⓐ 완전한 절 we ~ town 뒤에서 a small town을 수식하 고 있으므로 분사구문이 오는 자리인데 행위의 주체인 a small town은 무루파라라고 불렸으므로 수동의 의미를 갖 는 과거분사 called의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓓ ‘~이 있다’라는 뜻의 there + be 동사는 동사 뒤에 쓰 인 주어의 수와 일치시키므로 복수명사인 other people과 수일치 시킨 복수동사 were의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓕ 완전한 절 they ~ together 뒤에 놓이고 주절 동작의 목적(작별 인사를 하기 위해)을 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사(~하기 위해)인 to say의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. 8) old men, missing names, done 요약문 두 노인이 빠져있던 이름들을 되찾기 위해 조용한 마을에서 재회했고 그들의 작업은 마침내 끝났다. 9) ①, ② : ⓐ 콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(has ~ years)을 이끌어 Tā moko를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사 절이므로, 계속적 용법에는 쓸 수 없는 that을 계속적 용 법의 주격 관계대명사 which로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ ‘A 뿐만 아니라 B도‘를 뜻하는 표현으로 not only A but also B가 짝지어 쓰이므로 and을 but also로 고쳐야 한다. 오답 ⓒ 타 모코를 지칭하는 목적격 대명사가 오는 자리이므로 단수 대명사인 it의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓓ 완전한 절 뒤에 오고 주절의 동작의 목적을 나타내므 로 ’~하기 위하여‘라는 의미를 갖는 부사적 용법의 to부정 사 to reflect의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓔ 주어 it은 타 모코를 지칭하고 이는 ’실행되는‘ 대상이 므로 수동태로 표현되어야 한다. 따라서 be 동사인 is 뒤 에 과거분사인 practiced의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. 10) tattooing, individual’s journey, curved lines 제시문 구부러진 선과 패턴을 가진 개인의 여정에 대한 상 징적 표현인 마오리족의 문신, 타 모코 11) ③: 과거의 잿더미에서 벗어날 방법을 찾기 위해 나니가 다 시 와카파파를 기록하기 시작했다는 주어진 글에 이어, He가 나니를 지칭하고 그가 조상들의 이름들을 읊조렸 고 그의 목소리에 마을 사람들이 귀를 기울였다는 내용 의 (B), 기억해 내기 어려운 부분에 그가 읊조림을 멈추 면 마을 사람들도 걱정스레 침묵하며 다음 이름이 나오 기를 기다렸다는 (C), 그러한 작업이 거의 2년에 이어졌 지만 여전히 빠진 이름들이 있어 그의 작업을 마무리하 려고 무루파라로 가려한다는 내용의 (A)로 이어지는 것 이 알맞다. 12) ④: (A) 나니의 모습을 보고 그의 여행을 말리고 있으므로 나니의 건강 상태가 매우 안 좋았음을 알 수 있다. 따 라서 나니 타마가 얼마나 thin(말랐는지)를 보고 충격 받았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. fit (몸이) 건강한, 탄탄한 (B) 와카파파를 다 마치지도 못한 상태에서 가만히 앉아 서 죽음을 기다리는 대신 고통스럽고 힘들더라고 와카 파파를 마무리하러 가겠다는 강한 의지를 소리치며 보 여주고 있으므로, 화자가 그를 말렸을 때 분노의 감정을 느꼈다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 anger(화)가 난 상 태로 화자에게 말했다는 표현이 오는 것이 알맞다. smile 미소 (C) 그가 딸에게 가르쳐준 노래였다고 하고 둘이 같이 목소리를 높여 불렀다는 내용이 이어지므로 나니가 딸 에게 가르쳐줬던 노래를 burst into(갑자기 불렀다)라는 표현이 흐름상 자연스럽다. leave ~ out ~을 배제하다, 생략하다, 무시하다 13) ③: 어둠 속에서 여행하면서 나니가 읊조리는 소리를 듣는 것이 낯설지만 아름다웠다고 했으므로 ③ ‘어둠 속 에 서 나니의 읊조림을 들으면서 밤새 여행하는 것은 화 자를 겁먹게 했다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ① 화자는 나니가 여행하기에 너무 약해 보였기 때문 에 그를 데려가고 싶지 않았다. ② 나니는 와카파파를 완성하지 않은 채 죽고 싶지 않 았다. ④ 나니는 그가 걸을 수 있다는 것을 증명하기 위해 최선을 다했다. ⑤ 고모는 나니에게서 그 노래를 배웠기 때문에 그와 함께 노래 부를 수 있었다. 14) ⑤: 기억해 내기 어려운 부분에서 갑자기 읊조림을 멈추었 고 마을 사람들이 걱정스러운 침묵 속에서 다음 이름 이 터져 나오기를 기다렸다고 묘사하고 있으므로 ⑤ ‘가끔 나니는 마을 사람들의 주의를 끌기 위해 그의 읊 조림을 멈췄다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ① 나니는 와카파파를 그의 옛집에 보관했다. ② 와카파파는 하룻밤 사이에 불에 타서 파괴되었다. ③ 나니는 그의 집이 불타고 난 후 히라이나와 함께 지냈다. ④ 나니는 그의 조상들의 몇몇 이름을 기억해 낼 수 있었다. 15) ③: (A) 완전한 절(we ~ town)에 이어져 앞의 Have you ever wondered what happens to sound
waves when they enter our ears? Let’s take a closer
look. The journey starts from the external part of
the outer ear, (A)[that / which] gathers the waves
and directs them into the ear. The collected waves
then travel through the ear canal and reach the
eardrum located in the middle ear. When the
eardrum vibrates, these vibrations (B)[transmit / are
transmitted] to three small bones in the middle ear.
These bones make the vibrations stronger and then
pass them to a snail-shaped structure in the inner
ear. Inside this fluid-filled structure are tiny hair
cells. When the vibrations make waves in the fluid,
the tiny hair cells move and generate electrical
signals that travel to the auditory nerve. This nerve
carries the information to the brain, where the
signals are interpreted, allowing us (C)[hear / to
hear] sound. Undoubtedly, it is a quite remarkable
journey!

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 쉼표 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌어 선행사 the external part of the outer ear에 대해 부연 설명을 하는 관계절을 이루고 있으므로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. that은 계속적 용법으로 사용하지 않는다. (B) 주어인 these vibrations(이 진동)가 전달되는 대상에 해당 하므로, ‘be동사+과거분사’ 구조의 수동태인 are transmitted가 알맞다. (C) 5형식 동사로 쓰일 때 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취해 ‘~가 …하도록 허락하다’라는 뜻의 ‘allow+목적어+목적격 보어(to부정사)’ 구문을 이루므로, 현재분사 형태로 쓰인 allowing의 목적격보어로 to부정사인 to hear가 알맞다.

소리는 음원으로부터 발생하는 진동을 통해 생성된다,
when the strings of a guitar are played, for
instance. The vibrations of the sound source cause
the air to vibrate and the sound to travel as waves,
similar to the ripples created in a lake when you
throw a stone. When these sound waves reach our
ears, the brain interprets them as sound. Just as
different ripples in water might overlap if you throw
two stones, sound waves can also interfere with
each other when they meet. There are two types of
interference:
constructive
and
destructive.
Constructive interference occurs when the peaks of
two waves overlap, resulting in a bigger wave and
a louder sound. Destructive interference, on the
other hand, occurs when a peak of one wave
overlaps with a valley of another wave, so they
cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound,
or no sound at all.

body:
Have you ever wondered what happens to sound
waves when ⓐthey enter our ears? Let’s take a
closer look. The journey starts from the external
part of the outer ear, which gathers the waves and
directs them into the ear. The collected waves then
travel through the ear canal and reach the eardrum
located in the middle ear. When the eardrum
vibrates, these vibrations are transmitted to three
small bones in the middle ear. These bones make
the vibrations stronger and then pass ⓑthem to a
snail-shaped structure in the inner ear. Inside this
fluid-filled structure are tiny hair cells. When the
vibrations make waves in the fluid, the tiny hair
cells move and generate electrical signals that travel
to the auditory nerve. This nerve carries the
information to the brain, where the signals are
interpreted, allowing us to hear sound. Undoubtedly,
it is a quite remarkable journey!

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel
Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to
Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet
three amazing artists who never gave up on their
art, despite ⓐchallenges in their lives. Each artist
has a unique painting style and story that has
made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each
artist’s life and artwork.
Bill Traylor
The first artist we’re going to examine (A)[are / is]
Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S.
in 1853 and spent his early life working on a
cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free
man after the American Civil War, he still had to
face racial discrimination, working for very ⓑlow
wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70
years
old,
Traylor
moved
to
the
city
of
Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a
factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and
became too ill to work (B)[what / that] he ⓒturned
away from drawing to express his life experiences.
Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings,
starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog.
Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had
often been used on farms to watch and hunt
slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in
these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and
Man with Umbrella portrays the ⓓfree lives of
African Americans that he observed on the streets
of Montgomery. (C)[Used / Using] simple shapes
and colors, Traylor ⓔcaptured complex moments in
American history from slavery to freedom. As a
result, he’s now considered an important figure in
American folk art.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 주어(The first ~ to examine)의 핵심이 단수명사구인 The first artist이므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 적절하다. 참고로, 명사구 The first artist를 examine의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절 ‘we’re going to examine‘이 수식하고 있으며, we’re 앞에 사람 선행사와 쓰이는 목적격 관계대명사 who(m) 또는 that이 생략되어 있다. (B) It wasn’t 뒤에 부사절 ‘until he was ~ to work’가 쓰였고, 뒤에는 완전한 절(he ~ his life experiences)이 이어지므로, ‘~ 할 때까지 …하지 않았다, ~하고 나서야 비로소 …했다’를 뜻하 는 ‘It wasn’t until ~ that …’ 형태의 강조구문을 이루는 that 이 적절하다. (C) 주절인 ’Traylor ~ freedom’ 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰인 분사 구문의 분사 자리로, 주절의 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 Traylor가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 simple shapes and colors가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재 분사 Using이 적절하다.

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may
have encountered docents and curators. While these
two roles may appear similar, they actually have
quite different responsibilities, requiring different
skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin
word meaning “to teach,” docents are guides who
lead museum tours and provide information about
the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition.
They are usually volunteers who have a passion for
art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out
their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized
training in presentation and communication skills.
On the other hand, curators are professionals who
design and organize exhibitions, with the word
curator coming from a Latin word meaning “to take
care of.” Curators determine the main theme of
each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the
theme, and arrange them in an engaging way
which captivates the audience. Curators are typically
employed by museums and are expected to possess
advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or
a related field. Despite _______________________________,
both docents and curators share a common goal:
enriching every visitor’s experience.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel
Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to
Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet
three amazing artists who never gave up on their
art, ⓐdespite challenges in their lives. Each artist
has a unique painting style and story that has
made their work (A)[highly valued / greatly devalued].
Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork.
Bill Traylor
ⓑThe first artist we’re going to examine is Bill
Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in
1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton
farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man
after the American Civil War, he still had to face
(B)[racial / religious] discrimination, working for very
low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around
70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of
Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhere he found a job in
a factory. ⓓIt wasn’t until he was 85 years old and
became too ill to work that he turned to drawing
to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to
look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean
Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong
fear of dogs because they had often been used on
farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is
expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast,
Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays
the free lives of African Americans that he observed
on the streets of Montgomery. ⓔUsing simple shapes
and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in
American history from slavery to (C)[apathy / liberty].
As a result, he’s now considered an important
figure in American folk art.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 삶의 역경에도 불구하고 자신들의 예술을 포기 하지 않았 던 세 명의 예술가들 중 첫 번째 예시로, 노예제도와 인종차별 의 경험을 바탕으로 미국 역사의 복잡한 순간을 포착함으로써 민속 예술의 중요한 인물이 된 Bill Traylor의 이야기를 다루고 있으므로, 각 예술가에게는 그들의 작품을 높이 평가받게 만들 어 준 이야기가 있다고 설명하는 흐름으로 highly valued(높이 평가받는)가 알맞다. (B) 노예로 태어나 미국 남북전쟁 이후 자유의 몸이 되었다는 내용이 앞에 언급되어 있으므로, 노예 해방 이후에도 아프리카 계 미국인으로서 여전히 인종적인 차별에 직면해야 했다는 흐 름으로 racial(인종적인)이 알맞다. (C) <비열한 개>와 <남자와 큰 개>에서는 노예를 감시하던 개에 대한 두려움을 묘사하고 있고, <핸드백을 든 여인과 우산을 든 남자>에서는 아프리카계 미국인의 자유로운 삶을 묘사하고 있다고 했으므로, 노예부터 자유에 이르기까지 미국 역사의 복 잡한 순간들을 포착했다는 흐름으로 liberty(자유)가 알맞다.

Maud Lewis
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist
known for her ⓐheart-warming paintings. Born in a
small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from
physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and
fingers. This ⓑrestricted her mobility and caused
her to drop out of school. To make a living, she
began to paint and sell Christmas cards. (A) When
her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with
her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her
future
husband,
Everett
Lewis.
(B)
She
often
depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as
Edge of Digby Harbor. (C) Her artwork used a
mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple
forms, ⓒgenerating an original, innovative style. (D)
Although her physical limitations confined her to a
small cottage, her talent and imagination were both
limitless. (E) In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear
on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen
shows decorated cows standing in a flower field.
With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a
ⓓmagical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her
paintings gradually ⓔlost popularity, her story
inspired many people and was later made into
books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love
for the world through her paintings and became an
iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

body:
Anna Ancher
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this
exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from
Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may
notice a common theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting
school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris,
(A)[which / in which] was unusual for women at the
time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she
was able to take advantage of these opportunities.
Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in
painting, (B)[objecting / objected] to the social
pressure that married women were to solely focus
on household duties. Ancher differed from other
artists of that era, who depicted women as still life
subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active
participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works
The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s
Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color,
which (C)[contributing / contributed] to the rich
Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting
Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the
sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed.
Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women
in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional
artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us
to this day.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was ~ the time) 을 이끌어 앞 절을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므 로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. (B) 완전한 절(Ancher persisted in painting)에 접속사 없이 콤 마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이 루는 분사 자리이며, 주절의 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 의 주어 Ancher가 ‘반대하는’ 행위의 주체이므로 능동을 나타 내는 현재분사 objecting이 알맞다. (C) 콤마(,) 뒤에 쓰인 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리로, 선행사인 앞 절의 내용이 과거 ‘기여한’ 주체이므 로, 과거시제 능동태 동사인 contributed가 알맞다.

The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill
Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in
1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton
farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man
after the American Civil War, he still had to face
racial discrimination, working for very low wages on
the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old,
Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama,
where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until
he was 85 years old and became too ill to work
that he turned to drawing to express his life
experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of
his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and
Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs
because they had often been used on farms to
watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is
expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast,
Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays
the free lives of African Americans that he observed
on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes
and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in
American history from slavery to freedom. As a
result, he’s now considered an important figure in
American folk art.
Bill Traylor, who was born into slavery and
(A)____________ racial discrimination throughout his
life, began painting to express his experiences and
captured complicated moments in American history
using simple shapes and colors, which made him
a(n) (B)____________ artist in American folk art.
(A)
(B)
solution: [요약문] 노예로 태어나 평생 인종차별(A)로 고통을 받았던 Bill Traylor는 자신의 경험을 표현하기 위해 그림을 그리기 시작했 고 단순한 형태와 색채를 사용하여 미국 역사의 복잡한 순간 들을 포착했으며, 이는 그를 미국 민속 미술에서 (B)중요한 예 술가로 만들었다.

body:
Anna Ancher
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this
exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from
Denmark. ⓐWhen observing her paintings, you may
notice a common theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting
school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris,
which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks
to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to
take advantage of these opportunities. Even after
getting
married,
Ancher
persisted
in
painting,
objecting to the social pressure ⓑthat married
women were to solely focus on household duties.
Ancher differed from other artists of that era,
ⓒwho depicted women as still life subjects. In
contrast, she showcased them as active participants
in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in
the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also
skillfully explored light and color, ⓓcontributing to
the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her
painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection
of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly
portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles
of women in the 20th century and displayed her
exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to
amaze us to this day.
Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope
ⓔthat
my
explanations
have
aided
you
in
appreciating these paintings. Please take some time
to further explore the exhibition.

다음 글의 Maud Lewis에 관한 내용과 일치하지않는 것은?

Maud Lewis
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known
for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small
Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical
weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers.
This limited her mobility and caused her to drop
out of school. To make a living, she began to paint
and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed
away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby,
Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband,
Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the
rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to
paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in
paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her
artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil
paints and simple forms, generating an original,
innovative style. Although her physical limitations
confined her to a small cottage, her talent and
imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red
maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape,
and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in
a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings
create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As
her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story
inspired many people and was later made into
books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love
for the world through her paintings and became an
iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
choices: Her physical weaknesses restricted her movement,which forced her to leave school.
She met Everett Lewis after moving to Digby,Nova Scotia, and spent the rest of her life withhim there.
She used bright colors and simple shapes tocreate a distinctive style, thanks to talent andimagination undiminished by her physical limits.
Her works Red Sleigh and A Pair of Oxen realisticallydepicted nature and animals as they are.
Through her paintings, she showed her love for theworld and became a symbol of Canadian folk art.

confusion about whether we are human, AI, or

AI-powered neural implants, many tricky ethical
issues should be addressed. __________________________
_____________________________________________________. Our
brains are believed to be central to our identity,
existence, and value as human beings. However, an
over-reliance on technology may delay our natural
development and create confusion about whether
we are human, AI, or something in between.
Another critical issue is privacy. There’s a risk that
organizations or hackers could access personal data
without permission through AI-connected implants.
This means that our thoughts, emotions, and
behaviors could be controlled by hackers. There’s an
additional risk that this technology could lead to
even greater social inequality, given that it may not
be available to all due to its high cost. Such
unequal access to the technology could intensify
the division between those who can afford the
implants and those who cannot.

Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to
Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet
three amazing artists who never gave up on their
art, (A)[despite / though] challenges in their lives.
Each artist has a unique painting style and story
that has made their work highly valued. Let’s
explore each artist’s life and artwork.
Bill Traylor
The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill
Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in
1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton
farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man
after the American Civil War, he still had to face
racial discrimination, (B)[working / worked] for very
low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around
70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of
Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a
factory. ⓐ그가 85세가 되고 몸이 너무 아파서 일을
할 수 없게 된 후에야 그는 자신의 인생 경험을 표현
하기 위해 그림으로 눈을 돌렸다. Now, we’re going
to look at some of his paintings, starting with
Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a
strong fear of dogs because they had often been
used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear
of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In
contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella
portrays the free lives of African Americans (C)[what
/ that] he observed on the streets of Montgomery.
Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor ⓑ__________

As a result, he’s now considered an important
figure in American folk art.

Anna Ancher
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this
exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from
Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may
notice a ⓐcommon theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting
school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris,
which was ⓑunusual for women at the time.
Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was
able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even
after getting married, Ancher ⓒpersisted in painting,
objecting to the social pressure that married women
were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher
ⓓfollowed other artists of that era, who depicted
women as still life subjects. In contrast, she
showcased them as active participants in everyday
tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen
and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully
explored light and color, contributing to the rich
Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting
Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the
sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed.

paintings continue to amaze us to this day.

focused on the interplay of light and shadow ininterior scenes
pioneered abstract techniques in Danish painting

Neuroscience has a long history of exploring
treatments for disorders of the nervous system,
including the brain and spinal cord. Traditionally,
(A)연구자들은 신경 임플란트의 다양한 기능을 연구해
왔고, 이것은 신경계에 이식될 수 있는 컴퓨터 칩과
같은 의료 기기이다. But here’s the exciting part:
with the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence
(AI), researchers have begun to integrate AI into
neural implants. In this post, we’ll examine the
incredible benefits of AI-powered neural implants,
their amazing potential for the future, and the
ethical concerns surrounding them.
First, let’s explore how this fascinating technology
has been applied. The AI-powered neural implant
has shown great promise in medical applications,
offering solutions to a range of problems. For
instance, neural implants are used to treat brain
disorders like Parkinson’s disease. These implants
electrically stimulate targeted regions of the brain at
the right time with the help of AI to restore normal
brain activity. In addition, paralyzed people can
have the ability to walk again with the help of a
“digital bridge” between two implants inserted into
their brain and spine. When they think about
moving their legs, the AI analyzes the brain signals
and sends them to their legs through the implants.
Similarly, those who have lost their arms can use
artificial arms operated by the same mechanism.

brain implants, similar to computer memory

even though you didn’t intend to buy it? Or have
you ever felt rushed into making a purchase
because of a limited-time offer? If you have, then
you ⓐmay have fallen prey to a dark pattern. Dark
patterns are manipulative designs on websites and
applications that trick users into making unintended
decisions. These deceptive practices often have
consequences that cause financial damages to the
users.
A widely used dark pattern is the practice of
“forced continuity,” which requires users to pay a
membership fee after a free trial ends. Companies
deliberately avoid informing users about the end of
the free trial period or make the cancellation

pay membership fees even if they no longer want
to use the service.

“hidden fees.” This design suddenly adds extra fees
at the last step of the ordering process. On the
final page, consumers are surprised to discover
additional charges, such as shipping or processing
fees, which the seller ⓒhas added to increase the
final cost of the order.

of.

technique
manipulates users into feeling ashamed for cancelling

Another common type of dark pattern is known as
“hidden fees.” This design suddenly adds ⓐextra
fees at the last step of the ordering process. On
the final page, consumers are surprised to discover
additional ⓑcharges, such as shipping or processing
fees, which the seller has added to increase the
final cost of the order.
“Confirm-shaming” is another online trick that
users should be ⓒaware of. (A)이 기법은 사용자가
회원권을 취소하거나 주문에 대한 환불을 요청하는 것
을 부끄럽다고 느끼도록 조종한다. Companies use

goes against the members’ intentions. For example,
when users want to cancel their ⓓsubscription, they
are offered two options: “I want to keep my
benefits” and “I want to give up my ⓔbenefits.”
The first option is presented in an appealing way,

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ extra: more than what is usual, expected, ornecessary
ⓑ charge: a responsibility or duty given to someoneto take care of or manage something
ⓒ aware: knowing or realizing that something existsor is happening
ⓓ subscription: an arrangement in which you paymoney regularly to receive a product orservice
ⓔ benefit: an advantage, improvement, or helpfuleffect that something gives you
solution: charges는 ‘요금’의 뜻으로 쓰였으나 ‘누군가에게 어떤 것을 돌 보거나 관리하도록 맡겨진 책임이나 의무’라는 charges의 또 다른 뜻인 ‘의무, 책임’에 대한 영영풀이이므로, ‘the amount of money that someone asks for goods or services (누군가 가 상품 또는 서비스에 대해 요구하는 돈의 액수)’와 같은 설 명으로 고쳐야 한다.
