다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?

Have you ever bought something online after
seeing a message such as “Hurry! One item left!”
even though you didn’t intend to buy it? Or have
you ever felt rushed into making a purchase
because of a limited-time offer? If you have, then
you may have fallen prey to a dark pattern. Dark
patterns are manipulative designs on websites and
applications that trick users into making unintended
decisions. These deceptive practices often have
consequences that cause financial damages to the
users.
A widely used dark pattern is the practice of
“forced continuity,” which requires users to pay a
membership fee after a free trial ends. Companies
deliberately avoid informing users about the end of
the free trial period or make the cancellation
process complicated. As a result, users have to pay
membership fees even if they no longer want to
use the service.
choices: Limited-time discounts and low-stock messagesare common marketing tactics to boost sales.
Requiring payment after a free trial is a strategicchoice that lets users try useful features.
Dark patterns are strategies intended to improveuser satisfaction during free trials.
Dark patterns like “forced continuity” coerce usersinto unintentional decisions.
“Forced continuity” provides users with remindersto prevent missing payments.

body:
Dark patterns, in contrast, not only manipulate
customers to act against their intentions, but they
can also lead to financial losses and personal data
leaks. To tackle this problem, extensive research
across various websites and applications is being
conducted to document the prevalence of dark
patterns and come up with solutions. In addition to
research, governments are actively discussing how
to regulate these deceptive design patterns. The
EU’s Digital Service Act, which banned dark patterns
on online platforms in 2022, is a good example of
such regulation in this area. Such regulations are
expected to increase, limiting companies’ deceptive
marketing practices in the digital market. However,
regulations
alone
may
not
be
sufficient.
As
individuals, we should take steps to combat dark
patterns and be responsible for our online shopping
behavior. This includes being cautious while making
purchases, reading terms and conditions carefully,
and recognizing that companies’ interests may not
be the same as our own. Developing an awareness
of dark patterns is also essential to avoid potential
harm and economic loss. Ultimately, (A)우리의 주의
와 노력은 우리를 조작으로부터 보호하고 이 디지털 시
대에 우리가 현명한 결정을 내릴 수 있게 할 것이다.

to compare the EU’s Digital Service Act withother international regulations
to argue that dark patterns are inevitable andthat individuals cannot avoid them
to explore dark patterns as design examples inapps and websites for academic interest
to inform readers about the problems of darkpatterns and suggest solutions to address them

B: Hi, Sumin! What are you doing on your tablet?
G: Hi, Brandon. I’m trying to find a new online fitness
class. (A)I’m not happy with the one I’m taking.
B: Whose class is it?
G: Adriana Estefan’s class.
B: Isn’t that one of the most popular online fitness
courses? What’s wrong with it?
G: Despite her reputation, I realized that her course
is a bit too challenging for me. It’s hard to
follow all the moves.
B: You should probably watch the class introduction
video and check the reviews before signing up
for a course next time. The first class is usually a
free trial, so you can watch that, too.
G: That’s a good idea. I’ll do that. I hope I can find
the right course for me.
B: Good luck!
choices: I’m displeased with the one I’m taking.
I’m not satisfied with the one I’m taking.
I’m disappointed with the one I’m taking.
I’m quite delighted with the one I’m taking.
I’m not really content with the one I’m taking.
solution: ’I’m not happy with ~‘는 어떤 것에 불만족을 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현으로, 유사한 의미를 갖는 ’I’m displeased with ~(~에 불 쾌해)‘, ’I’m not satisfied with ~(~에 만족하지 않아)‘, ’I’m disappointed with ~ (~에 실망했어)‘, ’I’m not really content with ~(~에 정말로 만족하지 않아)‘ 등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 그러나 ’I’m quite delighted with ~‘는 ’~에 꽤 기뻐‘라는 만족 의 뜻을 나타내는 표현이므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘나는 내가 듣고 있 는 것에 마음에 들지 않아.’를 ❹ ’나는 내가 듣고 있는 것에 꽤 기뻐.‘로는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.

deliberately avoid informing users about the end of

complicated. As a result, ⓒthey have to pay membership
fees even if they no longer want to use the service.

into feeling ashamed for cancelling their membership
or requesting a refund for an order. Companies use

goes against the members’ intentions. For example,

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel
Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to
Spotlights exhibit. (A)오늘, 여러분들은 삶에서의 역경
들에도 불구하고 결코 자신들의 예술을 포기하지 않았
던 세 명의 놀라운 예술가들을 만날 것입니다. Each
artist has a unique painting style and story that has
made their work highly ⓐvalue. Let’s explore each
artist’s life and artwork.
Bill Traylor
The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill
Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in
1853 and spent his early life ⓑworking on a cotton
farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man
after the American Civil War, he still had to face
racial discrimination, working for very low wages on
the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old,
Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama,
ⓒwhich he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until
he was 85 years old and became too ill to work
that he turned to drawing to express his life
experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of
his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and
Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs
because they had often been used on farms to
watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs ⓓis
expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast,
Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays
the free lives of African Americans that he observed
on the streets of Montgomery. ⓔUsing simple
shapes
and
colors,
Traylor
captured
complex
moments in American history from slavery to
freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an
important figure in American folk art.

Maud Lewis
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist
known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a
small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from
physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and
fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her
(A)[drop / to drop] out of school. To make a living,
she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When
her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with
her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her
future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the
couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis
continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby
landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby
Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and
vivid oil paints and simple forms, (B)[generated /
generating] an original, innovative style. Although
her physical limitations confined her to a small
cottage, ⓐ_________________________. In Red Sleigh, red
maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape,
and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in
a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings
create a magical quality, like (C)[that / those] of a fairy
tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity,
her story inspired many people and was later made
into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her
love for the world through her paintings and
became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill

Anna Ancher
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this
exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from
Denmark. When ⓐobserving her paintings, you may
notice a common theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen ⓑto attend a private
painting school. After that, she even studied abroad
in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time.
Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was
able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even
after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting,
objecting to the social pressure that married women
were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher
differed from other artists of that era, ⓒwhich
depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast,
she showcased them as active participants in
everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in
the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also
skillfully explored light and color, ⓓcontributing to
the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her
painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection
of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly
portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles
of women in the 20th century and displayed her
exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to
amaze us to this day.
Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope
my explanations have aided you in appreciating
these paintings. Please take some time to further
ⓔexploring the exhibition.

(B)[knowing / known] as “behavioral enrichment.” For

G: Hello, everyone! I’m Kelly. Are you thinking of
adopting a hamster? Today, I’d like to share
what I’ve learned from raising my hamster. First
of all, it’s important to understand that hamsters
are quite sensitive. While many people think that
taking care of hamsters is easy, they actually
require a lot of special attention. For example,
hamsters are active at night and sleep during
the day, so it’s crucial to provide a quiet
environment during the day. Also, their living
areas need to be cleaned regularly, and they
should be provided with fresh food and water
every day. One final tip: hamsters have poor
vision but have a strong sense of hearing. So,
try to spend some time talking to them near
their cage, and you’ll be amazed at how they
recognize your voice and respond to it. Keep
these tips in mind and take responsibility for
your hamster’s care.

solution: ⓐ special something → something special (-thing으로 끝나 는 부정대명사는 형용사가 뒤에서 수식해야 하므로 something 뒤에 형용사 special을 써서 something special로 고친다.) ⓒ filling → filled (과거동사 made와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결 되는 동사 자리이며, 주어 we가 과거 ‘채웠던’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적 어 them이 이어지므로, filling을 능동태 과거동사 filled로 고친다.) ⓔ actively → active (원급 비교 구문 ‘as ~ as …(…만큼 ~한/~하 게)’에서 as와 as 사이에는 형용사나 부사가 올 수 있으나, ‘keep+목 적어+목적격보어(~를 …한 상태로 유지하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루 는 목적격보어 자리이므로 부사 actively를 형용사 active로 고친다.)

Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely
Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight
species, all living in very different habitats around
the world. Polar bears, (A)________________, live in the
Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South America.
These bears should have the freedom to live, but
they are often killed when they come into contact
with humans. One of the worst examples of this is
bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and North
America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and Asiatic
black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept
illegally for their bile, which is sold at a high price
for traditional Asian medicine. Although bile farming
is prohibited in many countries, it continues due to
the constant demand. Governments and animal
welfare organizations make persistent attempts to
find these farms and rescue the bears, allowing
them to live in bear sanctuaries or other safe
places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that animals
are born with the right to be respected, progress
has been made in animal rights. (B)________________,
some animals are still not fully protected outside
the law, and need more of our attention and care.
(A)
(B)

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight
species, all living in very different habitats around
the world. Polar bears, for example, live in the
Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South America.
These bears should have the freedom to live, but
they are often killed when they come into contact
with humans. One of the worst examples of this is
bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and North
America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and Asiatic
black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept
illegally for their bile, which is sold at a high price
for traditional Asian medicine. Although bile farming
is prohibited in many countries, it continues due to
the constant demand. Governments and animal
welfare organizations make persistent attempts to
find these farms and rescue the bears, allowing
them to live in bear sanctuaries or other safe
places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that animals
are born with the right to be respected, progress
has been made in animal rights. However, some
animals are still not fully protected outside the law,
and need more of our attention and care.

What do governments and animal welfare organizationskeep doing for bears?

As the leader of our school club Care for Animals,
I organized a volunteer trip to an animal sanctuary
for my club members. An animal sanctuary is a
special place (A)[which / where] rescued, injured, or
abused animals can live in a safe and caring
environment. All the club members and I agreed
(B)[that / what] the sanctuary would be the perfect
place to learn about animal care. (C)[Exciting / Excited]
for a new experience, we set out to volunteer.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 앞의 명사구 a special place를 선행사로 하고 주어와 자동 사(live), 부사구로 이루어진 완전한 절(rescued ~ environment) 을 이끌고 있으므로 장소의 관계부사 where가 알맞다. (B) 동사 agreed의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(the ~ care)을 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다. 참고로, 관계대 명사·의문대명사 what은 주어, 목적어, 또는 보어가 없는 불완 전한 절을 이끌어 명사절을 이룬다. (C) Being이 생략된 분사구문에서 생략된 Being의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사 자리이며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 we가 ‘들뜨게 된’ 대상 이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사형 형용사 Excited가 알맞다.

Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely
Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight
species, all living in very different habitats around
the world. Polar bears, for example, (A)[live / living]
in the Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South
America. These bears should have the freedom to
live, but they are often killed when they come into
contact with humans. One of the worst examples of
this is bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and
North America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and
Asiatic black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept
illegally for their bile, which (B)[is / are] sold at a
high price for traditional Asian medicine. Although
bile farming is prohibited in many countries, it
continues due to the constant demand. Governments
and animal welfare organizations make persistent
attempts to find these farms and rescue the bears,
allowing them (C)[live / to live] in bear sanctuaries or
other safe places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that
animals are born with the right to be respected,
progress has been made in animal rights. However,
some animals are still not fully protected outside the
law, and need more of our attention and care.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 주절의 주어 Polar bears와 두 개의 콤마(,) 사이에 삽입된 접속부 사 for example에 이어지는 문장의 동사 자리이므로 live가 알맞다. (B) 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리에서 수동태(be동사+p.p.)를 이루는 be동사 자리로, 관계 사절이 부연 설명하고 있는 선행사 their bile이 단수명사구이 므로, 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 알맞다. 참고로, ‘쓸개즙, 담즙’ 을 뜻하는 bile은 불가산명사이므로 단수로 쓰였다. (C) 현재분사 형태로 쓰인 allowing과 목적어인 them에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리이며, ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문에 서 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 to live가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 1과

Another common type of dark pattern is known as
“hidden fees.” This design suddenly adds extra fees
at the last step of the ordering process. On the
final page, consumers are surprised to discover
additional charges, such as shipping or processing
fees, which the seller has added to (A)[decrease /
increase] the final cost of the order.
“Confirm-shaming” is another online trick that users
should be aware of. This technique manipulates users
into feeling (B)[guilty / proud] for cancelling their
membership or requesting a refund for an order.
Companies use this to keep their members subscribed,
even if it goes against the members’ intentions. For
example, when users want to cancel their subscription,
they are offered two options: “I want to keep my
benefits” and “I want to give up my benefits.” The first
option is presented in an (C)[appealing / undesirable]
way, while the second option seems like a bad choice.

solution: (A) 다크 패턴 유형 중 하나인 ‘숨겨진 비용’은 주문 과정의 마 지막 단계에서 갑자기 추가 요금을 부과하는 것이므로, 주문의 최종 금액을 ‘높이기’ 위해 배송료나 처리 비용과 같은 추가 요금을 부과한다는 흐름으로, increase(증가시키다)가 알맞다. (B) ‘수치심 유발 선택 강요’는 뒤에 이어지는 예시처럼 구독을 취소하고 싶을 때 ‘내 혜택을 포기하고 싶다’와 같이 나쁜 선 택지처럼 보이게 만들어, 사용자가 회원권 취소나 환불 요청에 대해 부정적으로 느끼도록 조종하는 것이므로 guilty(죄책감 있 는)가 알맞다. (C) 사용자가 구독을 취소하고 싶을 때 “나는 내 혜택을 유지하고 싶다”는 “나는 내 혜택을 포기하고 싶다”와 같이 나쁜 선택처럼 보이는 것과 다르게 제공되는 긍정적인 옵션이므로 appealing (매력적인)이 알맞다.

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. This explains why no two
tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have it on their lips and chins.
The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still practiced today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

Sound is produced through vibrations that occur from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a lake when you throw a stone. When these sound waves reach our ears, the brain interprets them as sound. Just as different ripples in water might overlap if you throw two stones, sound waves can also interfere with each other when they meet. There are two types of interference: constructive and destructive. Constructive interference occurs when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a bigger wave and a louder sound. Maud Lewis
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist
ⓐknown for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a
small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from
physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and
fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to
drop out of school. To make a living, she began to
paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents
passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in
Digby, Nova Scotia, ⓑwhich she met her future
husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple
spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis
continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby
landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby
Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and
vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an
original, innovative style. ⓒAlthough her physical
limitations confined her to a small cottage, her
talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red
Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter
landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows
ⓓstanding in a flower field. With these features,
Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of
a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained
popularity, her story inspired many people and
ⓔlater made into books and movies. Maud Lewis
expressed her love for the world through her
paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian
folk art.

(C) ‘A도 B도 아닌’을 뜻하는 상관접속사 ’neither A nor B’가 주 어 자리에 올 경우, 동사는 두 번째 명사(구)인 B에 수일치되므 로 단수 명사구 sticky rice에 수일치된 단수 동사 is가 알맞다.

Some people love this combination, while others
can’t seem to stand it. It can even cause quite
heated arguments. If you haven’t guessed already, it’s
the tasty or nasty — depending on your taste — ham
and pineapple pizza. The man who created this pizza
was neither Italian nor Hawaiian. A Greek immigrant
from Canada, Sam Panopoulos did not want to stick
to the usual ingredients on pizzas, like pepperoni and
mushrooms. He spread canned pineapple and sliced
ham onto a pizza and called it “the Hawaiian”
because that’s what was written on the pineapple
can. Little did he know that he had created a classic
combination. Even now, in the U.S. and U.K., no pizza
menu seems complete without it. In Italy, however,
most people find pineapple on pizza distasteful.
Why is Hawaiian pizza so divisive? The combination
is not that odd. Pineapple and ham is not the only
fruit and meat pairing in kitchens around the world.
In France, duck is paired with a sweet orange
sauce, and American Thanksgiving turkey dinner
would not be complete without cranberry sauce.
Many
people

body:
다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Some people love this combination, while others
can’t seem to stand it. It can even cause quite
heated arguments.
(A) He spread canned pineapple and sliced ham onto
a pizza and called it “the Hawaiian” because
that’s what was written on the pineapple can.
Little did he know that he had created a classic
combination. Even now, in the U.S. and U.K., no
pizza menu seems complete without it. In Italy,
however, most people find pineapple on pizza
distasteful. Why is Hawaiian pizza so divisive?
The combination is not that odd.
(B)
If you haven’t guessed already, it’s the tasty or
nasty — depending on your taste — ham and
pineapple pizza. The man who created this
pizza was neither Italian nor Hawaiian. A Greek
immigrant from Canada, Sam Panopoulos did
not want to stick to the usual ingredients on
pizzas, like pepperoni and mushrooms.
(C) Pineapple and ham is not the only fruit and
meat pairing in kitchens around the world. In
France, duck is paired with a sweet orange
sauce, and American Thanksgiving turkey dinner
would not be complete without cranberry sauce.
Many people enjoy salty and sweet flavor
combinations, whereas some others prefer to keep
those tastes as far from each other as possible.
solution: 어떤 사람들은 이 조합을 좋아하지만 다른 사람들은 싫어하며, 큰 논쟁을 일으킬 수도 있다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, this combination(이 조합)에 해당하는, it이 호불호가 갈리는 햄과 파인애플 피자이며, 이를 만든 사람은 캐나다 출신의 그리스 이민자인 샘 파노풀로스였는데, 그가 평범한 피자 재료에 얽매 이고 싶어 하지 않았다는 내용의 (B), (B)의 마지막 문장에 언 급된 샘 파노풀로스를 지칭하는 He가 통조림 파인애플과 슬라 이스 햄을 피자 위에 얹었고, 파인애플 캔에 적힌 대로 “하와 이안”이라 불렀다는 내용과, 이는 고전적인 조합이 되어서 지 금도 미국, 영국에서 대부분의 메뉴에 있지만 이탈리아에서는 피자 위의 파인애플을 불쾌하게 여기는 사람들이 많은데, 이렇 게 호불호가 갈리는 것에 의문을 제기하며 그 조합이 그렇게 이상하지 않다는 내용의 (A), (A)의 마지막 문장에 상응하는 것 으로서 이것은 유일한 과일과 고기의 조합이 아니며 프랑스에 서는 오리에 오렌지 소스를 곁들이고, 미국은 칠면조와 크랜베 리 소스를 함께 낸다는 내용과, 많은 이들이 짠맛과 단맛의 조 합을 즐기지만 일부 사람들은 그렇지 않다는 내용의 (C)로 이 어지는 것이 알맞다.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

When you think of curry, do you think of your
favorite spicy dish from a local Indian restaurant or
something milder spread over steamed white rice?
There are different types of curries all around the
world. Curry comes in many flavors, and the recipes
are different depending on where you are in the
world. For example, Japanese curry differs significantly
from Indian curry despite sharing the same origin.
The term “curry” comes from the Tamil word “kari,”
which means “sauce.” According to The Japan Times,
curry made its way to Japan from India in the
1850s and 1860s, when the country began trading
with British sailors. The Royal Navy introduced curry
to Japan in the late 19th century, and the Japanese
Navy adapted it to suit their own tastes and needs.
Not surprisingly, the Japanese curry (or kare raisu)
looks quite different from the Indian version.

an example of different variations of curry
the debate about preferences for spicy or mild curry
how curry became a popular food in various countries

W: It’s amazing how smart cats are.

humans?

with humans using different meows.

communicating with.

different languages depending on who they’re
talking to.

medium of communication with humans.
M: Do wild cats know that?
W: Probably not. I read that they rarely meow, unlike
house cats.
M: They’ve really evolved.

What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car
seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers,
which make up the majority of artificial leathers,
require a lot of energy to produce and a long time
to break down. So companies have been trying to
find more environmentally friendly options. The first
success came in the 1990s, when a company made
leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers’
relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients
have been tested, and some have been proven to
make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the
wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming
waste have been successfully turned into leather-like
sheets. As _______________________ continues to grow,
more will be invented and used. The market for
eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly.
In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and
is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.

choices: skeptical views about the use of oil-based leathers
the ever-changing nature of fashion trends
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South
Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over
20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold
sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among
the dense seaweed forests (A)[which / where] I met
an octopus.
I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of
shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap
and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of
the
octopus,
I
swam
a
little
closer,
but
it
disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of
seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring
at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary
creature! I wondered what would happen if I
(B)[kept / had kept] watching it. To see the world
from the octopus’s perspective, I left a camera near
the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped
the environment around the den. (C)[Expected /
Expecting] some drama to come, I waited.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 장소를 나타내는 선행사 the dense seaweed forests를 수 식하는 완전한 절(I met an octopus)을 이끌고 있으므로 관계 부사 where가 알맞다. (B) ‘계속 관찰하면 어떤 일이 일어날지 궁금하다‘는 의미로 미 래의 일을 나타내므로 가정법이 아니라 조건문이다. 따라서 주 절의 과거동사 wondered에 세제를 일치시켜 종속절에도 조동 사 will의 과거형인 would가 쓰였으므로, if절에도 동사 keep의 과거형 kept를 쓰는 것이 알맞다. (C) 분사구문으로, 주절의 주어인 ‘I’가 ‘기대하는’ 주체이며 목 적어로 some drama가 오므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Expecting이 알맞다.

What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car
seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers,
which make up the majority of artificial leathers,
require a lot of energy to produce and a long time
to break down. So companies _______________________.
The first success came in the 1990s, when a company
made leather from pineapple leaves. To many
customers’ relief, since then, many other eco-friendly
ingredients have been tested, and some have been
proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste
from the wine industry and a mushroom grown
from farming waste have been successfully turned
into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for
eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will
be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly
leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the
market was valued at $725 million and is expected
to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.

What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car
seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers,
(A)[that / which] make up the majority of artificial
leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a
long time to break down. So companies have been
trying to find more environmentally friendly options.
The first success came in the 1990s, when a
company made leather from pineapple leaves. ⓐ많
은 고객이 안도하게도, 그 이후로, 다른 많은 친환경
재료들이 시험을 거쳤고, 일부는 대체 가죽을 만들 수
있는 것으로 입증되었다. Grape waste from the wine
industry and a mushroom (B)[grown / was grown]
from farming waste have been successfully turned
into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for
eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will
be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly
leather alternatives (C)[are / is] growing rapidly. In
2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is
expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)

(B) 문장의 동사는 have been successfully turned이므로, 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 분사 자리이다. 따라서 수식받는 a mushroom이 ‘자라게 된’ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분 사 grown이 알맞다. Naadam Festival
Where: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia  When: July
The Naadam Festival celebrates Mongolia’s unique
culture, with events that were popular in the 13th
century. The festival features three (A)[athletic /
intellectual] competitions: wrestling, archery, and
horse racing.
In the wrestling competition, hundreds of male
players participate. In the archery competition, each
athlete is given four (B)[arrows / spears] to hit
targets 65 to 75 meters away. A horse race can be
as long as 30 kilometers. The (C)[organizers /
participants] in the horse race are children 5 to 13
years old.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 콜론(:) 다음에 레슬링, 양궁, 경마와 같은 구체적인 경기 종목이 제시되므로, 축제가 세 종류의 스포츠 경기를 특징으로 한다는 흐름으로 ‘athletic(운동 경기의[체육의])’이 알맞다. (B) 양궁 경기에서 각 선수에게 주어지는 것이므로, ‘arrows(화 살들)’가 알맞다. (C) 레슬링, 양궁 경기에 이어 각 경기의 선수들의 특징을 설 명하고 있으므로, 경마의 참가자들이 어린아이들이라는 흐름으 로 ‘participants(참가자들)’가 알맞다.

have predicted that the sweet taste of bananas
coupled with salty, nutty peanut butter would
become an American comfort food. This sandwich

you feel full, while the carbohydrates provide
sustained
energy.
The
best
thing
about
this
sandwich is that the ingredients are readily available

Some people, however, like to take things to
another level. Imagine a regular peanut butter and
banana sandwich, and then add fried bacon to it. It
has been said that the famous singer Elvis Presley
loved this sandwich, which is why it’s called, “The
Elvis.” Even though you may not want to eat the
Elvis every day, there are many fans of this
unconventional combination.

Some people love this combination, while others
can’t seem ⓐto stand it. It can even cause quite
heated arguments. If you haven’t guessed already, it’s
the tasty or nasty — depending on your taste — ham
and pineapple pizza. The man who created this pizza
was neither Italian ⓑor Hawaiian. A Greek immigrant
from Canada, Sam Panopoulos did not want to stick
to the usual ingredients on pizzas, like pepperoni and
mushrooms. He spread canned pineapple and sliced
ham onto a pizza and called it “the Hawaiian”
because that’s what was written on the pineapple
can. Little ⓒknew he that he had created a classic
combination. Even now, in the U.S. and U.K., no pizza
menu seems complete without it. In Italy, however,
most people find pineapple on pizza distasteful.
Why is Hawaiian pizza so divisive? The combination
is not that odd. Pineapple and ham is not the only
fruit and meat pairing in kitchens around the world.
In France, duck ⓓis paired with a sweet orange
sauce, and American Thanksgiving turkey dinner
would not be complete without cranberry sauce.
Many
people
enjoy
salty
and
sweet
flavor
combinations, whereas some others prefer to keep
those tastes as far from each other ⓔas possible.

body:
The main difference between Japanese curry and
Indian curry is the spice mix that is used. In Japan,
curry spices come in the form of small, pre-packaged
blocks, which are sold in grocery stores. On the
other hand, Indian cooks do not typically use
pre-mixed spices. They create their own mixtures of
turmeric, ginger, and other spices to make curry.
Since pre-packaged spices are not commonly used,
Indian curries vary in color and texture: some are
bright yellow, while others are deep red. Some are
thin and soupy, while others are thick and dense.
The curry that we eat in Korea today was
introduced by the Japanese. It became popular in
the late 1960s when (A)기성품 카레 가루가 빠르고
간단한 식사를 준비하는 것을 쉽게 만들었다. Therefore,
the curry served in Korea is similar to Japanese
curry, with the main difference being that Korean
curry is bright yellow because it contains turmeric, a
deep yellow spice.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Japanese curry and Indian curry differ mainly inthe type of spice blend used.
Japanese curry is made with pre-packagedblocks of curry spices.
Indian curries are typically uniform in color and texture.
Korean curry is quite similar to Japanese curry.
Turmeric, a deep yellow spice, gives Koreancurry its bright yellow appearance.

body:
A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling
excited and a little scared that I was traveling
without my parents. My only companions would be
my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn’t
sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but
Dan assured me that we would be the coolest
travelers in Northern California. When we finally
landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan
shouted, “Let’s get rolling!”
Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive
public transportation system. I was disappointed to
find out that the historic cable cars, which I had
been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate
wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a
city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and
I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us
aboard, and we were off.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Rolling into San Francisco with My Wheelchair
A Journey of Failure and Missed Opportunities

ⓑ cuts: thin slices of cooked meat, especially servedcold for sandwiches
ⓒ waving: moving your hand or arm back andforth to signal something
ⓓ masterpiece: a poor or unsuccessful work thatdoes not meet expectations or goals
ⓔ cool: very impressive or fashionable in a waythat people admire
solution: masterpiece는 ‘걸작’이라는 뜻이나 ‘기대나 목표에 미치지 못 하는, 형편없거나 성공적이지 않은 작품‘은 ’failure(실패작)‘의 영영풀이이므로 알맞지 않다. ’an outstanding work of art showing great skill and beauty(훌륭한 기술과 아름다움을 보 여주는 뛰어난 예술 작품)‘과 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.

kindly gave us a ride to the park. While ⓑ[headed
/ heading] east in his car, we saw the scenery
gradually changing from city to suburb, to forest,
and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at
the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to
fuel up for a hike.
While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped
frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing
through the giant sequoias. We passed some
famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, and ⓒ[it /
which] is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000
years old. It was massive, and I felt quite small in

ⓐ
ⓑ

solution: ⓐ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(lives in San Francisco)을 이끌어 주어인 Dan’s uncle Roy를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으며, 선행사가 사람이므로 주격 관계대 명사 who가 알맞다. 참고로, 계속적 용법으로 관계대명사 that은 쓸 수 없다. ⓑ 부사절 접속사 While 뒤에 주어와 동사가 있는 완전한 절 이 와야 하나 뒤에 부사로 쓰인 ease와 부사구 in his car만 이어지므로, 접속사 While 뒤에 주어(we)와 동사(were)가 생략 되고 분사만 남은 형태가 되어야 한다. 흐름상 생략된 주어 we가 ‘향하는’ 주체이고, ‘향하다’ 의미로 head는 자동사이므 로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 heading이 알맞다. ⓒ 앞의 절(We ~ Giant)에 접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로 두 번째 절의 주어 자리이며, 흐름상 앞의 단수명사구 the Grizzly Giant를 가리키므로 대명사 it이 적절하다.

glass?

pets, and she gave me some.
W: They’re really cool. Why are their shells pink?

shells like sea turtles, so I gave them some pink
shells to move into.

now and then?

that hermit crabs are really social.
W: Really? Do you mean like ants and bees?

Sometimes they even trade shells with each
other.

shouldn’t go in the water if you have an open
wound. Sharks are very sensitive to the smell of
blood.

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South
Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over
20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold
sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among
the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.
I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of
shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap
and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the (A)_____________
of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it
disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of
seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring
at me out of a little gap. What a(n) (B)______________
creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept
watching it. To see the world from the octopus’s
perspective, I left a camera near the den and
started
visiting
regularly.
I
even
mapped
the
environment around the den. Expecting some drama
to come, I waited.

An octopus’s average life is about a year, which
ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after
meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It
was bittersweet knowing her
final
days were
approaching even though she would bear young.
After mating, she didn’t come out of her den.
There would be no feeding or hunting. She was
timing her final moments for the hatching of her
eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few
months later, my son found a little octopus. We
believe her story continues on.
I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing
wildness she represented. I built a relationship with
her and witnessed her life up to the final moments.
(A)나는 이 경험이 없었다면 가질 수 없었을 관점으로
그녀를 보았다. She was smart, sensitive, and strong,
often going through rough and tough days just like
humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to
protecting the birth of her young before she died.
As a human being, (B)________________________________.
She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of
this world just as I am a part of it now, and in
that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.

I believed her sacrifice was unnecessary

Welcome to a new season of High School
Magazine. To start off the new school year on the
right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates
ⓐgiving us tips on how to succeed in the coming
year and beyond.
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024: In high school,
everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I
dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university,
though, everyone seemed ⓑvery more talented
than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt
small in comparison. I thought about giving up my
dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I
happened to see a drawing I had won an award
for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was
ⓒembarrassing because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to
oranges, and they’re right. That’s why it doesn’t
make
sense
to
compare
yourself
to
Internet
personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe
they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage,
ⓓwhat you didn’t. If you are going to compare
yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is
“yesterday-you.” Only you know where you started
and what much effort you’ve put in. I couldn’t see
the progress in my ability when I only compared
myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I’m
able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full
of
mistakes
that
I
no
longer
make.
It
is
ⓔempowered to see how I have improved rather
than
to
envy
the
success
of
others.
Your
competition isn’t the person next door or the
influencer on social media: it’s you.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Let go of past mistakes and concentrate solelyon advancing forward.
Establish your goals by acquiring inspiration fromthe strengths of others.
Focus on how much “yesterday-you” have grown,not on comparing yourself to others.
Don't become complacent about your currentsituation and instead constantly explore new paths.
Instead of being bound by your past self, envisionthe person you aspire to be in the future.

body:
Charlie
One possible benefit of a “Dislike” button is that it
would let people disagree with or be unhappy with
a post without having to say something bad about
it. This could help make conversations on social
media platforms more open, honest, and respectful.
A “Dislike” button could also help figure out what
users like or find useful. By letting people express
what they don’t like about a post, content creators
can get useful feedback and learn what their
audience likes and doesn’t like.
Jimin
The “Dislike” button can definitely be a useful tool
to measure online engagement, but there are more
negative effects than the positive. The presence of
“Dislike”
buttons
and
other
negative
replies
illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many
businesses directly ask for “5-star” ratings because
anything less may actually hurt their reputation. A
“Dislike” button encourages users to take advantage
of the system rather than provide an honest
opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can
also be harmful to both them and everyone else.

ways in which social media can foster morepositive interactions
pros and cons of the existence of the 'dislike'button on social media platforms
the impact of the 'dislike' button online on thegrowth of creators and businesses
various reasons why the 'dislike' button on socialmedia increases user engagement

body:
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I
had more troubles balancing school and personal
life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and
bored all at once and then separately. I would get
exhausted when I had to write a report for my
courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and
respond to the comments on my online journal. I
was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns,
and anxieties, and that was when I read an article
with a simple insight.
The article advised me to draw two big circles,
with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my
circle of influence, and I have direct control over
the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I
behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle
is called my circle of concern: things I worry about
but have no direct control over. For example, I
have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research I do for it. Believing that
everything was in my circle of influence left me
stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting
less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to
invest more energy into things that mattered. I no
longer worry about what my friends think, and I
focus on my own actions. I don’t get anxious over
what might be on the test, and instead I put in
every effort to understand the concepts themselves.
Now, __________________________________________________.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: I find myself trying to change situations that areinherently beyond my control
I am confident that my actions and thoughtscan make a significant difference in the world
I focus my energy on things I can control, likeeating healthy, staying in shape, and workinghard
I believe that larger transformations have a moreprofound impact on my life
I concentrate on pursuing concrete and achievablegoals rather than abstract ones
solution: 정답은 ③ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I
had more troubles balancing school and personal
life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and
bored all at once and then separately. I would get
exhausted when I had to write a report for my
courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and
respond to the comments on my online journal. I
was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns,
and anxieties, and that was when I read an article
with a simple insight.
The article advised me to draw two big circles,
with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my
circle of influence, and I have direct control over
the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I
behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle
is called my circle of concern: things I worry about
but have no direct control over. For example, I
have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research I do for it. Believing that
everything was in my circle of influence left me
stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting
less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to
invest more energy into things that mattered. I no
longer worry about what my friends think, and I
focus on my own actions. I don’t get anxious over
what might be on the test, and instead I put in
every effort to understand the concepts themselves.
Now, __________________________________________________.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024: In high school,
everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I
dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university,
though, everyone seemed much more talented than
me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in
comparison. I thought about giving up my dream
of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to
see a drawing I had won an award for from middle
school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed
because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to
oranges, and they’re right. That’s why it doesn’t
make
sense
to
compare
yourself
to
Internet
personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe
they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage,
that you didn’t. If you are going to compare
yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is
“yesterday-you.” Only you know where you started
and how much effort you’ve put in. I couldn’t see
the progress in my ability when I only compared
myself to others. Everyone _______________________. I’m
able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full
of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering
to see how I have improved rather than to envy
the success of others. Your competition isn’t the
person next door or the influencer on social media:
it’s you.
choices: faces the same challenges as you
is perfect and never makes mistakes
solution: 나현이는 자신을 다른 사람과 비교하기보다는 어제의 자신과 비 교하는 것이 중요하며, 다른 사람들과 비교할 때 자신의 발전을 제대로 볼 수 없었다. 다른 사람들의 성공을 부러워하기보다는 자신의 발전에 집중하고, 경쟁은 타인이 아니라 자신임을 인식 하는 것이 중요하다는 흐름이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❶ ‘다르게 발 전한다’가 가장 알맞다.

body:
Don’t Be Afraid to Speak Up
Elias Walter Class of 2025: Do you share your
opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay
silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I
often found myself in the second group. A little
black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I
considered speaking up. (A)조롱을 당하거나 틀리거
나 한 결과들이 늘 나의 마음에 걸렸습니다.
Then, after a particularly heated conversation in
class, I asked myself, “What am I afraid of?” I was
scared that bad things would happen, but I never
thought about good things. When I noticed others
taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same
in order to ⓐ[withdraw / participate]. Many people
are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it
anyway because they think it’s worth it. So I left
my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew
intellectually and socially by expressing myself more
ⓑ[clearly / incoherently]. I got closer to friends who
liked how open I was with them. Now I have more
people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and
learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of
expressing yourself can be extremely ⓒ[unfulfilling /
rewarding] in unexpected ways.

A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling
excited and a little scared that I was traveling
without my parents. My only companions would be
my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn’t
sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but
Dan assured me that we would be the coolest
travelers in Northern California. When we finally
(A)[departed from / landed in] San Francisco, the
Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, “Let’s get rolling!”
Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive
public transportation system. I was disappointed to
find out that the historic cable cars, which I had
been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate
wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a
city tour bus with wheelchair (B)[access / excess].
When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver
welcomed us (C)[aboard / abroad], and we were off.

solution: ⓐ ‘~가 …하는 것을 보다’라는 뜻의 5형식 구문(see+목적어+ 목적격보어)에 쓰일 때 지각동사 see는 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동이면 목적격보어로 동사원형을 취하고, 능동에 진 행의 의미가 더해지면 현재분사를 취한다. 목적어인 the scenery가 ‘변하고 있는’ 주체이며 진행 중인 상황을 나타내고 있으므로, 현재분사 changing이 알맞다. ⓑ 부사절 접속사 While 뒤에 주어와 동사가 있는 완전한 절 이 와야 하나 뒤에 명사구 a trail과 부사구 in Yosemite만 이 어지므로, 접속사 While 뒤에 주어(we)와 동사(were)가 생략되 고 분사만 남은 형태가 되어야 한다. 흐름상 생략된 주어인 we가 ‘탐험하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어인 명사구가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 exploring이 알맞다. ⓒ 앞의 명사구 the fresh air를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분 사 자리이며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘불고 있는’ 주체이므로 능동 을 나타내는 현재분사 blowing이 알맞다. ⓓ 완전한 절(We ~ Giant)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지 고 있으며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ old)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 the Grizzly Giant를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이 루므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 참 고로, 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 that은 쓸 수 없다. 비상(홍민표) 4과

choices: (A) I see it differently.   (B) I’d rather you didn’t.
(A) I feel the same way.   (B) Yes, I do.

solution: (A) 여자가 프리젠테이션(발표) 스크립트(원고)를 작성하고 있 지만, 진행에 어려움을 겪고 있어서 그 상황이 매우 짜증스럽 다고 말한 부분에 대해 남자도 원고 작업을 하고 있지만, 너무 길어진 것 같다고 말하고 있으므로, 상대방의 감정이나 상황을 이해하고 그것에 공감을 표현하거나 의견에 동의한다는 메시 지를 전달할 때 쓰는 표현이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 ‘나도 그 렇게 생각해.’라는 뜻의 ‘I feel the same way.’ ‘I understand how you feel.’이 알맞다. Use Energy on What You Can Control
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I
had more troubles ⓐbalancing school and personal
life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and
bored all at once and then separately. I would get
exhausted when I had to write a report for my
courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and
respond to the comments on my online journal. I
was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns,
and anxieties, and that was when I read an article
with a simple insight.
The article advised me (A)[to draw / draw] two big
circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle
is my circle of influence, and I have direct control
over the things ⓑinside it: what I eat and drink,
how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger
circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry
about but have no direct control over. For example,
I have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research (B)[that / what] I do for it.
ⓒBelieving that everything was in my circle of
influence left me stressed out and constantly
(C)[exhausted / exhausting]. By wasting ⓓmore
energy on my circle of concern, I was able to
invest more energy into things that mattered. I no
longer worry about what my friends think, and I
focus on my own actions. I don’t get anxious over
what might be on the test, and instead I put in
every effort to understand the concepts themselves.
Now, I only put my mental and physical energy
into my circle of ⓔinfluence: eating healthy, staying
in shape, and working hard.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) ‘~에게 …을 조언하다’라는 뜻의 ‘advise+목적어+목적격보 어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문이므로, 과거형 advised의 목적격보 어인 to부정사 to draw가 알맞다. (B) 동사 do의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(I do for it)을 이끌 어, 선행사 the amount of research를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. (C) 동사 leave는 ‘leave+목적어+목적격보어(‘~을 …상태로 남 기다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓸 때, 목적격보어로 형용사 또는 분 사가 올 수 있다. 동사 left의 목적어인 me가 ‘스트레스를 받고 지치게 된’ 대상이므로 목적격보어 stressed out과 등위접속사 and로 연결되는 과거분사형 형용사 exhausted가 알맞다.

Welcome to a new season of High School
Magazine. To start off the new school year on the
right
foot,
we
asked
some
of
our
recent
ⓐgraduates to give us tips on how to succeed in
the coming year and beyond.
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024: In high school,
everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I
dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university,
though, everyone seemed much more ⓑtalented
than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt
small in comparison. I thought about giving up my
dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I
happened to see a drawing I had won an award
for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was
embarrassed because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to
oranges, and they’re right. That’s why it doesn’t
make
sense
to
compare
yourself
to
Internet
ⓒpersonalities or even people in your real life.
Maybe
they
had
an
advantage,
or
even
a
disadvantage, that you didn’t. If you are going to
compare
yourself
to
anyone,
the
only
ⓓfair
comparison is “yesterday-you.” Only you know
where you started and how much effort you’ve put
in. I couldn’t see the progress in my ability when I
only compared myself to others. Everyone develops
differently. I’m able to see now the drawing in the
kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make.
It is ⓔempowering to see how I have improved
rather than to envy the success of others. Your
competition isn’t the person next door or the
influencer on social media: it’s you.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: a person who has completed a course ofstudy, especially from a school or university
ⓑ: having a natural ability or skill in a particulararea, such as art, music, or sports
ⓒ: the characteristic set of behaviors, attitudes,and emotions that make a person unique
ⓓ: treating all people or things equally andjustly, without favoritism or bias
ⓔ: giving someone the authority or power to dosomething; making someone feel stronger ormore confident
solution: ⓒ의 personalities는 문맥상 인물들이라는 의미로  ‘a person, especially one who is notable or has a distinctive character (특히 유명하거나 독특한 성격을 가진 사람)’으로 풀이되지만, the characteristic set of behaviors, attitudes, and emotions that make a person unique는 ‘사람을 독특하게 만드는 행동, 태도, 감정의 특성 모음’이라는 뜻을 가진 ‘개성’의 영영풀이이다.

알맞다.ⓑ 작은 원은 영향력의 원으로서 자신이 먹고 마시는것, 행동하는 방법, 그리고 방과 후 해야 하는 것 등 통제할 수 있는 것이므로 inside(안에)는 알맞다.ⓒ Abigail은 책임감과 걱정과 불안에 빠져 있었고, 자신이 통제할 수 없는 우려의 원에 있는 것들을 통제하고자했다. 자신이 모든 것을 통제할 수 있다고 생각하여 스트레스를 받고 지치게 된 5형식 구문이므로, 과거형 advised의목적격보어인 to부정사 to draw가 알맞다.(B) 동사 do의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(I do for it)을이끌어, 선행사 the amount of research를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.본문변형 원래 that은 생략되어 있었음(C) 동사 leave는 ‘leave+목적어+목적격보어(‘~을 …상태로 남기다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓸 때, 목적격보어로 형용사 또는 분사가 올 수 있다. 동사 left의 목적어인 me가‘스트레스를 받고 지치게 된’ 대상이므로 목적격보어stressed out과 등위접속사 and로 연결되는 과거분사형형용사 exhausted가 알맞다.7) ⑤: Elias는 수업 토론에서 의견을 나누지 않고 침묵을 지키며 혼자만의 생각을 간직하는 경우가 많았고, 목소리를낼 때마다 조롱이나 틀릴 것에 대한 두려움이 항상 마음을 짓눌렀지만, 다른 사람들이 위험을 감수하고 말을 하는 것을 보면서 자신도 그렇게 해야 한다는 것을 깨닫았고, 자신이 의견을 표현하면서 지적, 사회적으로 성장하게 되었다는 흐름이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ⑤ ‘나는 내 편안한 구역을 벗어나 말을 하기 시작했다’가 가장 알맞다.오답① 나는 토론에서 완전히 물러날 기회를 가졌다② 나는 말보다는 행동을 통해 자신을 표현하기로 결심했다③ 나는 경청하는 데 집중하고 침묵이 더 큰 소리를 낸다고 믿었다④ 나는 말을 할 완벽한 순간을 기다리기로 했다8) ③: ⓒ의 personalities는 문맥상 인물들이라는 의미로  ‘aperson, especially one who is notable or has adistinctive character (특히 유명하거나 독특한 성격을 가진 사람)’으로 풀이되지만, the characteristic set ofbehaviors, attitudes, and emotions that make a personunique는 ‘사람을 독특하게 만드는 행동, 태도, 감정의특성 모음’이라는 뜻을 가진 ‘개성’의 영영풀이이다.오답ⓐ 졸업생: 특히 학교나 대학에서 학업 과정을 마친 사람ⓑ 재능있는: 예술, 음악, 스포츠 등 특정 분야에서 타고난 능력이나 기술을 가진ⓓ 공정한: 모든 사람이나 사물을 편애나 편견 없이 동등하고 공정하게 대하는ⓔ 힘을 부여하는: 누군가에게 무엇을 할 권한이나 능력을 부여하는; 어떤 사람을 더 강하고 자신감을 느끼도록 만드는9) ④: 나현이는 여러분을 인터넷상의 인물이나 심지어 당신의실제 삶 속 사람들과 비교하는 것은 말이 되지 않는다고 했으며, 다른 사람과 비교하는 것에 대한 긍정적인측면은 언급하고 있지 않으므로 ④ ‘나현이 자신을 다른사람과 비교하는 것으로부터 얻었던 유익들’은 글의 내용으로 알 수 없다.오답① 나현이가 고등학교 때 삽화가가 되길 원했던 이유(→ 다른 사람들로부터 자신이 예술적으로 재능이 있다고 인정받았기 때문에)② 나현이가 대학에서 예술가가 되는 그녀의 꿈을 포기하려고 고려했던 이유 (→ 다른 사람들이 훨씬 더 재능이 있고 열심히 공부하는 모습을 보고 자신이 상대적으로 작게 느껴졌기 때문에)③ 중학교 때 상을 받았던 그림을 우연히 보았을 때 나현이의 느낌 (→ 별로 잘 그리지 않아서 부끄러워했다.)⑤ 나현이가 생각하는 공정한 비교 대상 (→ ‘어제의 당신만’이 공정한 비교 대상이라고 생각한다.)10) Improving, Comparing, Others    : 나현이는 대학에서 모든 사람들이 자신보다 훨씬 더 재능있어 보이고 너무 열심히 해서 작게 느껴졌지만, 과거에자신이 그린 그림을 보고, 자신이 얼마나 성장했는지를깨닫고, 진정한 경쟁 상대는 나 자신임을 깨달았다는 내용의 글이다. 따라서 글의 제목으로 ‘여러분 자신을 다른사람과 비교하는 것에가 아니라, 여러분 자신을 발전시키는 데 집중하세요!’가 알맞다.11) ②: ⓐ 주어와 동사의 목적어가 같은 대상일 때, 목적어로재귀대명사를 쓴다. 동사 found의 주어 I와 목적어가같으므로 me를 myself로 고쳐야 한다.ⓒ ‘겁먹은’의 뜻인 형용사 scared 뒤에서 완전한 절(bad things would happen)을 이끌고 있으므로 which를 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 한다.ⓖ more people을 선행사로 하고, 뒤로는 완전한 절(I cantalk ~ new things)이 이어지므로 불완전한 절을 이끄는관계대명사 whom은 쓸 수 없다. 선행사 more people이 관계사절의 세 동사 talk, share, learn과 어울리는전치사 with의 의미상 목적어 역할을 하므로 whom을‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태인 with whom으로 고쳐야 한다.오답ⓑ 동사 considere는 목적어로 동명사를 취하므로 과거형 considered의 목적어인 동명사구 speaking up은 알맞다.ⓓ 지각동사 notice는 ‘notice+목적어+목적격보어(~가...하는 것을 알아차리다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이며, 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동의 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 원형부정사 또는 현재분사를 쓴다. 동사 noticed의목적어 others가 ‘위험을 감수하는’ 주체로 능동 관계이므로 목적격 보어로 taking은 알맞다.ⓔ 주어 I의 과거형 동사 left와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬 구조를 이루는 과거동사 started는 알맞다.ⓕ 전치사 by의 목적어를 이루는 동명사 expressing을수식하고 있으므로 부사 clearly의 비교급 more clearly는 알맞다.12) ④: Elias는 수업 토론 중 조롱이나 틀린 말을 할 것에 대한두려움 때문에 자신의 의견을 표현하지 못했지만, 다른사람들이 위험을 감수하며 의견을 내는 모습을 보고 자신도 그와 같은 용기를 내야 한다고 결심한다. 결국Elias는 편안한 영역을 벗어나 의견을 표현하기 시작하면서, 지적, 사회적으로 성장하고, 친구들과의 관계를더욱 돈독히 만드는 유익한 경험을 얻게 된다는 내용의글이다. 따라서 글의 요지로 ④ ‘두려움에도 불구하고너의 의견을 표현하는 것은 더 큰 성장과 예상치 못한보상으로 이끈다.’가 가장 알맞다.오답① 목소리를 내기 전에 차분하게 당신의 생각을 정리하는 것이 더 중요하다.② 토론에 참여하는 가장 좋은 방법은 당신 자신의 의견을 지속적으로 의심하는 것이다.③ 말을 할 완벽한 순간을 기다리는 것이 즉흥적으로행동하는 것보다 더 가치 있다.⑤ 의사소통에서 위험을 피하는 것이 사회적 환경에서평화와 조화를 유지하는 데 도움이 된다.13) ⑤: ⓓ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(might be thrown away)을 이끌어 선행사 something을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야하므로 what을 주격 관계대명사 that으로 고쳐야 한다.ⓕ 주어 Something like that이 ‘주어지는’ 대상이므로‘give A away to B(A를 B에게 그냥 주다)’의 수동태인‘A be given away to B’ 형태가 와야 한다. 따라서 조동사 shouldn’t 뒤이므로 동사원형 be를 사용하여 give를 be given으로 고쳐야 한다.ⓖ 동명사 keeping이 뒤로 문장의 동사가 없으므로You should가 생략된 명령문 형태임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 keeping을 동사원형 keep으로 고쳐야 한다.오답ⓐ 주어 Many gifts가 ‘맞춰진’ 대상이므로, 보어 자리의 형용사 thoughtful과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬연결된 과거분사 personalized는 알맞다.ⓑ 뒤로 완전한 절(the giver isn’t caught empty-handed)이 이어져, ‘~하기 위하여, ~하도록’의 뜻의 목적의 부사절을 이루므로 구접속사 so that은 알맞다.ⓒ the actual gift를 강조하는 재귀대명사 itself는 알맞다.ⓔ 완전한 절(regifting is a good thing)을 이끌어 동사think의 목적어인 명사절을 이루므로 명사절 접속사that은 알맞다.본문변형 원래 that은 생략되어 있었음.14) (A) common gifts (B) A gift (C) regifting15) ⑤: 주어진 문장은 ‘예를 들어, 저는 교수님이 제 보고서에어떻게 반응할지에 대한 직접적인 통제권은 없지만, 그것을 위해 제가 하는 연구의 양에 대하여서는 정말로통제권은 가지고 있다.’라는 뜻으로 영향력의 원과 우려의 원에 대한 구체적인 예시이므로 영향력의 원인 더작은 원과 우려의 원인 더 큰 원에 대한 설명이 끝난뒤인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.16) ⓐ I had more troubles balancing school and personal life.ⓑ I was able to invest more energy into things thatmattered.    : ⓐ⦁ Abigail은 진로 보고서 작성, 친구들 간의 재난 중재,온라인 저널 댓글 응답 등 책임감과 불안으로 지쳐있었다는 내용이 이어지므로 빈칸에는 ‘저는 학교와 개인 생활의 균형을 맞추는 데 더 많은 어려움이 있었다.’가 들어가야 한다.⦁주어와 동사로 I had를 쓰고 ‘~하는데 어려움을 겪다’라는 표현으로 ‘have troubles+-ing’를 이용하여 hadmore troubles balancing을 쓴다. 그리고 balancing의 목적어로 school and personal life를 쓴다.     ⓑ⦁Abigail은 모든 것이 자신의 영향력 안에 있다고 믿었기 때문에 스트레스를 받았고 끊임없이 지쳤으나 우려의원에 대해 더 적은 에너지를 낭비함으로 더 이상 친구들이 무엇을 생각하는지가 아닌 자신의 행동에 집중한다는흐름이므로, 빈칸에는 ‘저는 중요한 것들에 더 많은 에너지를 투자할 수 있었다.’가 들어가야 한다.⦁ 주어 I를 쓰고, ‘~할 수 있다’의 뜻인 ‘be able to+동사원형’의 구문을 이용하여 was able to invest를 쓰고, ‘~에...을 투자하다’의 구문이 되도록 invest 뒤에 목적어 moreenergy, 전치사 into를 쓰고 into의 목적어로 things를 쓴다.⦁‘중요한 것’의 뜻이 되도록 things를 선행사로 하는 주격관계대명사 that을 이어 쓰고, ‘중요하다’의 뜻을 가진 자동사 matter를 주절의 시제에 맞춰 mattered로 변형해 영작한다. matter는 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓰지 않는다.17) ②: ⓐ Lucia는 보통의 선물이 그것을 고마워할 누군가와함께 있을 곳을 찾을 때까지 그것을 남에게 선물로 주는 것에 문제가 있다고 보지 않는다고 했으므로, 그 근거로 선물 그 자체가 아니라, 선물을 주는 것이 ‘배려하는’ 표현이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는'배려하는'의 뜻을 가진 considerate 또는 thoughtful이알맞다.*본문에는 thoughtful이 쓰였음ⓑ Richard는 선물은 주는 사람의 생각과 노력이 들어가 있고 선물은 물건 이상이라고 했으므로 주는 사람의 감정이 ‘포함된다’는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는‘포함하다’의뜻을가진contains또는encompasses가 알맞다.*본문에는 contains가 쓰였음오답① 의미없는오해하다③ 일시적인포함하다④ 사려깊은배제하다⑤ 실용적인상쇄하다18) ⑤: 고등학교 때 삽화가가 되는 것이 꿈이었던 나현은 대학교 진학 후 다른 사람들이 훨씬 더 재능있어 보이고 너무 열심히 하는 모습에 꿈을 포기하려 했으나 우연히중학교 때 상을 받은 그림이 별로 잘 그리지 못한 것에당황하면서 다른 사람과 비교하기보다는 어제의 나와비교하며 발전을 인정하는 것이 중요하다는 것을 깨닫게 되었다는 내용이다. 따라서 시사점으로 ⑤ ‘다른 사람의 자로 너 자신을 재지 마라.’가 알맞다.오답① 노력은 재능을 이긴다.② 로마는 하루 아침에 이루어지지 않았다. (큰 성취는시간이 걸리고, 인내와 노력이 필요하다.)③ 모든 구름의 뒤편은 은빛으로 빛난다. (아무리 안 좋은 상황에서도 한 가지 긍정적인 측면은 있다.)④ 성공은 목적지가 아니라 여정이다.19) ⑤: ⓔ의 them은 creators를 가리킨다.오답ⓐ 게시물ⓑ 사람들ⓒ 콘텐츠 창작자들ⓓ 많은 기업들20) ①: (A) 소셜미디어 플랫폼에서 싫어요’ 버튼의 한가지 장점은 사람들에게 게시물에 대해 반대하거나 불쾌감을 표현할 수 있는 방법을 제공하며, 콘텐츠 창작자들은 유용한 피드백을 얻을 수 있으므로 소셜미디어 플랫폼에서 사람들이 터놓고 대화를 한다는 흐름이므로 open(공개하는)이 알맞다.confidential 비밀의(B) ‘싫어요’ 버튼은 온라인 참여를 측정하는 데 유용할수 있지만, 부정적인 효과가 더 많다고 했으므로, ‘싫어요’ 버튼들의 존재와 다른 부정적인 댓글들이 소셜미디어가 얼마나 ‘비우호적’일 수 있는지 보여준다는 흐름이자연스럽다. 따라서, unfriendly(비우호적인)가 알맞다.friendly 친근한, 우호적인(C) 소셜 미디어상에서 ‘싫어요’ 버튼의 존재는 부정적인 효과가 더 많으며, ‘싫어요’ 버튼은 솔직한 의견보다는 그 시스템을 이용하도록 부추긴다는 흐름이므로, 생산자들에게 유용할 수 있지만 동시에 ‘해로울’ 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 harmful(해로운)이 알맞다. harmless 무해한

다음 대화의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

W: Oh, we’ve been sitting here in the library all
day. My body needs a break.
M: I feel the same way. I didn’t realize we’ve been
studying for so long.
W: I’m going to take a break and do some
stretches.
M: That’s a great idea! I’ll join you, but I don’t
know what to do.
W: Stand up and just follow me. Start by reaching
your arms over your head and stretching
towards the sky.
M: Ah, that feels good!
W: Now, touch your toes like this. It helps relieve
tension in your lower back.
M: Good! Sitting for a long time always makes my
lower back ache.
W: Next, let’s do some neck stretches. Slowly turn
your head to the left, and then to the right.
M: I feel much better now. Thanks!
choices: how to stretch to relieve your fatigue
things to keep in mind when doing stretches
the importance of rest for efficient healthmanagement
solution: 남자와 여자는 공부를 오랫동안 한 후 피로를 느끼고, 이를 풀 기 위해 스트레칭을 하기로 결심하고, 여자는  어떻게 스트레 칭을 할지 남자에게 설명하는 내용의 대화이다. 따라서 대화의 주제로 ❸ ‘당신의 피로를 풀기 위한 스트레칭을 하는 방법’이 가장 알맞다.

다음 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞지 않은 것은?

M: How’s it going with your presentation for
tomorrow?
W: I’ve been working on my script, but I’m stuck.
It’s incredibly annoying.
M: _______________________________. Writing scripts is a
lot of work. I’m almost finished, but I feel like
it’s too long.
W: Mind if I take a look?
M: Of course not. Here it is.
W: It looks good to me. But why don’t you add
more images to your slides?
M: Good suggestion! Thanks. Do you need any
help?
W: Would you review my script when I’m done?
M: I’d be happy to.
choices: I know exactly how you feel.
I wonder why you feel that way.
solution: 대본 작업이 막혀 짜증난다는 여자의 말에, 남자가 대본 작성 은 일이 정말 많다고 공감하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 공감을 나 타내는 표현이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 ❺ ‘나는 네가 왜 그렇 게 느끼는지 궁금해.’는 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 표현이다. 비상(홍민표) 1과

body:
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I
had more troubles balancing school and personal
life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and
bored all at once and then separately. I would get
exhausted when I had to write a report for my
courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and
respond to the comments on my online journal. I
was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns,
and anxieties, and that was when I read an article
with a simple insight.
The article advised me to draw two big circles,
with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my
circle of influence, and I have direct control over
the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I
behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle
is called my circle of concern: things I worry about
but have no direct control over. For example, I
have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research I do for it. _______________________
______________________________ left me stressed out and
constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my
circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy
into things that mattered. I no longer worry about
what my friends think, and I focus on my own
actions. I don’t get anxious over what might be on
the test, and instead I put in every effort to
understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only
put my mental and physical energy into my circle
of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and
working hard.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Prioritizing important and urgent tasks is
Having no criteria or control in doing tasks is
Distinguishing between what I can do and whatI can’t do is
Being convinced that all things fell within mysphere of control
Becoming preoccupied with the regrets andconsequences of past mistakes
solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I
had more (A)[difficulties / advantages] balancing
school and personal life. I would get excited,
anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then
separately. I would get exhausted when I had to
write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster
between friends, and respond to the comments on
my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of
responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that
was when I read an article with a simple insight.
The article advised me to draw two big circles,
with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my
circle of influence, and I have direct control over
the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I
behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle
is called my circle of concern: things I worry about
but have no direct control over. For example, I
have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research I do for it. Believing that
everything was in my circle of influence left me
stressed
out
and
constantly
exhausted.
By
(B)[preserving / wasting] less energy on my circle of
concern, I was able to invest more energy into
things that mattered. I no longer worry about what
my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I
don’t get anxious over what might be on the test,
and instead I put in every effort to understand the
concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental
and physical energy into my circle of (C)influence /
concern] eating healthy, staying in shape, and
working hard.

(C)

life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and

exhausted when I had to write a report for my
courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and

and anxieties, and that was when I read an article
with a simple insight.

with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my
circle of influence, and I have direct control over
the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I

react to my report, but I do have control over the

shape, and working hard.

floating in space. The large ones are called planets,

has shown that asteroids contain valuable resources

person
on

on

a

Off-Earth Manufacturing
Being on the International Space Station (ISS) is a
unique experience. Astronauts live and work in
microgravity, floating around instead of walking.
Researchers get to see Earth from a completely new
perspective, and they get to work on important
scientific research in conditions that are different
from Earth’s. Many manufacturers are interested in
manufacturing in space because the quality of a lot
of products manufactured on Earth is influenced by
temperature, pressure, radiation, and even the
effects of gravity.
Creating good conditions for certain types of
manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of
energy and resources, but those conditions occur
naturally in space. Drugs, beauty and food products,
and advanced materials are all potential candidates
to be tested and produced in space. For example,
without the effects of gravity, products that require
a uniform quality like cosmetics would be easier to
mix. Other materials like 3D printed skin or muscle
benefit from low pressure and gravity too. Although
the sun’s radiation can be unhealthy for our skin,
getting away from the protective effects of the
atmosphere could also benefit the testing of
products. For example, fabrics and skin creams
could be tested for their ability to protect against
solar radiation. Also, semiconductors and glass
communication cables could be produced with
higher purity and fewer faults.

In space, it is difficult to evenly mix materials forcosmetics and test the ability of the productsthat protect our skin from the sun’s radiation.
Semiconductors and glass fibers made in spacecan have higher purity and fewer defects thanthose made on Earth.

M: Mrs. Seo, I have a question about the last lesson.
W: What is it?
M: I noticed that Korean bills have a historical
figure on the front and a painting on the back.
Are the front and back related?
W: Yes. The historical figure on the front is
connected to the art on the back.
M: That’s interesting. So on the 5,000 won bill,
what does the painting on the back have to do
with the man on the front?
W: The man is Yi I, and the painting was done by
his mother.
M: She was a great artist! The plants look so real.
W: Many of my students have similar comments.
M: The house on the bill is beautiful, too. (A)I
wonder why it is drawn there.
W: It’s where he grew up. The mother and son are
honored by the bill’s design.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: Can you tell me why it is drawn there?
I'm curious about why it is drawn there.
I'd like to ask you why it is drawn there.
I have no doubt about why it is drawn there.
I'd be interested to know why it is drawn there.
solution: 밑줄 친 ‘I wonder ~’는 ‘나는 ~이 궁금해’라는 뜻의 궁금증을 나타내는 표현으로 ‘Can you tell me about ~?(내게 ~에 대해 말해 줄 수 있니?)’, ‘I’m curious about ~(나는 ~에 대해 궁금 하다)’, ‘I'd like to ask you about ~(나는 ~에 대해 묻고 싶 다)’, ‘I’d be interested to know ~(나는 ~을 알고 싶다)’ 등으 로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. 그러나 ❹ ‘I have no doubt about ~’ 은 ‘나는 ~에 대해 의심의 여지가 없다’라는 뜻으로 확신을 나 타내는 표현이므로, 밑줄 친 ‘나는 그것이 그곳에 그려진 이유 가 궁금해.’를 ❸ ‘나는 그것이 그곳에 그려진 이유에 대해 의 심의 여지가 없어.’로 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.

M: Mrs. Seo, I have a question about the last lesson.
W: What is it?
M: I noticed that Korean bills have a historical
figure on the front and a painting on the back.
Are the front and back related?
W: Yes. The historical figure on the front is
connected to the art on the back.
M: That’s interesting. So on the 5,000 won bill,
what does the painting on the back have to do
with the man on the front?
W: The man is Yi I, and the painting was done by
his mother.
M: She was a great artist! The plants look so real.
W: Many of my students have similar comments.
M: The house on the bill is beautiful, too. (A)I
wonder why it is drawn there.
W: It’s where he grew up. The mother and son are
honored by the bill’s design.

he created paintings depicting urban scenes that

the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness.
(A) The bright yellow walls create a dramatic
contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing
how people can be in the same space and feel
apart.

solution: 밑줄 친 ‘It reminds me of ~’는 ‘그것은 나에게 ~을 생각나게 한다’라는 뜻으로, 앞서 언급된 내용을 들은 뒤 떠오른 생각이 나 그와 관련된 경험에 대해 구체적인 예시를 덧붙일 때 사용 하는 표현이며, ‘It recalls ~(그것은 ~을 상기시킨다)’, ‘It brings to mind ~(그것은 ~을 마음속에 떠올리게 한다)’, ‘It makes me think of ~(그것은 나로 하여금 ~에 대해 생각하게 한다)’, ‘It serves as a reminder of ~(그것은 ~을 상기시켜 주 는 역할을 한다)’ 등으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으나, ‘그것은 나에게 ~에 대해 알려준다’라는 의미로 어떤 것에 대한 정보를 알게 되었을 때 쓰는 표현인 ❷ ‘It informs me of ~’와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

solution: (A) 부사 very는 원급을 강조할 때 쓰이므로, 비교급 형태의 부 사인 further를 수식할 수 없다. 따라서 ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 형 용사나 부사의 비교급을 강조하는 부사인 much가 알맞다. (B) mentions의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(he ordered ~ in July 1768)을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사인 that이 알맞다. 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 뒤에 주어나 목적어, 보어 가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어져야 한다. (C) that절의 동사로 had가 있으므로 ‘a summer dish ~ royal court’는 주어(naengmyeon)와 동사(had) 사이에 이중콤마로 삽 입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 동격의 명사구 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 a summer dish를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 형 태가 되어야 하며, a summer dish(여름철 요리)는 ‘즐겨지는’ 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 enjoyed가 알맞다.

solution: 글쓴이의 새로운 인생의 목표는 한국을 여행하는 것이라고 했 으므로, ❸ ‘글쓴이의 새로운 인생의 목표는 그녀가 가장 좋아 하는 프로그램들을 더 즐길 수 있도록 한국어를 배우는 것이 다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 비상(홍민표) 2과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 공통영어2 비상(홍민표) 2과 예상문제 1회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ② 2. ⑤ 3. ④ 4. ② 5. ② 6. ⑤ 7. ⑤ 8. ④ 9. 주관식 10. ③ 11. ② 12. ④ 13. 주관식 14. ③ 15. 주관식 16. ⑤ 17. ⑤ 18. 주관식 19. ③ 20. ③ 정답 및 해설 ┃1회┃ 1) ②: 밑줄 친 ‘It reminds me of ~’는 ‘그것은 나에게 ~을 생 각나게 한다’라는 뜻으로, 앞서 언급된 내용을 들은 뒤 떠오른 생각이나 그와 관련된 경험에 대해 구체적인 예 시를 덧붙일 때 사용하는 표현이며, ‘It recalls ~(그것은 ~을 상기시킨다)’, ‘It brings to mind ~(그것은 ~을 마음 속에 떠올리게 한다)’, ‘It makes me think of ~(그것은 나로 하여금 ~에 대해 생각하게 한다)’, ‘It serves as a reminder of ~(그것은 ~을 상기시켜 주는 역할을 한다)’ 등으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으나, ‘그것은 나에게 ~에 대해 알려준다’라는 의미로 어떤 것에 대한 정보를 알게 되었 을 때 쓰는 표현인 ② ‘It informs me of ~’와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다. 오답 ① 그것은 ~을 상기시켜 ③ 그것은 ~을 마음속에 떠올리게 해 ④ 그것은 나로 하여금 ~에 대해 생각하게 해 ⑤ 그것은 ~을 상기시켜 주는 역할을 해 2) ⑤: 타지마할이 지어지는 데 걸린 기간에 대한 언급은 없으 므로, ⑤ ‘타지마할을 짓는 데 얼마나 걸렸는가?’에는 답 할 수 없다. 오답 ① 정조는 왜 수원 화성을 지었는가? (→ 자신의 아버지 에게 경의를 표하기 위해) ② 정조는 언제 자신의 아버지를 잃었는가? (→ 열한 살 때) ③ 타지마할은 어디에 있는가? (→ 인도에) ④ 황제 샤자한의 아내는 죽었을 때 무엇을 하던 중이었 는가? (→ 아이를 출산 중이었음) 3) ④: wanted → wanting (부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+명사 (구)+분사(구)’ 구문에 해당하며 전치사 with에 이어지는 명사구 more people(더 많은 사람들)이 ‘원하는’ 주체이 므로 과거분사 wanted를 능동의 의미인 현재분사 wanting으로 고친다.) 4) ②: K-드라마와 케이팝의 전 세계적 인기가 한국어 학습에 대한 관심의 증가뿐만 아니라 한국 문화의 다른 측면에 도 영향을 미치면서, 한국 문화를 경험하고자 하는 사람 들이 많이 늘어나고 있음을 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 주 제로 ② ‘한국 문화의 세계적 확산과 그 영향’이 알맞다. 오답 ① 한국 대중문화 수출의 경제적 이익 ③ 한국 드라마가 전 세계에서 인기 있는 이유 ④ 미국과 영국의 교육 제도의 차이점 ⑤ 한국어를 공부하는 데 있어 학생들이 직면하는 어려움 5) ②: 프랑스 출신의 피에르 뒤부아(Pierre Dubois)가 중학교 때 부터 케이팝 팬이었다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 중학 교 시절을 That으로 받아 그가 친구로부터 케이팝을 처 음 소개받은 것이 바로 그때로, 뮤직비디오를 몇 편 본 기억이 난다는 (B), 그가 (뮤직비디오의) 안무에 놀란 이 후 매료되었으며, 온라인과 TV에서 팔로우하는 제일 좋 아하는 그룹들이 있다는 (A), (A)에 대한 추가적인 내용 으로서 부사 even(심지어)과 함께, 그가 친구들과 춤 동 작을 연습하고 연습 영상을 소셜 미디어에 올리기도 한 다는 내용과, 케이팝 팬덤의 일원이 된 것이 그에게 책 과 학업으로부터의 휴식을 준다는 (C)의 흐름이 자연스 럽다. 6) ⑤: few(많지 않은) → most(대부분의), many(많은) *원래 지문에는 most가 쓰였음 7) ⑤: what → that (is의 보어 자리에서 완전한 절(I now realize that ~ there)을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속 사인 that으로 고친다. 참고로, what은 선행사를 포함하 는 관계대명사 또는 간접의문문을 이루는 의문사로 쓰 이며, 뒤에 주어나 목적어, 보어가 없는 불완전한 절이 온다.) 8) ④: 글쓴이는 한국어를 배우는 과정이 느리지만, 제일 좋아하 는 아티스트가 자신에게 응답할 때 환상적이라고 느낀다 고 했으므로, 자신이 좋아하는 케이팝 아티스트들과 한 국어로 소통하고자 하는 욕구가 한국어 공부에 대한 동 기부여가 된다는 흐름이 되는 ④ ‘가장 좋아하는 아티스 트들과 그들의 언어로 소통하다’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 한국 소설과 에세이를 유창하게 읽다 ② 케이팝 팬인 친구들을 만나러 해외를 여행하다 ③ 한국에서의 케이팝 콘서트에 매년 참석하다 ⑤ 제일 좋아하는 아티스트의 노래들을 이해하지 않고 외우다 9) Being part of this K-pop fandom gives me a much-needed break from books and schoolwork too. : ⦁be의 동명사인 Being이 문장을 시작하도록 한다. ⦁‘~에게 …을 주다’라는 뜻의 4형식 구문인 ‘give+간접목 적어+직접목적어’를 활용한다. ⦁동명사(구)가 주어 자리에 올 경우 단수 취급하므로, 술 어동사 자리에 give를 단수형인 gives로 변형하여 쓴다. 10) ③: 피에르 뒤부아(Pierre Dubois)가 케이팝 뮤직비디오를 보 고 안무에 바로 놀랐으며, 그날 이후로 매료되었다고 공통영어2 비상(홍민표) 2과 예상문제 1회 - 주관식(서답형) 9. Being part of this K-pop fandom gives me a much-needed break from books and schoolwork too. 13. ⓐ a Korean drama ⓑ my parents ⓒ a Korean neighbor 15. the familiar cultural themes made it easy for me to engage with the story 18. (1) ⓐ that → which (2) ⓔ deliver → be delivered 했으므로, ③ ‘처음에, 피에르 뒤부아는 케이팝 영상의 안무를 별로 좋아하지 않았지만, 나중에는 즐기게 되었 다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 피에르 뒤부아는 중학교 때부터 케이팝에 빠져 있었다. ② 피에르 뒤부아는 자신의 친구를 통해 처음으로 케이 팝에 대해 알게 되었다. ④ 피에르 뒤부아는 자신이 제일 좋아하는 케이팝 그룹 을 온라인과 TV에서 팔로우한다. ⑤ 피에르 뒤부아와 그의 친구들은 케이팝 춤을 연습하 고 자신들의 연습 영상을 소셜 미디어에 공유한다. 11) ②: 주어진 문장은 ‘더 중요한 것은, 그것은 새로운 인생의 목표를 주었는데, 그것은 한국을 여행하는 것이다.’라는 뜻이며 부사구 ‘More importantly(더 중요한 것은)’를 포함하는 추가적인 설명에 해당하므로, 앞선 언급으로 서 it에 해당하는 ‘K-드라마에 매혹된 것’을 통해 글쓴 이가 더 범세계적이 되었고 다른 문화의 진가를 인정 하게 되었다는 내용 뒤이자, 주어진 문장의 한국 여행 에 대한 부연 설명으로서, 글쓴이가 제일 좋아하는 프 로그램의 촬영지를 탐험하고, 현지 음식을 먹으며, 진정 한 한국 경험을 즐기고 싶다는 내용 앞인 (B)에 들어가 야 한다. 본문변형 ~ super excited, but I won’t … → ~ super excited. But I won’t … 12) ④: (A) 글쓴이가 가사의 의미를 이해하지 못한다면 노래를 완전히 이해할 수 없는 것 같은 기분이 든다고 했으므 로, 케이팝에 관심이 자연스럽게 한국어 공부에 대한 관심을 유발했다는 흐름이 되는 triggered(유발했다)가 알맞다. discourage 의욕을 꺾다 (B) 글쓴이가 공부를 그리 좋아하지 않는다는 내용 다 음에, 역접의 접속사 but(그러나)으로 연결된 대조적인 내용이 이어져야 하므로, 한국어를 배우는 것은 다르다 는 흐름이 되는 different(다른)가 알맞다. the same 같은 (C) 글쓴이가 제일 좋아하는 아티스트가 자신에게 응답 할 때 환상적인 기분이 든다는 내용이 역접의 접속사 but(그러나)에 연결되어 뒤에 이어지므로, 한국어를 배 우는 것이 느린 과정이라는 대조적인 흐름이 되는 slow(느린)가 알맞다. fast 빠른 13) ⓐ a Korean drama ⓑ my parents ⓒ a Korean neighbor : ⓐ it은 앞 절에 언급된 a Korean drama(한국 드라마)를 가리킨다. ⓑ they는 앞서 언급된 my parents(나의 부모님)를 가리 킨다. ⓒ her는 앞서 언급된 a Korean neighbor(한국인 이웃)를 가리킨다. 14) ③: (A) Anna Valera가 TV를 너무 많이 보고 있었다는 내용 다음에, 이에 대한 결과로서 부모님이 그녀가 볼 수 있 는 것과 볼 수 없는 것에 제한을 두셨다는 내용이 이어 지므로, 빈칸에는 ‘~이기 때문에’라는 뜻의 Since가 알 맞다. (B) K-드라마에서 본 다양한 한국 음식을 먹어보고 싶 었다는 내용 다음에, 글쓴이의 동네에 한국 식료품점이 있어서 재료를 구매하여 집에서 한국 요리를 해볼 수 있었다는 긍정적인 결과가 이어지므로, 빈칸에는 ‘다행 히’라는 뜻의 Luckily가 알맞다. 오답 (A)        (B) ① 비록 ~이지만 다행히 ② 만약 ~이 아니면 불행히도 ④ 비록 ~이지만 대신에 ⑤ ~이기 때문에 불행히도 15) the familiar cultural themes made it easy for me to engage with the story : ⦁‘~가 …하도록 만들다’라는 뜻의 5형식인 ‘make+목적어 +목적격보어(형용사)’ 구문을 활용하되, <조건>에 따라 가목적어 it을 사용하여 ‘make+it+목적격보어+진목적어 (to부정사구)’ 형태로 영작한다. ⦁<조건>에 따라 to부정사의 의미상 주어를 to 앞에 ‘for+목적격’ 형태로 쓴다. ⦁‘~에 몰입하다’라는 뜻의 ‘engage with ~’를 활용한다. 16) ⑤: (A) 부사 very는 원급을 강조할 때 쓰이므로, 비교급 형 태의 부사인 further를 수식할 수 없다. 따라서 ‘훨씬’이 라는 의미로 형용사나 부사의 비교급을 강조하는 부사 인 much가 알맞다. (B) mentions의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(he ordered ~ in July 1768)을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사인 that이 알맞다. 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 뒤 에 주어나 목적어, 보어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어져 야 한다. (C) that절의 동사로 had가 있으므로 ‘a summer dish ~ royal court’는 주어(naengmyeon)와 동사(had) 사이 에 이중콤마로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 동격의 명사구 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 a summer dish를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 형태가 되어야 하며, a summer dish(여름철 요리)는 ‘즐겨지는’ 대상이므로, 수 동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 enjoyed가 알맞다. 17) ⑤: 한국의 음식 배달의 역사에 대해 설명하며, 냉면에 대 한 배달 서비스가 기록되어 있는 학자 황윤석의 저서 와 이유원의 저서가 언급되고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ⑤ ‘한국에서의 초기 음식 배달 서비스에 대한 기록들’ 이 알맞다. 오답 ① 한국 음식 문화에 대한 왕들의 영향 ② 여름철 요리로서의 냉면의 인기 ③ 한국 음식 배달 문화의 현대화 ④ 전통적인 한국 냉면의 제작 과정 18) (1) ⓐ that → which (2) ⓔ deliver → be delivered : ⓐ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was popular in the 1800s)을 이끌어 앞 절의 hyojonggaeng에 대한 부 연 설명을 하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, that을 계속 적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which로 고쳐야 한다. 참고로 that은 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 사용하지 않으며, 완전 한 절(A late ~ hyojonggaeng)에 접속사 없이 콤마로만 다른 완전한 절이 이어질 수 없으므로 동사 was에 대한 주어인 지시대명사 that도 될 수 없다. ⓔ 주어인 food(음식)가 ‘배달되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어지 는 목적어가 없으므로, ‘can+be+과거분사’ 형태의 조동사 의 수동태를 이루는 be delivered로 고친다. 19) ③: 새벽 종소리와 함께 먹는 국밥인 효종갱이 1800년대에 인기가 있었다고 되어 있을 뿐, 그 이유에 대한 언급은 없으므로, ③ ‘1800년대 효종갱의 인기의 이유’는 이 글 을 읽고 알 수 있는 내용으로 알맞지 않다. 오답 ① 효종갱에 사용된 재료의 종류 (→ 고기, 버섯, 각종 채소 등) ② 효종갱을 포장하고 배달하는 방식 (→ 솥에 담아 솜 으로 단단히 싸서 배달함) ④ 배달이 가능한 현대 음식의 종류 (→ 햄버거, 스테이 크, 디저트 등의 모든 종류의 음식) ⑤ 현대 배달 서비스의 장점 (→ 모든 종류의 음식에 적용되며, 음식이 한 시간도 안 되어 바로 집 앞에 배 달되어 식당에 갈 필요가 없음) 20) ③: 글쓴이의 새로운 인생의 목표는 한국을 여행하는 것이 라고 했으므로, ③ ‘글쓴이의 새로운 인생의 목표는 그 녀가 가장 좋아하는 프로그램들을 더 즐길 수 있도록 한국어를 배우는 것이다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 글쓴이는 집에서 한국 요리를 만들어 보기 위해 지 역의 한국 식료품점에서 재료를 산다. ② 글쓴이의 한국인 이웃은 그녀에게 한국 요리에 대 해 조언을 해 준다. ④ K-드라마를 보는 것은 글쓴이를 더 범세계적이고 다양한 문화에 관심을 갖도록 만들었다. ⑤ 글쓴이는 한국 여행 중에 현지 음식을 먹고 싶어 한다.

Hi, everybody. We’ll begin our tour today with this
picture, The Arnolfini Portrait ⓐcreated by Jan van
Eyck in the 15th century. I wonder ⓑif you have
ever thought about the stories behind the painting.
One story says ⓒwhat it’s a portrait of Mr. and
Mrs. Arnolfini, a newly married Dutch couple in
their house. There are many objects in the picture
and some of them are quite symbolic. Do you see
the mirror on the back wall? Mirrors represent holy
marriage. The dog ⓓstood between Mr. and Mrs.
Arnolfini may suggest a faithful marriage. Can you
guess
ⓔwhat

green

represents? It may be an expression of hope. Look

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward
Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper
lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and
he created paintings depicting urban scenes that
showed ________________________. Hopper’s Nighthawks
is a good example of this. There are four people in
the same diner, but they’re clearly not together. The
bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the
darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be
in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper’s
Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more
direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the
yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of
the other colors contrast with the warm yellow,
emphasizing that she’s on her own.

daily routines in a city might cause people tofeel bored or tired
bright colors like yellow can create feelings ofhappiness in viewers
a big city like New York can be too crowdedfor people to live comfortably
how even familiar surroundings could cause theviewer to feel a sense of loneliness비상(홍민표) 3과
