something that didn’t require a mechanical device.
One day, he was brainstorming with friends, and
the group came up with an idea for an app that
could translate sign language.
(A) In just a few months, he developed an app
based on artificial intelligence for translating
American Sign Language (ASL) in real time.
(B) Nand’s app was basically a speech-to-text app
for sign language, where hand movements
corresponded to speech.
(C) In the end, they decided not to develop it, but
Nand couldn’t stop thinking about the translator.
The hardest part was ⓐ__________________________. At
times, he felt he was stuck. When that happened,
he would go to sleep. For Nand, sleeping on it
paid off. He decided to focus on the body parts
which are important in signing, such as individual
fingertips. Using a machine-learning program, he
then taught the app to identify those key points in
the videos he took.

While ⓐthinking about her homework, Seoyoung
Jun closed one eye and successfully picked up her
pencil holder. At that moment, she realized that
orienting herself in a 3D space didn’t require both
eyes. This surprised her. With research, she learned
ⓑwhat the brain can process 3D information without
any vision at all. And with that, the idea for a new
device for people with visual disabilities was born.
Those who have lost sight ⓒgets their spatial
information mainly from touch, not vision. She
based her new navigation device on this fact. This
little device sends a beam of infrared light to
gather 3D information about what may lie around
the user, including walls and furniture. The bounced
beam conveys that information to the device, which
then ⓓraise little pins to indicate where those
obstacles are. By “reading” the positions and
heights of those pins, the user can understand the
arrangement of structures and objects lying ahead
and navigate around them.
The heart of this device is a 3D depth sensor
connected to a small computer. Seoyoung coded
the computer to control the nine motors ⓔlined up
in three rows of three so that each motor could
move a pin up and down. The sensor can scan
eighteen blocks of space before it, each 0.06㎥ in
size. When it detects an obstacle in any of these
blocks, the corresponding pin rises to either the
middle or high position, depending on the height
of the obstacle. By running your hand over the
nine pins, you can tell where the obstacles are and
how high they are.

the group came up with an idea for an app that
could translate sign language. In the end, they
decided not to develop it, but Nand couldn’t stop
thinking about the translator. In just a few months,
he __________________________________. Nand’s app was
basically a speech-to-text app for sign language,
where hand movements corresponded to speech.
The hardest part was figuring out how to make
the app recognize hand gestures. At times, he felt
he was stuck. When that happened, he would go to
sleep. For Nand, sleeping on it paid off. He decided
to focus on the body parts which are important in
signing, such as individual fingertips. Using a
machine-learning program, he then taught the app

Aranmula, a village in India, is home to the
traditional craft of mirror making. Here, the mirrors
are made entirely of metal. With typical glass
mirrors, light has to travel through the glass in
order to get reflected on the back of the glass
coated with metal. In contrast, the Aranmula mirror
reflects light on the surface of the metal and shows
a more accurate reflection. The craft has been
passed down in Aranmula for around 500 years.

father when she was little, including the formula for
the perfect ratio of tin and copper to create the
mirror’s reflective surface.

In Jeonju, Korea, Kim Dong-sik has been making
hapjukseons, traditional folding fans that used to be
reserved for royal families. He uses a 350-year-old
technique ⓐthat has been passed down through his
family. Although the fan looks simple, the process
of making it involves about 150 manual steps
ⓑused natural materials. It ⓒtakes four to five days
to make just one fan.
It starts with ⓓpreparing bamboo. He makes it
soft by boiling it and leaves it out to dry for up to
two weeks. Then, he splits the bamboo into strips
and thins them down again and again until you can
see through them. He then glues two strips into
one rib and binds the ribs tightly. This makes the
fan incredibly ⓔstrong. Now that the framework is
ready, he spreads the fan ribs out with glue applied
on them. Then, he carefully attaches paper to the
ribs, ⓕfolds it for each rib. Afterward, the fan may
be left plain or ⓖdecorate by a painter.
Kim says, “To make a fan, you need a lot of patience
and determination. In the old days, all the fans were
made this way. (A)온전한 전통 기법들이 학습되고 미래
에 전수될 수 있도록 저는 이것을 고수하고 있습니다.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ used → using (수식을 받는 150 manual steps(150 단계의 수작업 공정)가 천연 재료를 ‘사용하는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나 타내는 현재분사 using으로 고친다.) ⓕ folds → folding (동사(attaches)가 있는 완전한 절(he ~ ribs) 뒤 에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 또 다른 동사가 연결될 수 없으므로 분 사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 의미상 주어인 he(그)가 it(그것), 곧 종이를 살마다 ‘접는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어인 it이 이어지고 있으므 로 folds를 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 folding으로 고친다.) ⓖ decorate → decorated (주어 the fan이 ‘남겨지는’ 그리고 ‘장식 되는’ 대상으로 조동사 may 뒤에 이어지는 be동사의 원형 be와 함 께 수동태를 이루는 과거분사 left와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되 어 있으므로 동사원형 decorate를 과거분사 decorated로 고친다.)

First of all, we need to be clear about the role of
the tongue. The information our tongues send to
our brains is very simple. We generally like
sweetness and hate bitterness, and the biological
reasons for that are deeply rooted in our brains.
For one, babies like sweet tastes, not bitter ones,
since bitterness can indicate poison. Not liking bitter
things is, in a sense, a natural defense mechanism.
Due to genetic differences, some people may be
more
sensitive
than
others
to
bitterness.
Interestingly, how sensitive you are to bitterness
doesn’t always relate to whether or not you like a
certain type of food. For example, the fact that
someone thinks celery is more bitter than other
people find it does not necessarily mean the person
can’t grow to like it. Likewise, even if you find it to
be less bitter than others do, you may still hate it.

First of all, we need to be clear about the role of
the tongue. The information our tongues send to
our brains is very ⓐsimple. We generally like
sweetness and hate bitterness, and the biological
reasons for that are deeply rooted in our brains.
For one, babies like sweet tastes, not bitter ones,
since bitterness can indicate poison. Not liking bitter
things is, in a sense, a natural defense mechanism.
ⓑDue to genetic differences, some people may be
more
sensitive
than
others
to
bitterness.
Interestingly, how sensitive you are to bitterness
doesn’t always ⓒrelate to whether or not you like
a certain type of food. For example, the fact that
someone thinks celery is more bitter than other
people find it does not necessarily ⓓmean the
person can’t grow to like it. Likewise, even if you
find it to be less bitter than others do, you may
still hate it.
The information our tongues convey does not,
however, paint a full picture of the world of tastes.
There are also flavors, a wider spectrum of
sensations we get from food. To ⓔappreciate
flavors such as chocolate, vanilla, blue cheese, and
cilantro, we need not just our tongues, but more
importantly our noses. As we chew food, its smells
make their way to the back of our noses from
inside our mouths, enabling us to distinguish
between many flavors. Some scientists discovered
that individuals with a certain gene are more
sensitive to the smell of cilantro. These people are
likely to say it has a soapy flavor.

As a coder, Nand Vinchhi wanted to invent
something that didn’t require a mechanical device.
(A)One day, he was brainstorming with friends, and
the group came up with an idea for an app that
could translate sign language. (B)In the end, they
decided not to develop it, but Nand couldn’t stop
thinking about the translator. (C)In just a few months,
he developed an app based on artificial intelligence
for translating American Sign Language (ASL) in real
time. (D)Despite its wide use, no accurate count of
ASL users has been kept. (E)Nand’s app was
basically a speech-to-text app for sign language,
where hand movements corresponded to speech.
The hardest part was figuring out how to make
the app recognize hand gestures. At times, he felt
he was stuck. When that happened, he would go to
sleep. For Nand, ⓐsleeping on it paid off. He decided
to focus on the body parts which are important in
signing, such as individual fingertips. Using a
machine-learning program, he then taught the app
to identify those key points in the videos he took.

choices: He failed because he wasted too much timesleeping.
He avoided solving the problem by going tobed early.
Taking a break by sleeping helped him discovera solution.
He used sleep as a way to escape from theproblem permanently.

Cars are now making steps toward their own kind
of freedom; that is, freedom from people. The goal
is to build a car that uses artificial intelligence so
that it thinks and drives like a human. The
technology for a self-driving car has reached the
point where it is becoming increasingly accessible.
Self-driving cars have clear advantages. Most of all,
sitting behind the wheel would no longer be limited
by age or ability. ⓐ____________________, a person
who has lost sight could rely on a self-driving car
to go from one place to another. Furthermore,
most accidents are caused by careless people on
the road. For example, many crashes are caused by
people using their phones while driving, falling
asleep at the wheel, or driving while drunk. With a
self-driving car, people would not need to worry
about such situations on the road.
ⓑ____________________, there are also some serious
concerns when it comes to the safety of self-driving
cars, since the technology is still far from perfect. In
fact, a self-driving car depends only on its sensors,
GPS, and computer programs to work properly. If
any of these broke down or were used for
unintended purposes, then the safety and security
of the rider as well as other people on the road
could be put at risk.

Personal Experiences
Can we learn to like a food we’ve long disliked?
“Your biology is not your destiny. When you’re
open to different foods, you learn to like what you
eat,” answers Julie Mennella, a researcher from the
Monell Chemical Senses Center. She says that kids
are particularly adaptable when it comes to learning
to like new foods. Research has shown that after
tasting a food eight or ten times, children will
become more accepting of it. Similarly, even people
who hate cilantro may be able to learn to tolerate
it or even like it. Over time and through exposure,
they can build up tolerance to cilantro, by adding a
small amount in a curry, for example.

First of all, we need to be clear about the role of
the tongue. The information our tongues send to
our brains is very simple. We generally like
sweetness and hate bitterness, and the biological
reasons for that are deeply rooted in our brains.
For one, babies like sweet tastes, not bitter ones,
since bitterness can indicate poison. Not liking bitter
things is, in a sense, a natural defense mechanism.

Food diplomacy means using food as a tool to
promote cooperation and peace. It is practiced at
many levels. For example, when the president of a
country hosts a state dinner, the meal serves as a
symbolic gesture of welcoming and honoring the
visiting head of state. Some governments even
launch public food diplomacy campaigns, using
food to promote trade or tourism. Food diplomacy
can also occur on an everyday level when each of
us interacts with people from around the world
through
food,
whether
at
a
neighborhood
Vietnamese restaurant, an Indian food truck in
Melbourne, or a Mexican taco stand in Berlin. In

global

we

more

restaurants serving food from formerly unreachable

of ourselves as well as other cultures. If you want
to learn about our global neighbors, sometimes it is

Can we learn to like a food we’ve long disliked?

who hate cilantro may be able to learn to tolerate

they can build up tolerance to cilantro, by adding a

Host: Welcome to Meet the Artisans. Our guest
today is Mr. Kim Deok-man. He’s here to talk
about yeot, an old Korean treat. Mr. Kim,
could you please introduce ⓐyourself to our
viewers?
Mr. Kim: Sure. Hello, everyone! It’s great to be here.
I’m from Chungju, Korea, and specialize in
making yeot.
Host: Could you first tell us a little bit about yeot?
When did Koreans first start enjoying it?
Mr. Kim: It is said that yeot dates back more than
1,000 years. Back in the old days, only the
rich could eat yeot, but nowadays, everyone
can enjoy it. It’s still popular.
Host: It has a long history. Where did you learn
how to make yeot?
Mr. Kim: I learned it from my father and grandfather.
Our family ⓑhas been made yeot for 140 years.
Host: Wow, that’s quite a long time! Could you
describe how to make it?
Mr. Kim: I stick to the traditional method and recipe.
First, ⓒsteamed rice is mixed with barley
malt and then fermented for several hours.
After that, it is boiled to make yeot batter.
The batter is then stretched and ⓓfolded
back over and over again by hand. Lastly,
it is cut into small pieces.
Host: Interesting! What do you think is important in
your work?
Mr. Kim: I think it’s important to pass down the
traditional family yeot recipe from one
generation
to
the
next.
I’m
proudly
representing the culture and tradition, and
that pride keeps me ⓔgoing.
Host: Mr. Kim, thank you for joining us.

Host: Welcome to Meet the Artisans. Our guest
today is Mr. Kim Deok-man. He’s here to talk
about yeot, an old Korean treat. Mr. Kim,
could you please introduce ⓐyourself to our
viewers?
Mr. Kim: Sure. Hello, everyone! It’s great to be here.
I’m from Chungju, Korea, and specialize in
making yeot.
Host: Could you first tell us a little bit about yeot?
When did Koreans first start enjoying it?
Mr. Kim: It is said that yeot dates back more than
1,000 years. Back in the old days, only the
rich could eat yeot, but nowadays, everyone
can enjoy it. It’s still popular.
Host: It has a long history. Where did you learn
how to make yeot?
Mr. Kim: I learned it from my father and grandfather.
Our family ⓑhas been made yeot for 140 years.
Host: Wow, that’s quite a long time! Could you
describe how to make it?
Mr. Kim: I stick to the traditional method and recipe.
First, ⓒsteamed rice is mixed with barley
malt and then fermented for several hours.
After that, it is boiled to make yeot batter.
The batter is then stretched and ⓓfolded
back over and over again by hand. Lastly,
it is cut into small pieces.
Host: Interesting! What do you think is important in
your work?
Mr. Kim: I think it’s important to pass down the
traditional family yeot recipe from one
generation
to
the
next.
I’m
proudly
representing the culture and tradition, and
that pride keeps me ⓔgoing.
Host: Mr. Kim, thank you for joining us.

In Jeonju, Korea, Kim Dong-sik has been making
hapjukseons, traditional folding fans that used to be
reserved for royal families. He uses a 350-year-old
technique that has been passed down through his
family. Although the fan looks simple, the process
of making it involves about 150 manual steps using
natural materials. It takes four to five days to make
just one fan.

Biology
First of all, we need to be clear about the role of
the tongue. The information our tongues send to
our brains is very simple. We generally like
sweetness and hate bitterness, and the biological
reasons for that are deeply rooted in our brains.
(A) For one, babies like sweet tastes, not bitter
ones, since bitterness can indicate poison. Not
liking bitter things is, in a sense, a natural
defense mechanism.
(B) For example, the fact that someone thinks celery
is more bitter than other people find it does
not necessarily mean the person can’t grow to
like it. Likewise, even if you find it to be less
bitter than others do, you may still hate it.
(C) Due to genetic differences, some people may be
more
sensitive
than
others
to
bitterness.
Interestingly, how sensitive you are to bitterness
doesn’t always relate to whether or not you like
a certain type of food.

Food diplomacy means using food as a tool to
promote cooperation and peace. It is practiced at
many levels. For example, when the president of a
country hosts a state dinner, the meal serves as a
symbolic gesture of welcoming and honoring the
visiting head of state. Some governments even
launch public food diplomacy campaigns, (A)[using /
use] food to promote trade or tourism. Food
diplomacy can also occur on an everyday level
when each of us (B)[interact / interacts] with people
from around the world through food, whether at a
neighborhood Vietnamese restaurant, an Indian food
truck in Melbourne, or a Mexican taco stand in
Berlin. In today’s global economy, we are more
interconnected than ever, with grocery store shelves
filled with large options from across the world and
restaurants (C)[serving / served] food from formerly
unreachable places. Having access to the cuisines
and cultures of the world has allowed for a better
understanding of ourselves as well as other cultures.
If you want to learn about our global neighbors,
sometimes it is as easy as going out for dinner.
(A)
(B)
(C)

(C) 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+목적어+분사’ 형태의 분사구문 으로, with의 목적어 restaurants가 음식을 ‘제공하는’ 주체이므 로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 serving이 알맞다. 참고로, 전치사 with에 이어 두 개의 ‘명사구+분사구’가 등위접속사 and로 병 렬 연결된 형태이다. 천재(강상구) 3과

Food preferences vary across cultures, too. Every
culture may have something that is considered
disagreeable in other cultures. Durian fruit from
Southeast Asia or American sweet potato pie
topped with marshmallows may seem distasteful to
people not familiar with them. In fact, food
preferences in different parts of the world have a
lot to do with what is available or essential: for
instance, beans in Mexico, okra in India, and
fermented shark in Iceland. Of course, we cannot
predict food preferences solely on the basis of a
person’s cultural background, as Isabella’s case
showed with cilantro.
It is not surprising that our food preferences are
as varied as the foods we eat. Some of the
preferences are biological, and some are learned.
Given this, is it any wonder that all sorts of foods
have both fans and haters?

Personal Experiences
Can we learn to like a food we’ve long disliked?
“Your biology is not your destiny. When you’re
open to different foods, you learn to like what you
eat,” answers Julie Mennella, a researcher from the
Monell Chemical Senses Center. She says that kids
are particularly adaptable when it comes to learning
to like new foods. Research has shown that after
tasting a food eight or ten times, children will
become more accepting of it. Similarly, even people
who hate cilantro may be able to learn to tolerate
it or even like it. Over time and through exposure,
they can build up tolerance to cilantro, by adding a
small amount in a curry, for example.

kids are particularly (A)[adaptable / resistant] when

tolerance to cilantro, by adding a small amount in

especially those you had when you were young —
can have a (B)[lasting / temporary] effect. Suppose

(C)[avoid / enjoy] the food for a long time. In

ⓕmake you like some foods. For example, you

solution: ⓑ which ~ → what ~ (like의 목적어 자리에서 동사 eat의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you eat)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 which를 선행 사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what으로 고쳐야 한다.) ⓔ ~ serving → ~ served (주어인 you는 미역국을 ‘제공받은’ 대상이므로 ‘serve A B(A에 게 B를 내놓다/제공하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘A be served B(A가 B를 제공받다)’를 써야 한다. 이때 be 대신 get을 사용하여 수 동의 의미를 나타낼 수 있으므로 get을 사용한 것은 적절하나, get 뒤에는 과거분사가 이어져야 하므로 serving을 served로 고쳐야 한다.) ⓖ ~ made ~ → ~ making ~ (전치사 of의 목적어인 동명사구를 이루는 자리로, 타동사 make(만들다)의 의미상 주어인 your grandmother가 수정과를 ‘만든’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어로 수정과를 가리키는 대명사 it이 이어지므로, 능동형 동명사인 making으로 고쳐야 한다.)

Food diplomacy means using food as a tool to
promote cooperation and peace. It is practiced at
many levels. For example, when the president of a
country hosts a state dinner, the meal serves as a
symbolic gesture of welcoming and honoring the
visiting head of state. Some governments even
launch public food diplomacy campaigns, using
food to promote trade or tourism. Food diplomacy
can also occur on an everyday level when each of
us interacts with people from around the world
through
food,
whether
at
a
neighborhood
Vietnamese restaurant, an Indian food truck in
Melbourne, or a Mexican taco stand in Berlin. In
today’s
global
economy,
we
are
more
interconnected than ever, with grocery store shelves
filled with large options from across the world and
restaurants serving food from formerly unreachable
places. Having access to the cuisines and cultures
of the world has allowed for a better understanding
of ourselves as well as other cultures. If you want
to learn about our global neighbors, sometimes it is
as easy as going out for dinner.

If you had to choose our greatest predator in
nature, which would you pick? Sharks, lions, or
bears? According to history professor Timothy
Winegard, it is actually the mosquito. Mosquitoes
can pass on ⓐdeadly diseases like malaria and
yellow fever. Over a million people worldwide die of
these diseases every year. Throughout history,
Winegard ⓑestimates that mosquitoes have killed
more people than any other single cause — about
fifty-two billion people, nearly half of all humans
who have ever lived.
Winegard claims that mosquitoes also played a
role in shaping the history of several countries. Take
the Roman Empire, for example. The fall of the
Western Roman Empire was ⓒsudden, spanning
over centuries. Here are commonly cited reasons for
the fall of the empire: invasions by outside forces,
economic troubles, and corruption. Diseases like
malaria, however, also ⓓcontributed. Rome, the
capital of the empire, was once surrounded by a
huge stretch of wetland. This was an ideal breeding
ground for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for
malaria. On the one hand, mosquitoes helped
protect the city against the armies coming to attack
it. However, they eventually spread the disease not
only throughout the city, but also throughout the
empire, ⓔcrushing much of the population.

body:
In Jeonju, Korea, Kim Dong-sik has been making
hapjukseons, traditional folding fans that used to be
reserved for royal families. He uses a 350-year-old
technique that has been passed down through his
family. Although the fan looks simple, the process
of making it involves about 150 manual steps using
natural materials. It takes four to five days to make
just one fan.
It starts with preparing bamboo. He makes it soft
by boiling it and leaves it out to dry for up to two
weeks. Then, he splits the bamboo into strips and
thins them down again and again until you can see
through them. He then glues two strips into one
rib and binds the ribs tightly. This makes the fan
incredibly strong. (A)이제 틀이 준비되었으니, 그것들
위에 풀이 발린 채로 그는 부챗살을 펼친다. Then, he
carefully attaches paper to the ribs, folding it for
each rib. Afterward, the fan may be left plain or
decorated by a painter.
Kim says, “To make a fan, you need a lot of
patience and determination. In the old days, all the
fans were made this way. I stand by this so that
the perfect traditional skills can be taught and
carried into the future.”

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Life Philosophy of Handicraft Masters
The Patience and Craftsmanship Behind Hapjukseons
Master of the Hapjukseon Training His YoungerStudents
The Quality of a Hapjukseon Depends on theBamboo Used
solution: 가문 대대로 내려오는 350년 된 기법을 사용하여 150 단계의 수작업 공정을 거쳐 합죽선을 만드는 세심한 과정과 합죽선을 만들려면 상당한 인내심과 결의가 필요하다는 김동식 씨의 말 을 통해 합죽선 뒤에는 인내와 장인 정신이 숨어 있음을 시사 한 내용이므로, ❸ ‘합죽선 뒤의 인내와 장인 정신’이 제목으로 알맞다.

Earthworms are a great addition to your garden as
well. They help keep your soil soft and breathable
by digging tunnels that bring air to the roots of
plants. They also eat the dead bits of plants that
fall to the ground, recycling them back into the soil
and helping new plants to grow. ⓐ_________________,
their waste makes your soil richer, and they are
excellent at breaking down organic matter in your
garden. ⓑ_________________, you should be careful
about applying artificial fertilizers to your garden
after introducing earthworms. They will find a new
home when the soil around them changes.

ⓑ
solution: ⓐ 지렁이가 식물의 죽은 부분들을 흙으로 재순환시켜 새로운 식물이 자라도록 돕는다는 내용 뒤에 지렁이가 정원에 제공하 는 또 다른 도움으로, 지렁이의 배설물은 토양을 더 비옥하게 만든다는 내용이 추가되고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 ‘게다가’를 뜻하 는 What’s more, In addition, Besides가 알맞다. ⓑ 정원에 있는 유기물을 분해하는 데에 탁월하다는 지렁이의 긍정적 역할을 설명한 뒤에 인공 비료를 사용하면 지렁이가 새로운 서식지를 찾을 수 있으므로 조심해야 한다는 역접 관 계의 내용이 연결되므로, ‘그렇기는 하지만’을 뜻하는 Even so 나 ‘그러나’를 뜻하는 However가 알맞다.

body:
If you had to choose our greatest predator in
nature, which would you pick? Sharks, lions, or bears?
According to history professor Timothy Winegard, it is
actually the mosquito. Mosquitoes can pass on ⓐ[fatal
/ mild] diseases like malaria and yellow fever. Over a
million people worldwide die of these diseases every
year. Throughout history, Winegard estimates that
mosquitoes have killed more people than any other
single cause — about fifty-two billion people, nearly
half of all humans who have ever lived.
Winegard claims that mosquitoes also played a role
in shaping the history of several countries. Take the
Roman Empire, for example. The fall of the Western
Roman Empire was ⓑ[immediate / progressive],
spanning over centuries.
(A) On the one hand, mosquitoes helped protect
the city against the armies coming to attack it.
However, they eventually spread the disease not
only throughout the city, but also throughout
the empire, crushing much of the population.
(B) Rome, the capital of the empire, was once
surrounded by a huge stretch of wetland. This
was a(n) ⓒ[adverse / flawless] breeding ground
for mosquitoes and hence a hot spot for malaria.
(C) Here are commonly cited reasons for the fall of
the empire: invasions by outside forces, economic
troubles, and corruption. Diseases like malaria,

earthworms. They will find a new home when the

term은 ‘기간’이라는 뜻으로 쓰였으나, ‘a word orexpression with a particular meaning, especially onethat is used for a specific subject or type oflanguage(특정한 의미를 가진 단어나 표현, 특히 특정주제나 언어 유형에 사용되는 단어나 표현)’는 term의여러 뜻 유용한 일을 하다② ⓑ변명: 어떤 잘못이나 거슬리는 행동을 옹호하거나 의무 등을 이행하지 않은 것에 대한 이유로 제공되는 설명④ ⓓ압박감: 특히 해야 할 일이 너무 많다고 느끼기때문에 많은 불안을 유발하는 일과 생활 방식⑤ ⓔ어려운[도전적인]: 흥미롭거나 즐거운 방식으로 어려운12) ②: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.ⓓ calling → called이중 콤마(,)로 삽입된 분사구로, 문장의 주어 Thiseffect를 부연 설명하고 있다. 주어 This effect는 ‘불리는’ 대상이므로, 능동의 현재분사 calling이 아닌 수동을나타내는 과거분사 called가 쓰여야 알맞다.ⓕ expressing → to express등위접속사 and에 의해 asked는 앞의 be동사 were에이어지는 shown과 병렬 연결되어 수동태를 이루고 있으므로, '…가 ~하도록 요청하다‘의 의미를 갖는 5형식동사 ask의 능동태 ’ask+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)‘를전환한 ‘be동사+asked+to부정사(~하도록 요청받다)’의수동태를 써야 한다. 따라서 expressing을 to express로고쳐야 한다.오답ⓐ 과거부터 현재까지 “에펠탑 효과”를 들어본 적이 있는지 경험을 물었으므로 현재완료가 쓰인 것은 알맞으며 hear of는 ‘~에 관해 듣다’라는 뜻이므로 Have youever heard of ~는 알맞다.ⓑ all은 ‘all+(of)+the[소유격, 지시형용사]+명사’의 형태로 쓰이며, 전치사 of는 생략할 수 있으므로 all theother architecture는 알맞다. 선행사가 all the otherarchitecture in Paris이고 쉼표 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절이 오므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가쓰인 것, architecture가 집합명사로 쓰였고 시제가 과거이므로 관계대명사 which에 대한 동사로 단수 과거 동사 was가 쓰인 것, 주어 which의 선행사 all the otherarchitecture in Paris가 돌로 만들어진 대상이므로 수동태 was made가 쓰인 것은 알맞다.ⓒ 등위접속사 and에 의해 disliked와 병렬 연결된complained는 알맞으며, 뒤에 완전한 절(it ~ Paris)을이끌어 complained의 목적어 역할을 하는 접속사 that도 알맞다. 또한 주절의 시제가 과거이므로 조동사 will의 과거 would가 쓰인 것도 알맞다.ⓔ 범위가 정해지지 않은 집단에서 ‘어떤 ~’과 ‘다른 ~’을 칭할 때 some과 others를 쓰므로 others를 쓴 것,others는 복수이며 과거 시제이자, ‘보여지는’ 대상이므로 수동태 were shown이 쓰인 것은 알맞다.13) This shows that the more we are exposed to something,the more favorably we view it.    : • 주어 ‘이것’을 This로 쓰고 동사를 이에 맞게 3인칭 단수 현재형 shows로 쓴다.• 목적어 ‘우리가 어떤 것에 더 많이 노출될수록 그것을더 호의적으로 본다’를 ‘~할수록 …하다’를 표현하는 문형’the+비교급~, the+비교급…‘의 형태로 영작한다. ‘우리가어떤 것에 더 많이 노출될수록‘은 주어 we(우리)가 ’노출되는‘ 대상이므로 expose A to B(A를 B에 노출시키다)를수동태 are exposed to ~(~네 노출되다)를 써서 themore we are exposed to something으로 영작한다.• ’그것을 더 호의적으로 본다‘의 주어는 ’우리‘이므로 we를 주어로 쓰고 ’호의적으로‘는 형용사 favorable을 부사favorably로 변형해서 the more favorably we view it으로 영작한다.14) ③: 사람들이 처음 세워졌을 때는 싫어했던 에펠탑을 계속보게 되자 좋아하게 된 사례를 통해 에펠탑 효과를 이야기하고, 그와 같은 효과로 심리학자 로버트 자이언스가 사람들의 얼굴 사진 노출 횟수와 호감도의 관계를조사한 실험을 통해 밝혀진 단순 노출 효과를 설명한뒤 결론으로 우리는 어떤 것에 더 자주 노출될수록 그것을 더 호의적으로 본다고 서술함으로써 사람이든 사물이든 자주 접할수록 호감을 느끼게 되는 심리 현상을 설명한 글이다. 따라서 ③ ‘자주 보면 정든다’가 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞다.오답① 파리 건축의 역사② 아름다움의 고정된 심리적 기준④ 에펠탑은 어떻게 세상을 매료했나⑤ 단순 노출 효과: 광고 속 심리학15) ④: ⓓ give in은 ‘항복하다’라는 뜻이므로 ‘제출하다’의 뜻으로 쓰인 submit 대신 쓸 수 없다. hand in, present 등을 submit 대신 쓸 수 있다.오답ⓐ particular가 ‘특별한’의 뜻으로 쓰였으므로 special(특별한)로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.ⓑ occur는 ‘일어나다, 생기다‘라는 뜻이므로 happened(일어났다) 대신 occurred를 뜻 수 있다.ⓒ opt for는 ’~을 선택하다‘라는 뜻이므로 choose(고르다, 선택하다) 대신 쓸 수 있다.ⓔ register는 ’(명부에) 이름을 올리다’, ’등록하다‘라는뜻이므로 signed up(등록했다) 대신 쓸 수 있다.16) ②: 하준이는 동아리 선택을 앞두고 야외 활동을 좋아하지않기에 어떤 것이든 실내 동아리를 선택할 생각이었음에도 불구하고, 많은 급우가 축구 동아리를 선택하자그들을 따라 축구 동아리에 가입했다가 결국 후회를 했다는 내용의 글로, 그런 하준이의 후회를 통해 다른 사람들이 아닌 자신에게 맞는 것을 선택해야 후회하지 않는다는 사실을 알 수 있다. 따라서 ② ‘후회하지 않을결정을 내리기 위해서는 다른 사람이 아닌 자신에게 맞는 것을 선택해야 한다.’가 글의 시사점으로 알맞다.오답① 어떤 것의 인기가 그 품질이나 가치를 보장하지는않는다.③ 자신만의 특별한 선호가 없다면, 무언가를 선택하는데 어려움을 겪게 된다.④ 무언가에 대한 충분한 정보 없이 결정을 내릴 때는군중을 따르는 것이 안전하다.⑤ 학교생활에서 무언가를 결정해야 할 때는 학교 상담사나 교사에게 도움을 구하는 것이 좋다.17) ③: 사람들은 과제를 잘 수행할 자신감이 없을 때, 스스로성공에 방해가 되는 장애물을 만드는 “자기불구화”를하는데 이는 좋지 않은 성과에 대해 변명할 수 있게함으로써 자존감이 낮아지는 것을 막아주는 단기적 효과가 있을 수 있지만 결국은 자신감이 없는 특정 과제에서 반복적인 실패로 이어질 수 있다는 내용이므로,자기불구화에 의한 변명은 나쁜 결과가 자존감을 낮추는 것을 막아준다는 문장과 그것은 단기적으로 효과가있을 수 있다는 문장 사이에서 자신감과 자존감의 차이를 밝힌 (C) ‘자신감은 우리의 능력에 대한 태도와관련이 있는 데 반해, 자존감은 우리 자신에 대한 사랑과 우리가 자신을 소중히 여기는 방식과 관련이 있다.’가 글의 흐름과 상관없는 문장이다.18) ⑤: (A) 심리학자들에 따르면 사람들은 단지 다른 사람들이하고 있다는 이유로 특정 행동에 참여하는 경향이 있으며 사람들은 또래 집단에서 제외되는 것을 원하지 않는다는 내용에 이어지며 These psychological factors(이러한 심리적 요인)는 앞의 이 내용을 가리키므로, 그런심리적 요인이 사람들이 자신만의 행동을 하기보다는군중을 따르게 만든다는 흐름이 되어야 자연스럽다. 따라서 prompt(촉발하다)가 알맞다.forbid 금지하다본문변형 cause → prompt(B) 뒤에 역접의 but(그러나)에 이어 그것, 곧 군중을따르는 것은 후회로 이어진다는 내용이 오므로, 이와모순되는 내용, 곧 군중을 따르는 것이 항상 나쁜 결과로 이어지는 것은 아니라는 내용이 와야 흐름상 자연스럽다. 따라서 adverse(불리한, 해로운)가 알맞다.favorable 유리한본문변형 negative → adverse(C) 그것, 즉 자신이 진정으로 원하는 것이 친구들과 다를지라도 자신의 선택을 하는 것을 두려워하지 말라는내용에 이어지므로, 자신에게 맞는 올바른 선택을 한다면, 그 결정에 대해 만족할 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 자연스럽다. 따라서 happy(행복한)가 알맞다.unhappy 불행한19) ③: 주어진 문장이 ‘가장 중요한 것은 부정적인 감정을 극복할 수 있는 자신만의 방법을 찾는 것입니다.’라는 뜻이므로, 주어진 문장을 It(그것)으로 지칭해 부정적인감정을 극복할 수 있는 자신만의 방법을 찾는 것의 결과를 ‘그것은 당신의 학교생활을 훨씬 더 즐겁게 만들어 줄 것입니다.’라고 진술한 문장 앞인 (C)에 들어가는것이 알맞다.20) ③: 글 전반부에서 지역 사람들은 처음 세워졌을 때 에펠탑을 싫어했지만 자주 보게 되면서 좋아하게 되었다고 에펠탑 효과를 소개하고, ‘단순 노출 효과’라고도 불리는이 효과는 사람들에게서도 발견된다며 그와 관련된 심리학자 로버트 자이언스와 동료들의 실험에서 학생들은자주 본 사람들을 덜 본 사람들보다 더 좋아했다고 밝혔다. 따라서 흐름상 This(이것), 즉 학생들은 자주 본사람들을 덜 본 사람들보다 더 좋아했다는 사실을 통해알 수 있는 것은 글의 결론으로서 우리는 어떤 것에 더많이 노출될수록 그것을 더 좋게 본다는 내용이 되어야한다. 따라서 ③ ‘우리는 그것을 더 호의적으로 생각한다’가 빈칸에 알맞다.오답① 우리는 그것을 더 바꾸고 싶어 한다② 우리는 그것에 관해 더 궁금해 한다④ 우리는 그것을 더 쓸모없게 여긴다⑤ 우리는 그것에 대해 더 무관심해진다본문변형 the more favorably we view it → the morefavorable we consider it

When people do not have the confidence to
perform tasks well, they are likely to create
obstacles to success. This type of behavior is
referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping
enables people (A)[making / to make] excuses for
their poor performances. These excuses prevent the
poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This
might work in the short term. However, be careful!
It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks
that you are not confident in doing.
If you are self-handicapping, it might be (B)[because
/ because of] you consider the results more
important than the process. ⓐ_______________________
may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly,
you may feel more (C)[encouraging / encouraged]
to try to do the challenging tasks. This can
eventually stop your self-handicapping.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)               (B)               (C)
solution: (A) ‘…가 ~하는 것을 가능하게 하다’의 의미를 갖는 5형식 동 사 enable은 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, to make가 알맞다. (B) you consider the results ~라는 완전한 절이 이어지므로 접속사 because가 알맞다. 구전치사 because of 뒤에는 명사 (구)가 온다. (C) feel의 주격보어로서 주어 you가 ‘격려받는’ 대상이므로 수 동의 관계를 뜻하는 과거분사형 형용사 encouraged가 알맞다.

When people do not have the confidence to
perform tasks well, they are likely to create
obstacles to success. This type of behavior is
referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping
enables people (A)[making / to make] excuses for
their poor performances. These excuses prevent the
poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This
might work in the short term. However, be careful!
It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks
that you are not confident in doing.
If you are self-handicapping, it might be (B)[because
/ because of] you consider the results more
important than the process. ⓐ_______________________
may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly,
you may feel more (C)[encouraging / encouraged]
to try to do the challenging tasks. This can
eventually stop your self-handicapping.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Being consoled by others when you fail
Trying tasks that are less challenging to accomplish
Putting more emphasis on the process than theoutcome
solution: 빈칸에는 잘해야 한다는 압박감을 줄일 수 있는 방법이 들어 가야 하는데, ‘만약 여러분이 자기불구화를 하고 있다면 이는 결과를 과정보다 더 중요하게 생각하기 때문일 수 있다’는 앞 문장을 통해, ‘결과보다 과정을 중시하는 것’이 잘해야 한다는 압박감을 줄여 줄 수 있다는 맥락임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 ❺ ‘결과보다 과정에 더 중점을 두는 것’이 빈칸에 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ engage: to be doing or to become involved inan activity
ⓑ peer: a person who is an equal in social standing,rank, age, etc.
ⓒ factor: something that helps you to be moresuccessful than others, or the state of havingthis
ⓓ phenomenon: something that happens or existsin society, science, or nature, especially somethingthat is studied because it is difficult to understand
ⓔ afraid: frightened because you think that youmay get hurt or that something bad may happen
solution: factor는 ‘요인’이라는 뜻이나, ‘something that helps you to be more successful than others, or the state of having this (다른 사람들보다 더 성공할 수 있도록 도와주는 것, 또는 이 것을 가지고 있는 상태)’은 advantage(이점)에 대한 영영풀이 이므로 알맞지 않다. factor는 ‘something that contributes to a result or influences a situation(결과에 기여하거나 상황에 영향을 미치는 것)‘과 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다. 천재(조수경) 1과

The first case is about a student named Hajun. On
the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher
introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun
didn't have a particular preference for any of them.
He thought that any indoor club would be ⓐfine
since he was not an outdoor person. Can you
guess what ⓑhappened on the day of choice? He
joined the soccer club. What made him choose
soccer?
Well, a few days before submitting his application,
he heard that the soccer club was so ⓒpopular
that half of his classmates were applying for it. This
made him think that the soccer club was something
ⓓdull. With this in mind, he signed up for the
soccer club just because others did so. However,
after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer
was not for him. In the end, he ⓔregretted his
decision.

choices: Hajun, who thought carefully about which clubto join
Hajun, who joined the soccer club to makemany friends
the difference between Hajun's criteria for clubselection and those of his classmates
Hajun, who regretted following his classmatesand choosing a club that didn't suit him
Hajun's regret for choosing a club by followinghis classmates' choices rather than his homeroomteacher's advice

When people do not have the confidence to
perform tasks well, they are likely to create
obstacles to success. This type of behavior is
referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping
enables people to make excuses for their poor
performances. These excuses prevent the poor result
from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in
the short term. However, be careful! It could lead
to repeated failures in certain tasks that you are
not confident in doing.
If you are self-handicapping, it might be because
you consider the results more important than the
process. Focusing more on the process than the
outcome may ease the pressure to perform well.
Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try
to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually
stop your self-handicapping.
choices: People can excuse themselves for their bad resultsby self-handicapping.
People are inclined to create barriers to successwhen they are not assured of good results.
The reason you are self-handicapping could bethat you value the result over the process.
You can continue to do well in jobs that you arenot confident about by means of self-handicapping.
If the strain of carrying out tasks well is reduced,you may feel more inspired to try to do difficultones.

May 20.
This morning, I woke up to the most annoying
noise. I realized ⓐ[what / that] it was the sound of
cicadas, but I had never heard ones this loud! Then,
I read in the news that every 17 years a special
kind
of
cicada
which
ⓑ[called
/
is
called]
magicicada emerges here in Bloomington, and this
year is the 17th year. These magicicadas spend 17
years underground feeding on roots, and then
come to the surface for a few weeks to reproduce
and die. Now I know why it was the first time I
had heard them so loud. I’m 17.
According to the Internet, depending on the
species and their location, cicadas spend different
amounts of time underground. Most species emerge
annually, but there are others that come out at
longer intervals. The magicicadas in Bloomington
emerge every 17 years, but ones in other regions
can have intervals of 13 or 17 years.
Then, it hit me: 13 and 17 are prime numbers. I
remembered learning in math class that a prime
number is any natural number larger than 1 and
ⓒ[is / was] only divisible by 1 and itself. For
example, the prime numbers below 20 are: 2, 3, 5,
7, 11, 13, 17, and 19. I never imagined that there
are mathematical patterns in nature. I wonder why
magicicadas emerge in intervals of prime numbers.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
solution: ⓐ 동사 realized의 목적어 자리로, 완전한 절(it was the sound of cicadas)이어지므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. ⓑ that 절에서 주어의 핵심인 선행사 a special kind of cicada를 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, ‘call A B(A를 B라 고 부르다)’의 수동태는 ‘A be called B(A가 B라고 불리다)’로 쓰며, 선행사가 B에 해당하는 magicicada라고 ‘불리는’ 대상이 므로, 수동태 is called가 적절하다. ⓒ 동명사 learning의 목적어절인 ‘that a prime number is ~’ 의 주어 a prime number에 이어지는 동사 is와 등위접속사 and로 병렬연결 되어있으며 소수의 정의로 불변의 진리를 나 타내므로 현재시제 is가 적절하다.

May 23.
I have been thinking about the relationship
between prime numbers and the number of years
magicicadas live underground. So, I did some more
research, and this is what I found. It seems that
emerging in prime number intervals ⓐmaximizes
their
exposure
to
predators.
Their
predator
populations also have cycles, such as a cycle of
two, three, four, or six years. If magicicadas
followed a non-prime number cycle, for example, a
cycle of 12 years, magicicadas would ⓑevade
predators with a cycle of three years five times
every 60 years. However, (A)17년 주기를 가진 주기
매미는 주기가 3년인 포식자와 60년마다 한 번씩만
마주치게 된다. That is, by emerging every 17 years,
magicicadas
minimize
these
ⓒfatal
encounters
because 17 is a prime number. The way nature
works is amazing!
May 24.
After math class, I told Mr. Johnson about what I
had found studying magicicadas, and he was
pleasantly surprised. He smiled and told me I
should look for another of nature’s hidden secrets.
He said the hint was in flower petals. ⓓAnxious to
solve the mystery, I went to the school garden and
counted the number of petals.
I realized that most flowers have a specific number
of petals. These numbers follow a pattern: 1, 2, 3,
5, 8..., and so on, so each one equals the sum of
the previous two. This must be the secret Mr.
Johnson was talking about.
ⓔThrilled, I ran back to Mr. Johnson and told him
I had found the answer. He said he knew I would
figure it out, and he was proud of me. He told me
that this sequence is called the Fibonacci sequence,

May 24.
After math class, I told Mr. Johnson about what I
had found ⓐstudying magicicadas, and he was
pleasantly surprised. He smiled and told me I
should look for another of nature’s hidden secrets.
He said the hint was in flower petals. ⓑEagerly to
solve the mystery, I went to the school garden and
counted the number of petals.
I realized that most flowers have a specific number
of petals. These numbers follow a pattern: 1, 2, 3,
5, 8..., and so on, so each one equals the sum of
the previous two. This must be the secret ⓒthat
Mr. Johnson was talking about.
Excited, I ran back to Mr. Johnson and told him
ⓓwhat I had found the answer. He said he knew I
would figure it out, and he was proud of me. He
told me that this sequence is called the Fibonacci
sequence,
which
ⓔwas
named
after
the
mathematician who discovered it. The number of
petals in a Fibonacci sequence has to do with
maximizing the light absorption as plants grow.
Mr. Johnson went on to explain that not only
petals but also seeds form in a manner that
arranges them most efficiently without any gaps. He
showed me sunflowers and how their seeds in the
center bunch up in the middle and spiral out. He
explained that there are 21 clockwise spirals and 34
counterclockwise spirals. In bigger sunflowers, the
number of spirals increases to 34 and 55, and for
even bigger ⓕone, 55 and 89. I shouted, “That’s a
Fibonacci sequence, too!” He nodded and said that
this is called a Fibonacci spiral, and flowers can
produce more seeds that way than in a straight
line. I guess flowers can do math!
I must confess that I used ⓖto think mathematics
was just numbers and theories, but after finding the
secret numbers in nature, I’m excited to learn more
about math in real life.

다 양하며, Bloomington지역의 주기매미 는 13년(→ 17년) 동안 지하에 머문 후 지상으로 올라온다. 소수에 대한 깨달음 ㉢글쓴이는 13과 17이 소수라는 것 을 깨닫는다. 소수의 정의와 예시들 ㉣소수는 2, 3, 5, 7과 같이 1과 자 기 자신으로만 나눌 수 있는 1보다 큰 수이다. 자연 속 수학적 패턴 발견 ㉤글쓴이는 매미의 출현이 소수 간격 의 수학적 규칙을 따른다는 것을 알게 되었다. 4) ①: ⓐ maximizes(극대화하다) → minimizes(최소화하다), reduce (줄이다) *본문에는 minimizes가 쓰였음 ⓑ evade(피하다) → come across(우연히 마주치다), encounter(마주치다), meet(만나다) *본문에는 come across가 쓰였음 본문변형 선행사 predators(포 식자들)를 수식하는 관계사절의 관계대명사로 소유격 관계 대명사 whose를 쓰고, 바로 이어서 관계사절의 주어로 cycle을 쓴다. • 빈도를 나타내는 부사구는 ‘횟수+기간’으로 나타내므로 ‘60년마다 한 번씩만‘을 뜻하는 빈도를 나타내는 부사구는 only once every 60 years로 쓴다. 6) ④, ⑤ : 대부분의 꽃에 꽃잎 수는 무작위가 아니라 1, 2, 3, 5, 8... 같은 규칙의 피보나치 수열을 따른다고 했으므로 ④ ‘꽃잎 의 수는 대개 무작위로 보이며, 일정한 패턴이 없다.’는 일 치하지 않는 내용이다. 피보나치 수열의 꽃잎의 수는 빛의 흡수를 극대화하는 것 과 관련이 있다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘피보나치 수열은 식물이 빛 흡수를 제한하는 방식과 관련이 있다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 주기매미는 소수 간격으로 출현함으로써 포식자와 직 면할 가능성을 줄인다. ② 주기매미가 12년 주기로 산다면, 60년 안에 3년 주기의 포식자와 여러 번 마주치게 될 것이다. ③ Johnson 선생님은 글쓴이에게 힌트를 주고 그에게 자 연에 있는 또 다른 비밀을 찾아보라고 했다. 7) ③: 글쓴이는 5월 23일 일기에서 주기매미가 17년, 즉 소수 주기로 출현함으로써 포식자와 마주치는 위험을 줄일 수 있다고 수학적 관점(소수 주기)으로 설명하고 있으며, 5 월 24일 일기에서는 꽃잎 수에서 피보나치 수열 같은 수학적 규칙을 발견하고, 이것이 식물이 성장할 때 빛 공통영어1 천재(조수경) SL 예상문제 3회 - 주관식(서답형) 2. (→ 글쓴이가 찾아낼 줄 알았다며, 그가 자랑스럽다고 말했다.) ② 피보나치 수열은 꽃잎 수와 어떤 관련이 있는가? (→ 대부분의 꽃들은 피보나치 수열에 나오는 수만큼의 꽃 잎을 가지고 있다.) ③ 꽃은 씨앗 생산을 어떻게 늘릴 수 있는가? (→ 씨앗 들이 피보나치 수열의 수만큼 나선을 가짐으로써 더 많 은 씨앗을 생산할 수 있다.) ④ 글쓴이는 이전에 수학에 대해 어떤 생각을 가지고 있었는가? (→ 그저 숫자와 이론이라고만 생각했다.) 10) ①: 글쓴이는 꽃잎의 수와 해바라기 씨앗의 나선형의 수가 피보나치 수열의 수로 되어있다는 것을 발견하며, 자연 속에 숨겨진 수학적 규칙들을 알게 된다. 따라서 이 글 의 제목으로 ① ‘비밀 수학 코드가 자연 세계에 있다’가 적절하다. 오답 ② 꽃의 숨겨진 생활 주기를 발견하기 ③ 해바라기 씨앗 나선 무늬의 신비 ④ 빛 흡수를 통한 식물 성장 이해 ⑤ 자연의 방어 기제: 더 많은 씨앗 생산하기 11) underground, emerged, first, 17 요약문 글쓴이는 17년 동안 땅속에 사는 주기매미가 올해 Bloomington에 나타났다는 것을 알게 되었고 그러고 나서 그 또한 17살이기 때문에 그것들을 처음 들었다는 것을 깨 달았다. 12) followed a non-prime number cycle, would come across predators with a cycle of three years five times every : • 가정법 과거는 ‘If+S+과거형 동사 ~, 주어+조동사 과거 형+동사원형 …‘으로 쓰므로, If 절의 동사로 과거형 동사 followed를 쓰고, 주절에는 주어진 조동사 will의 과거형 would와 ’만나다‘라는 뜻의 표현 come across의 동사원 형 come을 쓴다. • ‘~를 가진’이라는 뜻을 지닌 전치사 with를 사용하여 predators를 수식하는 전치사구를 쓴다. 13) ②: 글쓴이는 소수와 주기매미가 땅속에 사는 해의 수 사이 의 관계에 대해 조사했고, 그 결과 이러한 소수 주기의 전략이 포식자와의 치명적인 마주침 횟수를 줄여준다는 것을 알게 되었다. 따라서 글의 요지로 ② ‘주기매미는 포식자를 피하기 위해 생존 전략으로서 소수 간격으로 나타난다.’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 주기매미가 전체 매미 종들 중에서 가장 강한 방어 기제를 갖고 있다. ③ 주기매미의 수가 줄어들면서 그들의 포식자 또한 줄 어들고, 이는 생태계를 위협한다. ④ 주기매미의 땅속에서 사는 기간이 짧아지고 있고, 이것이 포식자 개체 수 증가를 유발하고 있다. ⑤ 주기매미와 포식자 사이의 만남이 증가해오면서 주 기매미 개체수가 줄어들고 있는 중이다. 14) ②: 대부분의 매미 종들은 1년에 한 번씩 나타나지만, 더 긴 간격을 두고 나타나는 종들도 있다는 내용에 이어 그 예시로 Bloomington의 주기매미들은 17년마다 1번 씩 나타나고, 다른 지역의 주기매미들은 13년 또는 17 년 간격으로 나타난다고 설명하는 (B), 그리고 앞서 언 급한 13과 17이 소수라는 것을 깨닫고, 소수의 정의를 설명하는 (A), 마지막으로 소수의 예시를 언급하고, 자 연에 수학적 규칙이 있을 것이라 상상하지 못했다고 말하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 15) ②: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다. ⓔ have found → had found (과거형 동사 told의 직 접 목적어 자리로, 그에게 말했던(told) 과거보다 더 이 전에 답을 찾았던 것이므로 과거보다 더 앞섬을 나타 낼 때 쓰이는 과거완료가 되어야 한다. 따라서 have found를 had found로 고친다.) ⓕ how do their seeds in the center → how their seeds in the center (동사 showed의 두 번째 직접 목 적어 자리에서 뒤에 이어지는 동사구(bunch up ~ and spiral out)와 함께 의문사절을 이루어야 하므로, 간접 의문문의 어순을 따라야하며, 간접의문문은 ‘의문사+주 어+동사‘의 순서를 따른다. 따라서 how do their seeds in the center를 ’의문사+주어‘인 how their seeds로 고 친다.) ⓖ most → more (최상급과 함께 쓰이는 정관사 the가 없고, 뒤에 비교급과 함께 쓰이는 ‘~보다’라는 뜻의 접 속사 than이 있으므로 비교급인 more로 고쳐야 한다.) 오답 ⓐ 선행사 없이 불완전한 절(I had found)을 이끌어 전 치사 about의 목적어인 명사절을 이루는 관계대명사 what이 쓰인 것은 적절하다. ⓑ 콤마 뒤로 과거시제의 완전한 절(I went to ~ petals) 이 이어지고 있으므로 종속절을 이루는 부사절 접속사 As와, 주어 I, 1인칭 주어에 수일치하고 주절과 시제 일 치한 과거형 단수 be동사 was가 쓰인 것과 was의 보 어로 형용사 eager가 쓰인 것은 적절하다. 본문변형 Eager → As I was eager ⓒ 문장의 동사 자리로, 주어 each one은 단수명사구 이므로 단수 동사 equals가 쓰인 것은 적절하다. ⓓ 콤마 뒤로 과거시제의 완전한 절(I ran ~ answer)이 이어지고 있으므로 종속절을 이루는 부사절 접속사 As 와, 주어 I, 1인칭 주어에 수일치하고 주절과 시제 일치 한 과거형 단수 be동사 was가 쓰인 것은 적절하며, 주 어 I가 신남을 느낀 대상이므로 과거분사형 형용사 excited가 was의 보어로 쓰인 것도 적절하다. 본문변형 Excited → As I was excited 16) ⑤: 빈칸은 글쓴이가 꽃잎의 수를 세고 난 뒤에 깨달음이 들어가는 부분으로, 빈칸 뒤에서 이 꽃잎의 숫자들에서 각각의 숫자가 앞의 두 숫자의 합이 되는 규칙을 따른 다고 설명했다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ⑤ ‘대부분의 꽃들은 특정한 수의 꽃잎을 특징으로 한다’가 적절하다. 본문변형 원래 ‘most flowers have a specific number of petals’였음 오답 ① 모든 꽃은 같은 수의 꽃잎이 있다 ② 많은 꽃들은 무작위 수의 꽃잎이 있다 ③ 꽃잎의 수는 시간이 지남에 따라 달라진다 ④ 꽃잎의 수를 결정하는 것은 주변 환경이다 17) ③: 주어진 문장은 ‘더 큰 해바라기에서는 나선형의 숫자가 34개와 55개로 증가하며, 훨씬 더 큰 것에서는 55개와 89개로 증가한다.’라는 뜻으로, 더 작은 크기의 해바라 기의 나선형 수에 대한 설명으로 21개의 시계 방향 나 선형과 34개의 반시계 방향 나선형이 언급된 문장 뒤 와, 글쓴이가 지금까지 언급된 나선형의 수인 21, 34, 55, 89를 듣고서 피보나치 수열임을 깨닫는 문장 앞인 (C)가 적절하다. 18) where each number is the sum of the previous two 질문 글쓴이는 꽃잎 수를 세어 봄으로써 무엇을 발견했는가? → 글쓴이는 꽃잎의 수가 각각의 수가 앞의 두 숫자의 합 이 되는 수열을 따른다는 것을 발견했다. 19) ②: (A) 앞 절에서 대부분의 종들은 1년마다 한 번씩 나타 난다고 했고, 다음 문장에서 17년 또는 13년마다 한 번 씩 나타나는 주기매미를 언급하고 있으므로 longer(더 긴)가 알맞다. shorter 더 짧은 (B) 주기매미가 12년의 비소수 주기를 따를 때보다 소 수 주기를 따를 때 60년 동안 포식자를 마주칠 확률이 줄어든다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 포식자와 만남 을 줄인다는 내용이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 limits(제한 하다)가 알맞다. heightens 높이다 본문변형 minimizes → limits (C) 앞에서 17년의 소수 주기를 지닌 주기매미가 12년 의 비소수 주기를 가진 주기매미보다 같은 기간인 60 년 동안 3년 주기 포식자를 만나는 횟수가 다섯 번에 서 한번으로 적어진다는 예시를 들었고 이를 That is (즉)로 연결하여 다시 재진술하고 있으므로 포식자와의 만남을 가리키는 말에 deadly(치명적인)이 알맞다. harmless 무해한

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you
have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were
named "jeans" ⓐbecause they were made of jean, a
sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a
modification of Gênes, the French name of the
Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th
centuries, Genoa ⓑhas been a major center for
trade. Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their
goods throughout Europe, particularly in England
and France. (A)Genoa를 유명하게 만든 물품들 중 하
나는 튼튼한 면포로, 질긴 작업복을 만들기에 이상적
으로 적합했습니다. The cloth was most likely
ⓒcolored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe
at that time, so the cloth ⓓwas called "bleu de
Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the pants
ⓔwere made with "bleu de Gênes" became known
as blue jeans in English.

name origins as those introduced here?

(A)
(B)

solution: (A) 뒤에 오페라, 저녁 파티, 시상식과 같은 격식을 갖춘 행사의 구체적 인 예시가 이어지고 있고, 글의 후반에서 이제 남자들의 격식을 갖춘 옷은 턱시도라고 했으므로, 이와 같이 공식적인 복장 규정이 요구될 때 턱시도를 입는다는 흐름으로 required(요구되는, 필요한)가 알맞다. (B) 같은 스타일을 입기 시작했다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, Tuxedo Park에 한 남자가 꼬리가 없는 짧은 검정색 재킷을 입 고 나타났다는 내용에 이어 그곳에 있던 남자 손님들이 그 새로 운 재킷에 매료되었다는 흐름으로 fascinated(매료된)가 알맞다. (C) 앞에 언급된 this style of jacket(이 스타일의 재킷)은 꼬리가 짧 은 재킷 스타일을 말하며, 점점 더 많은 남자들이 더 짧은 스타일 을 입으면서 긴 버전을 대체하게 되었고 이제 남자들의 격식을 갖 춘 옷은 턱시도라는 설명이 뒤에 이어지고 있으며, 원래는 그렇게 격식을 갖춘 것으로 여겨지지 않았지만 이제는 가장 격식을 갖춘 남성복이라는 것이 역설적이라는 내용으로 마무리하고 있으므로, 처음에 이 스타일의 재킷이 긴 꼬리가 달린 재킷보다 덜 격식 있는 것으로 여겨졌다는 흐름으로 less 뒤에 formal(격식 있는)이 알맞다. 천재(조수경) 2과

clothes are suitable for them by identifying their

worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact that they

flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The sound became the
name of the shoes, flip-flops.

(B)

When you go deep into the sea, you can see a
variety of marine animals including corals. Over the
course of many years, corals build up to form large
structures called coral reefs. Brightly colored coral
reefs provide a beautiful underwater landscape.
However, this is not the only reason they are
valuable.
Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect
both marine life and people living near the sea.
Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of
marine life, such as fish and underwater plants.
Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs,
they are often called “the rainforests of the sea.”
Nearly one quarter of all known marine species
depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide
themselves from predators, find food, reproduce,
and raise their young in coral reefs.

Coral reefs offer shelter to plenty of fish andmarine plants.

Nearly a quarter of all known marine speciesowe their survival to coral reefs.

body:
As far as humans are concerned, over half a
billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and
survival. When large waves generated by storms
rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural
barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they
hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the
land on the shore from washing away and thus
protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a
source of medicine, and many organisms found in
coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer.
This is why they are sometimes referred to as the
“medicine chests of the sea.”

are various causes, like destructive fishing techniques,
overpopulation of corals’ natural enemies, and
careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the
rise in water temperature due to global warming.

solution: ⓐ 증가하는 산호초 손실은 전체 해양 생태계의 파괴로 이어 질 수도 있다는 흐름이므로 destruction(파괴)이 알맞다. ⓑ 세계의 많은 산호초가 멸종 위기에 처해 있다는 흐름이므 로, 세계에서 가장 큰 호주의 그레이트 배리어 리프의 거의 절 반이 사라졌다는 흐름이 되는 disappeared(사라진)가 알맞다. ⓒ This로 지칭되는 플라스틱 제품들이 바다에 버려지는 행위는 산호초와 그곳에 서식하는 생물들에게 피해를 주는 바이러스 와 질병을 퍼뜨린다는 흐름이므로 spreads(퍼뜨린다)가 알맞다.

These underwater treasures are (A)__________________
_________________________________. The more coral reefs
become damaged, the more creatures relying on
them will lose their homes. Thus, the increasing loss
of coral reefs might lead to the ⓐ[destruction /
restoration] of the entire marine ecosystem. The
U.N. reported that many of the world’s coral reefs
are currently endangered. In fact, nearly half of
Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, the world’s largest,
has ⓑ[appeared / disappeared]. If swift action is
not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs
will be destroyed by 2050.
What causes coral reefs to die? There are various
causes,
like
destructive
fishing
techniques,
overpopulation of corals’ natural enemies, and
careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the
rise in water temperature due to global warming.
The ideal temperature range for corals to live is
20°C to 28°C. When the water temperature rises
above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and eventually
die. Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic
products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have
been dumped into the sea. This ⓒ[spreads /
prevents] viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs
and their inhabitants.

What causes coral reefs to die? There are various
causes,
like
destructive
fishing
techniques,
overpopulation of corals’ natural enemies, and
careless tourism.
(A) When the water temperature rises above 30°C,
coral reefs turn white and eventually die.
Another serious cause is plastic waste.
(B) However, the leading cause is the rise in water
temperature due to global warming. The ideal
temperature range for corals to live is 20°C to
28°C.
(C) Plastic products, such as bottles and fishing
lines, have been dumped into the sea. This
spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral
reefs and their inhabitants.
solution: 산호초를 죽게 만드는 다양한 원인들이 있다고 설명한 뒤, However(하지만)에 이어 주요 원인으로 지구 온난화로 인한 수온 상승을 거론하는 (B), 수온이 30°C 이상 올라가면 산호초 가 죽는다고 설명하고 또 다른(Another) 심각한 원인으로 플 라스틱 쓰레기를 거론하는 (A), 플라스틱 제품들을 바다에 버 리는 행위가 바이러스와 질병을 퍼뜨려서 산호초와 그곳에 서 식하는 생물들에게 피해를 준다고 설명하는 (C)의 흐름이 자 연스럽다. 천재(조수경) 4과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 공통영어1 천재(조수경) 4과 예상문제 1회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. 주관식 2. 주관식 3. ② 4. ③ 5. 주관식 6. 주관식 7. ⑤ 8. ④ 9. 주관식 10. 주관식 11. ① 12. ② 13. 주관식 14. ④ 15. ⑤ 16. ② 17. ③ 18. ⑤ 19. ① 20. ② 정답 및 해설 ┃1회┃ 1) You should turn off the lights(또는 turn the lights off) when you leave the room. : • 엄마가 지민에게 전기를 낭비하고 있다고 했으며, 빈칸 뒤에서는 너는 그런 방식으로(that way) 에너지를 절약할 수 있다고 말하므로, 방을 떠날 때 불을 꺼야 한다는 흐름 이 적절하다. • 조동사 should(~해야 한다)와 turn off(끄다)를 사용한다. • ‘타동사+부사’로 이루어진 구동사 turn ~ off(~을 끄다) 의 목적어가 the lights처럼 짧은 명사(구)인 경우 부사 앞 과 뒤 둘 다 가능하다. 2) It seems that global warming is very serious. : • 지구 온난화에 대한 뉴스를 봤냐는 소녀의 질문에 그렇 다고 답한 뒤에 이어지므로, 지구 온난화가 아주 심각한 것 같다는 흐름이 적절하다. • ‘it seems that+주어+동사 ~’(~한 것 같다) 표현을 사용한다. 3) ②: 산호초는 해양 생물과 바다 근처에 사는 사람들 둘 다를 보호한다고 했으므로, ② ‘산호초는 해양 생물을 보호하 는 반면, 바다 근처에 사는 사람들에게는 해를 끼친다.’ 는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ① 산호가 산호초를 형성하는 데는 수년이 걸린다. ③ 산호초는 많은 물고기와 해양 식물에게 은신처를 제 공한다. ④ 다양한 동식물이 산호초에서 발견되기 때문에 산호초 는 ‘바다의 열대 우림’이라는 별명을 얻었다. ⑤ 모든 알려진 해양 종의 거의 4분의 1이 생존하고 있 는 것은 산호초 덕분이다. 4) ③: 산호초는 해안의 땅이 씻겨 나가는 것을 막는다고 했으 므로, ③ ‘산호초 때문에 해안의 땅이 사라진다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ① 5억 명이 넘는 사람들이 안전과 생존을 위해 산호초 에 의존한다. ② 산호초는 폭풍으로 인해 발생되는 큰 파도에 대한 자 연적인 장벽의 역할을 한다. ④ 산호초에 있는 많은 유기체가 암과 같은 질병을 치료 하는 데 도움이 된다. ⑤ 산호초는 ‘바다의 구급상자’라고 불린다. 5) coral reefs, protecting, diseases 제시문 해안 지역 사회를 보호하고 질병을 치료하는 데 있 어 산호초의 필수적인 역할 6) The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes. : • ‘the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 …(~할수록 …하다)’ 구문을 사용한다. • coral reefs가 ‘손상되는’ 대상이므로 동사 become의 보 어 자리에는 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 damaged를 쓴다. • ‘rely on ~(~에 의존하다)’을 사용하되 the more creatures가 그것들에게 ‘의존하는’ 주체이므로 rely를 능동 을 나타내는 현재분사 relying으로 변형하여 the more creatures를 뒤에서 수식하도록 한다. 7) ⑤: (A) cause는 to부정사를 목적격보어로 취하므로 to die가 알맞다. (B) 범위가 정해지지 않은 집합에서 ‘또 다른 한 ~’은 another로 표현하므로 Another가 알맞다. 참고로, the other는 ‘나머지 다른 ~(들)’을 지칭할 때 사용한다. (C) 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 앞 절 내용으로 이는 ‘피 해를 주는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어(coral reefs and their inhabitants)가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 damaging이 알맞다. 8) ④: 산호초는 다수의 해양 생물에게 서식지를 제공하고 해양 종의 거의 4분의 1이 의존하여 살 만큼 해양 생물에게 중요하다는 내용이므로, ④ ‘산호초가 해양 생물에게 중 요한 이유’가 제목으로 알맞다. 오답 ① 산호초: 바다의 신비 ② 해양 생태계의 구성 요소 ③ 산호초를 탐험해야 하는 이유 ⑤ 산호초의 구조와 구성 9) using, clean, save 요약문 산호초를 보호하기 위한 간단하면서도 효과적인 방 법은 미세 플라스틱 조각과 해로운 자외선 차단제 화학 물 질을 가진 제품을 사용하지 않는 것, 쓰레기를 줄여 바다를 깨끗하게 유지하는 것, 그리고 산호초에 대한 위협과 그것을 구하는 방법에 대한 인식을 높이는 것을 포함한다. 10) (1) ⓐ: restore → restoring (2) ⓓ: proposing → proposed (3) ⓕ: how → that 또는 which 공통영어1 천재(조수경) 4과 예상문제 1회 - 주관식(서답형) 1. You should turn off the lights(또는 turn the lights off) when you leave the room. 2. It seems that global warming is very serious. 5. coral reefs, protecting, diseases 6. The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes. 9. using, clean, save 10. (1) ⓐ: restore → restoring (2) ⓓ: proposing → proposed (3) ⓕ: how → that 또는 which 13. A lot of people may be unfamiliar with the fact that there are forests in the sea : ⓐ 전치사 by 뒤에 목적어를 이루는 동명사 monitoring, protecting과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되었으므로 restore를 동명사 restoring으로 고친다. ⓓ 주어(3D printing systems)가 ‘제안된’ 대상이므로 수동 태를 이루도록 proposing을 과거분사 proposed로 고친다. ⓕ 선행사 a way 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌 므로 관계부사 how를 사물의 주격 관계대명사 that이나 which로 고친다. *본문에서는 that이 쓰였음 11) ①: 어법상 어색한 것은 2개(ⓑ, ⓒ)이다. ⓑ Because → Because of (뒤에 명사구(the diversity ~ coral reefs)가 이어지므로 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사가 아닌 (구)전치사가 오도록 구전치사 Because of로 고친다.) ⓒ knowing → known (수식받는 대상인 marine species가 ‘알려진’ 대상으로 know와 marine species가 수동의 관계를 이루므로 과거분사 known으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓓ ‘as far as ~ be concerned’는 ‘~에 관한 한’이라는 뜻의 관용구이다. ⓕ 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지는 why, when, where 등의 관계부사는 선행사가 the reason, the day, the place처 럼 일반적일 때 선행사 없이 쓰일 수 있으며 명사절을 이끌어 be동사의 보어를 이룰 수 있으므로, 선행사 없 이 완전한 절(they ~ the sea”) 앞에 쓰인 이유의 관계 부사 why는 알맞다. 12) ②: (B) allies(동종의 것들) → predators(포식자들), enemies (적들) *본문에서는 predators가 쓰였음 13) A lot of people may be unfamiliar with the fact that there are forests in the sea : • 조동사 may(~할 수도 있다)와 ‘be unfamiliar with ~(~ 에 친숙하지 않다, ~을 잘 알지 못하다)’ 표현을 활용한다. • ‘추상 명사(구)+동격의 that절’ 구조를 활용해 ‘the fact+that절(~라는 사실)’을 쓴다. • ‘there(유도부사)+be동사+명사(구) 주어(~(들)이 있다)’ 표현을 활용한다. 14) ④: 바다 식목일에는 많은 단체들이 해양 식물을 심거나 더 작은 규모로는 사람들이 해안을 따라 쓰레기를 줍는다 는 내용에 이어지므로, 작은 실천이 해양 생태계 보호 에 큰 기여를 할 수 있다는 뜻이 되는 ④ ‘우리가 하는 작은 환경 활동이 바다를 보존하는 데 큰 물결을 일으 킬 수 있다’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 해양 보존은 더 큰 경제적 이익을 가져올 수 있다 ② 한국 정부는 바다를 보호하기 위해 노력해 왔다 ③ 우리는 해양 종들과 그들이 바다 숲에서 하는 역할 에 대해 배워야 한다 ⑤ 전국적인 캠페인이 없으면 환경 보호에 대한 대중의 인식은 여전히 낮다 15) ⑤: 세계의 많은 산호초가 현재 멸종 위기에 처해 있다는 유엔의 보고와 빠른 조치가 없으면 2050년쯤에는 대부 분의 산호초가 파괴될 것이라는 과학자들의 추정이 이 어지므로, ‘이 수중 보물들’로 지칭된 산호초가 멸종 위 기에 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ⑤ ‘멸종의 위협을 받는’이 적절하다. 오답 ① 생물다양성이 풍부한 ② 끊임없이 진화하고 있는 ③ 연구 대상들 ④ 인기 있는 관광지 16) ②: ⓐ 증가하는 산호초 손실은 전체 해양 생태계의 파괴로 이 어질 수도 있다는 흐름이므로 destruction(파괴)이 알맞다. restoration 복원, 복구 ⓑ 세계의 많은 산호초가 멸종 위기에 처해 있다는 흐 름이므로, 세계에서 가장 큰 호주의 그레이트 배리어 리프의 거의 절반이 사라졌다는 흐름이 되는 disappeared(사라진)가 알맞다. appeared 나타난 ⓒ This로 지칭되는 플라스틱 제품들이 바다에 버려지 는 행위는 산호초와 그곳에 서식하는 생물들에게 피해 를 주는 바이러스와 질병을 퍼뜨린다는 흐름이므로 spreads(퍼뜨린다)가 알맞다. prevents 예방한다 17) ③: 주어진 문장은 ‘결과적으로, 산호초는 해안의 땅이 씻겨 나가는 것을 막아서 바다 근처의 마을들을 보호한다.’라 는 뜻으로, 산호초가 자연적인 장벽의 역할을 해서 파 도의 힘이 줄어드는 원인이 됨을 설명한 뒤인 (C)에 들 어가야 한다. 18) ⑤: 산호초를 보호하는 것을 돕기 위해 우리가 취할 수 있 는 조치들로 바다를 오염시키는 미세 플라스틱 조각이 들어 있는 미용 제품과 산호를 손상시키는 특정 화학 물질로 만들어진 자외선 차단제를 사용하지 않는 것, 해변 청소를 돕는 자원봉사를 하는 것, 쓰레기를 재활 용하고 줄이는 것, 사람들에게 산호초에 대한 위협과 산호초를 구하기 위해 취해야 할 행동을 알리는 것을 언급했으므로, 산호초를 보호하는 방법으로 본문에서 제안되지 않은 것은 ⑤ ‘산호 보호 기술에 관한 정보를 다른 사람들과 공유하기’이다. 질문 산호초를 보호하는 방법으로 본문에서 제안되지 않은 것은? 오답 ① 해변 청소 활동에 자원봉사하기 ② 미세 플라스틱 조각이 들어 있는 화장품을 피하기 ③ 산호를 손상하는 화학 성분의 자외선 차단제를 사 용하지 않기 ④ 산호초가 직면한 위협에 대한 인식을 높이기 19) ①: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다. ⓒ that lives → that live (주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌며 선행사가 the contributors 뒤의 to(~에 대한)는 전치사이므로 동 명사 creating이 이끄는 동명사구가 목적어로 쓰였으며, 뒤에 목적어 a healthy marine ecosystem(건강한 해양 생태계)이 있으므로 능동형 동명사 creating은 알맞다. 20) ②: 산호초를 죽게 만드는 다양한 원인들이 있다고 설명한 뒤, However(하지만)에 이어 On beaches and at pools, everyone seems to wear
simple shoes with a band across the top of the
foot and between the big toe and second toe.
Amazingly, they are one of the (A)[latest / oldest]
shoes in history. Ancient Egyptian paintings show
they were worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact
that they have such a long history, they have
(B)[similar / different] names all around the world.
The Japanese call them zories. New Zealanders call
them jandals, which is a shortened form of "Japanese
sandals." However, in the USA, these shoes are
called "flip-flops." Just walk around in a pair of them,
and you can easily guess why they got this name.
The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you
walk, making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The (C)[sound
/ material] became the name of the shoes, flip-flops.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 고대 이집트인들이 기원전 4000년경에 착용했으며, 그렇게 오랜 역사를 가지고 있다는 내용이 이어지므로 역사상 가장 오래된 신발 중 하나라는 흐름으로 oldest(가장 오래된)가 알맞다. (B) 일본인들은 zories라고 부르며, 뉴질랜드인들은 jandals라고 부르고, 미국에서는 flip-flops라고 불린다는 내용이 이어지므로, 세계적으로 다양한 이름을 가지고 있다는 흐름으로 different(각 기 다른, 다양한)가 알맞다. (C) 미국에서는 ‘플립플랍(flip-flops)’이라고 부른다고 했으며, 그 이유 에 대한 설명으로 이 신발을 신고 걸을 때 고무 밑창이 발바닥에 부딪혀 플립플랍, 플립플랍 소리를 낸다는 내용에 이어지므로, 그 소리가 신발의 이름이 되었다는 흐름으로 sound(소리)가 알맞다.

body:
Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a
single item that covers your whole body, even your
arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and
to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit
began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later,
designers transformed this functional design into
luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion
shows around the world. Like the jumpsuit, there
are other fashion items with interesting stories
about how they got their names.
Sneak Up in Sneakers
You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for
everyday activities or sports. They are a type of
athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for
physical activities and sports. So, why are they
called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived
from the term "to sneak up." Due to the fact that
sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they
make little noise when people walk. This allows
people who are wearing (A)them to sneak up on
others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole
of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of
noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing
(B)them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly
sneak up on your friends and surprise (C)them.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is
required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or
awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from
Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in
New York. In the late 19th century, men usually
wore jackets with long tails that reached their knees
on formal occasions. One evening, a man showed
up with a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo
Park. The male guests who stayed there were
fascinated by the new jacket and started to wear
the same style. Later, more people asked their
tailors to make them a jacket "like the one worn in
Tuxedo Park." At first, this style of jacket was
considered less formal than one with long tails. As
more and more men wore the shorter style, ________
____________________________________________. Now men's
formal wear is the tuxedo. Isn't it ironic that the
tuxedo was not originally considered very formal,
but now it is the most formal clothing men wear?
choices: it became an exclusive fashion choice for thewealthy elite
tailors began combining elements of both longand short styles
it replaced the long-tailed jacket as men’s outfitfor formal occasions
people completely stopped wearing the new- stylejackets at formal events
it remained primarily associated with events atTuxedo Park and similar communities
solution: Tuxedo Park에 한 남자가 꼬리가 없는 짧은 검정색 재킷을 입 고 나타났을 때 그곳에 있던 남자 손님들이 그 새로운 재킷에 매료되어 점점 더 많은 사람들이 자신들의 재단사에게 그와 같은 재킷을 만들어 달라고 요청했다는 내용이 앞에 있었으며, 이후 글의 마지막에서는 턱시도가 이제 남성이 입는 가장 격 식을 갖춘 옷이라고 마무리하고 있으므로, 점점 더 많은 남자 들이 더 짧은 스타일을 입으면서 긴 스타일의 재킷 대신 짧은 스타일의 재킷이 남성들의 격식을 갖춘 옷이 되었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❸ ‘그것은 공식적인 행사를 위 한 남성복으로서 꼬리가 긴 재킷을 대체했다’가 알맞다.

The colors you wear are important in creating an
attractive appearance. People can learn which color
clothes are suitable for them by identifying their
personal color, a color that perfectly fits their
individual skin tone. To figure out the most
desirable color scheme for your clothing, you must
first determine if the underlying color in your skin
tone is warm or cool. Try holding an object with a
certain color up to your face in a mirror and
decide which color makes you look best. If your
face looks best with colors of pink, purple, or blue,
you have a cool skin tone. If your face looks best
with warm colors such as yellow, orange, or red,
your skin tone is warm. Generally you will look best
with clothes of similar tones to your personal color.
If a color causes your face to look dull, avoid that
color in your collection of clothes.

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you
have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were
named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a
sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a
modification of Gênes, the French name of the
Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th
centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade.
Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods
throughout Europe, particularly in England and
France. One of the items that made Genoa famous
was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making
tough work clothes. The cloth was most likely
colored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe
at that time, so the cloth was called "bleu de
Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the pants
made with "bleu de Gênes" became known as blue
jeans in English.
choices: What kind of fabric were jeans made from?
Where did the sailing merchants from Genoatrade their goods?
What was the item that made Genoa famous?
Why was French widely spoken throughout Europein the 17th and 18th centuries?
How did blue jeans get their name in English?
solution: 프랑스어가 당시 유럽에서 널리 사용되었기 때문에 Genoa를 유명하게 만들었던 무역품 중 하나인 튼튼한 면포가 프랑스어 로 "bleu de Gênes"로 불렸다고 했으나, 당시에 프랑스어가 널리 사용된 이유는 언급되어 있지 않으므로 ❹ ‘왜 프랑스어 는 17세기와 18세기에 유럽 전역에서 널리 사용되었는가?’는 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문이다.

Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a
single item that covers your whole body, even your
arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and
to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit
began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later,
designers transformed this functional design into
luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion
shows around the world. Like the jumpsuit, there
are other fashion items with interesting stories
about how they got their names.
Sneak Up in Sneakers
You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for
everyday activities or sports. They are a type of
athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for
physical activities and sports. So, why are they
called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived
from the term "to sneak up." Due to the fact that
sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they
make little noise when people walk. This allows
people who are wearing (A)them to sneak up on
others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole
of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of
noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing
(B)them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly
sneak up on your friends and surprise (C)them.

People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is
required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or
awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from
Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in
New York. In the late 19th century, men usually
wore jackets with long tails that reached their knees
on formal occasions. One evening, a man showed
up with a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo
Park. The male guests who stayed there were
fascinated by the new jacket and started to wear
the same style. Later, more people asked their
tailors to make them a jacket "like the one worn in
Tuxedo Park." At first, this style of jacket was
considered less formal than one with long tails. As
more and more men wore the shorter style, it
eventually replaced the longer version. Now men's
formal wear is the tuxedo. Isn't it ironic that the
tuxedo was not originally considered very formal,
but now it is the most formal clothing men wear?

Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect
both marine life and people living near the sea.
Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of
marine life, such as fish and underwater plants.
Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs,
they are often called “the rainforests of the sea.”
Nearly one quarter of all known marine species
depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide
themselves from predators, find food, reproduce,
and raise their young in coral reefs.
As far as humans are concerned, over half a
billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and
survival. When large waves generated by storms
rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural
barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they
hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the
land on the shore from washing away and thus
protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a
source of medicine, and many organisms found in
coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer.
This is why they are sometimes referred to as the
“medicine chests of the sea.”

People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is
required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or
awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from
Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in
New York. In the late 19th century, men usually
wore jackets with long tails ⓐthat reached their
knees on formal occasions. One evening, a man
showed up with a short black jacket without tails in
Tuxedo Park. The male guests who stayed there
were ⓑfascinating by the new jacket and started to
wear the same style. (A)나중에, 더 많은 사람들이 그
들의 재단사들에게 “Tuxedo Park에서 착용된 것과 같
은” 재킷을 그들에게 만들어 달라고 요청했습니다. At
first, this style of jacket was considered less formal
than ⓒone with long tails. As more and more men
ⓓwore the shorter style, it eventually replaced the
longer version. Now men's formal wear is the
tuxedo. Isn't it ironic that the tuxedo was not
originally considered very formal, but now it is the
most formal clothing ⓔmen wear?

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you
have at least one pair of blue jeans. They
(A)[named / were named] "jeans" because they were
made of jean, a sort of tough cotton cloth. The
word jean is a modification of Gênes, the French
name of the Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and
18th centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade.
Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods
throughout Europe, particularly in England and France.
One of the items that made Genoa famous was a
strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to (B)[make /
making] tough work clothes. The cloth was most
likely colored blue. French was widely spoken in
Europe at that time, so the cloth was called "bleu
de Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the
pants made with "bleu de Gênes" (C)[became /
becoming] known as blue jeans in English.
(A)
(B)

Sneak Up in Sneakers
You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for
everyday activities or sports. They are a type of
athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for
physical activities and sports. So, why are they
called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived
from the term "to sneak up." Due to the fact that
sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they
make little noise when people walk. This allows
people who are wearing them to sneak up on
others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole
of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of
noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing
them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly
sneak up on your friends and surprise them.

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you
have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were
named "jeans" ⓐ______________ they were made of
jean, a sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is
a modification of Gênes, the French name of the
Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th
centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade.
Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods
throughout Europe, particularly in England and
France. One of the items that made Genoa famous
was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making
tough work clothes. The cloth was most likely
colored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe
at that time, ⓑ______________ the cloth was called
"bleu de Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how
the pants made with "bleu de Gênes" became
known as blue jeans in English.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
solution: ⓐ 우리 대부분이 가지고 있는 청바지가 ‘jeans’라고 이름 지어 졌다는 내용 뒤에 그것이 질긴 면포의 일종인 jean으로 만들어 졌다는 이유를 연결하고 있으므로, 이유의 접속사 as(~하므로) 또는 because(~하기 때문에)가 알맞다. ⓑ 당시 유럽에서 프랑스어가 널리 사용되었다는 내용 뒤에 그 결과로 그 천이 ‘bleu de Gênes’(Genoa의 파란 색)라고 불 렸다는 내용을 연결하므로 so(그래서)가 알맞다.

forests, too. Sea forests are formed by marine
plants, and numerous marine animals live there with

That
is,
sea
forests
are
habitats
for
underwater creatures and the leading contributors

live
on

the Korean

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

As far as humans are concerned, over half a
billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and
survival. ⓐWhen large waves generating by storms
rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural
barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they
hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they ⓑprevent the
land on the shore from washing away and thus
protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a
source of medicine, and many organisms found in
coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer.
ⓒThis is why they are sometimes referred to as the
“medicine chests of the sea.”
These underwater treasures are under threat of
destruction. The more coral reefs become damaged,
ⓓmore creatures relying on them will lose their
homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs
might lead to the destruction of the entire marine
ecosystem. The U.N. reported ⓔthat many of the
world’s coral reefs are currently endangered. In fact,
nearly half of Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, the
world’s largest, ⓕhas been disappeared. If swift
action is not taken, scientists estimate that most
coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.
solution: ⓐ generating → generated (접속사 When 뒤에 완전한 절(large waves ~ toward shore)이 온 것은 알맞으나, 큰 파도가 폭풍에 의해 ‘발생되는’ 대상으로 동사 generate가 수식받는 large waves와 수동의 관계를 이루 므로 과거분사 generated로 고친다.) ⓓ more → the more (more creatures가 그것들(산호초)에 ‘의존하는’ 주체이므로 현 재분사 relying이 이끄는 분사구가 more creatures를 수식한 것은 알맞으나, ‘~하면 할수록 …하다’는 ‘the+비교급 ~, the+ 비교급 …’으로 표현하므로 the more로 고친다.) ⓕ has been disappeared → has disappeared (주어부 half of Australia's Great Barrier Reef의 핵심 단어 half는 부분을 나타내는 명사로, 전치사 of 뒤에 이어진 단수명 사구 Australia's Great Barrier Reef의 부분도 단수이므로 단수 조동사 has를 쓴 것은 알맞으나, 자동사 disappear는 수동태가 될 수 없으며 과거의 행위가 현재까지 영향을 미치는 일을 나 타내야 하므로 현재완료 능동태 has disappeared로 고친다. 명 사구 Australia's Great Barrier Reef와 동격을 이루는 표현인 the world's largest가 이중 쉼표에 의해 삽입되어 있다.)
